`on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `sys.path` 不同。`get_config` 被 185 个文件使用。 **(2) `common/utils.py`（2,954 行）假定 `~/.jiuwenswarm` 工作区布局**：解析顺序 `JIUWENSWARM_DATA_DIR` → `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` → `~/.jiuwenswarm`，并期望其下有 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `chromadb`、`faiss-cpu`、`playwright`、`tree-sitter`、`sqlite-vec`、`pgvector`、`opentelemetry-*`，以及对本项目完全无用的 `python-telegram-bot` / `discord.py` / `slack-bolt` / `dingtalk-stream` / `wecom-aibot-sdk`。 ### 6.2 C 型按块实测 | 块 | 依赖 `common.config` | 依赖 `common.utils` | `sys.path` 副作用 | **C 型等级** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **Skill Hub**（`marketplace/hub_client` + 3 个兄弟文件） | **0** | **0** | **无** | **无** | | **Skill 文件/归档原语**（`skill_files` `archive_store`） | 0 | 0 | 无 | **无** | | **jiuwenbox** | 0 | 0 | 无（本机 HTTP 服务） | **无** | | cron store | 0 | 1（一个路径函数） | 无 | **低** | | **Skill 包管理**（`skill_manager.py` 8,841 行） | **4** | 1 | **有** | **高** | | 会话存储 / 项目 Git | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高**（且与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 双主） | | 产品 rails / tools | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高** | 由此修订接入策略： - **Skill Hub**：四个文件干净到可以直接 import，也可以照抄（Apache-2.0）。零 C 型侵入。 - **jiuwenbox**：**它已经是独立组件**——自带 `pyproject.toml`（`name = "jiuwenbox"`），依赖只有 pydantic/pyyaml/httpx/fastapi/uvicorn/python-multipart/mcp，**不依赖 `workswarm`**，Python 代码对 `jiuwenswarm` 零引用；JiuwenSwarm 自己也是通过 HTTP 调它。我们可以 `pip install "jiuwenbox @ git+#subdirectory=jiuwenbox"`，零侵入。 - **cron**：只要一个路径函数。建议照抄 cron 表达式与 store 语义到 `adapters/native/`，不为一个函数引入 `common.utils`。 - **Skill 包管理**：8,841 行会带来全套 C 型侵入。三个选择：① 在 `sd-agent` 独立进程里接受它；② 只取 `skill_files` + `archive_store` 两个干净原语，打包逻辑自己写；③ 不接。 - **会话存储**：明确不接，避免与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 形成双主；会话回溯用 L0 的 `core/session/vcs` 底座自己做产品化。 **新增设计约束**：`adapters/swarm/` 每个适配器要在文件头声明它拖进来的 C 型侵入，由 `check_layers.py` 校验声明与实际 import 一致；未声明的 import 直接失败。 ### 6.3 A 型：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 源码的场景，已缩到 2 条 本方案下**不再适用**的四条：新增 `ReqMethod`（我们不跑 AgentServer）、改 `agent_adapter`（我们自己装配）、换协作调度内核（走 agent-core 的 seam）、复用 JiuwenSwarm 前端组件（前端用我们自己的）。 仍然适用的： | # | 场景 | 触发条件 | 处置 | |---|---|---|---| | **A1** | jiuwenbox 增加 macOS 隔离后端 | 要保住 macOS 源码模式**同时**采用 jiuwenbox（jiuwenbox 目前 Linux-only；我们的 `seatbelt.ts` 在 47 个文件被引用） | 上游 PR；或不采用 jiuwenbox，继续用 `services/runner` | | **A2** | `skill_manager` 解耦工作区与全局 config | 要接 Skill 包管理，且不接受 6.1 的 C 型侵入 | 上游 PR（改为构造参数注入）；短期用 6.2 的选择② | 另有 A3（`common/config.py` 去掉导入期 `sys.path` 变更）只在「后端完全合并为单一 Python 进程」的形态下出现；本方案的 Node + sidecar 形态天然规避。 ### 6.4 B 型：建议向上游提出的扩展点 | # | 对象 | 诉求 | 不给的代价 | |---|---|---|---| | B1 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider` 与 `ContextEngine.register_processor` 的**覆盖生效时机窗口** | 改基础算法只能依赖未文档化的时机 | | B2 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_window_mutator` 在处理器链中的**执行点** | 窗口权威降级为尽力而为 | | B3 | JiuwenSwarm | 给出**可外部复用模块清单**并脱离 beta | `adapters/swarm/` 全部建立在内部模块上 | | B4 | JiuwenSwarm | **Skill Hub HTTP API 版本化**（现有 `hub_asset_port.py` 是 Python 端口稳定声明，HTTP 层无版本） | 被动跟随；最坏退回本地库 | | B5 | JiuwenSwarm | `skill_manager` 路径/config **改为注入式** | 见 A2 | | B6 | JiuwenSwarm | `common/config.py` 提供**无副作用导入模式** | 单进程形态下有静默 shadow 风险 | | B7 | JiuwenSwarm | jiuwenbox 发布到 PyPI | 便利性诉求，可用 git 子目录安装替代 | **B1、B2 最该优先推动**——「改基础算法」的能力完全取决于它们。 ### 6.5 反向：我们会不会侵入 JiuwenSwarm 不会，且是结构性的：单向依赖（`workswarm` 按 extra 引入、jiuwenbox 按本机服务引入），JiuwenSwarm 对我们零依赖；我们不跑它的进程、不实现它的协议、不改它的配置语义。若要贡献科学能力，走 Rail 插件 / Skill / MCP 的正向 PR，对它是加法。 --- ## 七、工作量 估算口径：同语言搬运约 800–1,500 行/人周；跨语言重写含测试约 250–400 行/人周；协议与语义对齐按耦合点计。不含产品需求变更与跨团队协同开销。**未做原型验证，第 0 阶段完成后需重新校准。** | 阶段 | 内容 | 乐观 | 可能 | 悲观 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | M0-a | 证伪 spike（四个判据，见第八节） | 2 | 3 | 5 | | M0-b | `sd-agent` 骨架 + `sd-api` 的 `agent-client` + 37 类事件映射 | 10 | 14 | 22 | | M0-c | 分层护栏、`ports/` 定稿、`adapters/native/` 兜底 | 3 | 4 | 6 | | M1-a | 工具面迁移 + 13,675 行域包加 HTTP 外壳 | 12 | 17 | 26 | | M1-b | 上下文三语义 + 证据门禁与评审检查点 | 6 | 9 | 15 | | M1-c | 科学探索 Provider（PUCT / idea-tree） | 8 | 12 | 20 | | M2-a~d | 按块接 JiuwenSwarm（Hub / Skill 包 / jiuwenbox / cron） | 15 | 22 | 36 | | M3-a | 分发：Python 运行时进单可执行文件 payload（双架构）、Docker | 8 | 11 | 17 | | M3-b | 测试与 CI：增 Python 层；E2E 大部保留（REST/SSE 与 Web 不变） | 6 | 9 | 14 | | **合计（M2 全接）** | | **70** | **101** | **161 人周** | | **不接任何 JiuwenSwarm 块** | | **55** | **79** | **125 人周** | **M2 各块彼此独立**，可以只接 Skill Hub 不接 jiuwenbox，或反过来。这是本方案与「整体二选一」的主要差别：**JiuwenSwarm 从一次性决策变成逐块定价**。 **不可逆点**：M1-a 完成后，工具实现不再留在 Node 侧。M0 全程可回滚。 --- ## 八、第 0 阶段的证伪判据 | # | 判据 | 决定什么 | |---|---|---| | ① | `create_deep_agent()` 跑通一次带工具调用 + 审批中断 + 流式的会话，并映射成现有 37 类 SSE | 自建装配的 4,000–8,000 行估算是否成立 | | ② | `register_window_mutator` 注入的受保护段，能否存活到最终 LLM 窗口（构造一个会被内置压缩器改写的长会话） | 上下文三语义能否等价迁移，还是要接受行为回退 | | ③ | 实现一个最小 `Provider` 并 `use_provider()`，验证 workflow 原语被整体替换后行为正确 | 科学探索能否成为多 agent 范式 | | ④ | `pip install workswarm` 后做依赖裁剪试验，量出可接受的最小依赖集 | M2 各块的分发成本 | 判据 ①③④ 直接决定路线，判据 ② 决定产品行为是否回退。**在第 0 阶段之前讨论总工期意义不大。** --- ## 九、待决定事项 1. **复用边界**：agent-core 直接依赖（本 issue）还是经 JiuwenSwarm Gateway（#84）。建议在 M0-a 一并验证后再定。 2. **是否采用 jiuwenbox**：采用则获得 Landlock、cgroup、推理隐私代理，但 **macOS 源码模式会失去沙箱**（jiuwenbox Linux-only）。需要产品明确。 3. **是否接 Skill 包管理**：涉及 6.2 的高 C 型侵入，三个选择需要拍板。 4. **控制面语言**：本方案保持 `services/api` 为 Node（保全约 81% 后端代码）。若未来要合并为单一 Python 后端，M0–M2 完成后可平滑过渡，但会额外触发 A3。 5. **差异化定位**：如果本项目的差异化主要在科学域能力（工具、连接器、证据溯源、科学环境、NPU），现有分层足够；如果在 agent 算法本身（上下文、探索、检索、演进），则应进一步收紧对 agent-core 的直接控制。这决定第 5 节各层级的使用频度。 --- ### 补充说明 - 本 issue 的全部结论来自上述基线 commit 的只读代码盘点，**未改动任何仓库**，未建分支、未提 PR。 - 归属用的「依赖率」是「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件数 / 该模块 `.py` 文件总数」，是**代理指标**而非逻辑占比的精确度量；每条归属结论另有行数对照或具体文件路径佐证。 - C 型侵入的判定口径是「模块文件是否 import `jiuwenswarm.common.config` / `jiuwenswarm.common.utils`」，是传递依赖的一级近似；真正接入前应在 M0/M2 用一次真实 import 验证完整传递闭包。 - 与 #84 互为补充，不替代。

This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

pr:196.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

pr:222.body:
## Summary

**Draft — do not merge until the full UT/ST/browser-E2E gates and remaining integration acceptance checks below are completed.** The implementation is available for review; targeted validation passed, but full local validation is incomplete.

Extract Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and expose its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools. This is the service-extraction work for #101 (part of #84), establishing a separate lifecycle and state boundary before the evolve migration in #102.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`. The candidate is `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e` (one commit; 45 changed files, including detected moves).

## 1. Independent service and state ownership

- Move `idea_tree_service`, `research_service`, the research engine, tree models, prompts and templates from evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree/src/sciencediscovery_idea_tree`.
- Remove both router registrations from the evolve server. The new package has no imports from evolve; the existing research algorithm is preserved rather than rewritten as part of the extraction.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI entry point, health endpoint, locked dependencies, shutdown cleanup and service-only authentication. Standalone startup fails closed without `SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`.
- Use a dedicated state root (`SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_DATA_DIR`, defaulting under the shared data root's `idea-tree` directory), atomic JSON persistence and independently persisted research settings.
- Copy legacy tree/research records on first startup without deleting originals. A migration marker prevents re-importing stale legacy data; conflicting destination records fail startup instead of overwriting data. Import the old API catalog's settings once, then keep settings authoritative in the service.
- Serve persisted skill references so skill deletion-impact checks include autonomous research as well as historical trees and chat-run references.

## 2. Service-owned MCP tools and capability isolation

The service publishes four tool contracts:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_idea_research` | Start autonomous research with an objective and prepared evidence/materials |
| `get_idea_research` | Query the current session's research and findings |
| `control_idea_research` | Pause, continue or end research |
| `view_idea_tree` | Read a historical tree graph |

The trusted control plane provisions a five-minute capability using its service credential. The scoped MCP endpoint supports initialization, discovery, calls, ping, notifications and revocation. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from that trusted scope, not model-supplied tool arguments. Continue grants are pinned to a specific research ID. Expired scopes are rejected, active scope count is bounded, and revoking a transport scope does not terminate autonomous research. Access logging is disabled for this process to avoid logging capability URLs.

The API obtains schemas from the service and contributes them to the existing JiuwenSwarm MCP bridge/native executor. The former hard-coded create/get tool definitions in `packages/evolve` are removed. Tool discovery failure does not prevent unrelated chat tools from being used.

## 3. TypeScript client and unchanged frontend interfaces

- Replace `services/api/src/idea-tree/python-client.ts` with `IdeaTreeServiceClient` in `packages/idea-tree`. The client provides authenticated, bounded HTTP transport, dynamic tool discovery, scoped MCP research calls, settings transport and historical-tree reads.
- Route active research through the independent service rather than evolve. Preserve the research-created event, create-time chat messages and SSE forwarding.
- Keep historical compatibility types/read transport in `packages/idea-tree`; legacy mutating `tree_*` tools remain disabled.
- Preserve all six frontend paths and their existing response shapes:

| Interface | Handling after this change | Contract mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Research service command/query | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Independent research lifecycle; control plane retains chat-message creation | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` | Independent service SSE, forwarded through the existing public route | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` | Historical graph read from independent storage | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned settings | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |
| `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned partial update, preserving values on an empty update | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |

These are contract-case mappings, not a claim that a full baseline/candidate L1 differential run passed. The committed lifecycle golden fixture records the stable `running → paused → paused after restart → completed` projection and is asserted by the service journey; it is not a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace.

## 4. Startup, packaging and test discovery

- Provision/start the new service through `scripts/start-stack.sh` and include it in the Docker image.
- Default to loopback port `4314`; reserve `4414` for the isolated browser-test stack and include it in busy-port checks.
- Add `pnpm idea-tree:test`, relocate the existing Python tree/research tests with the service, and include the service in tagged test discovery, environment preparation and coverage roots.
- Add standalone-service documentation covering configuration, migration and the remaining control-plane boundary.

## Compatibility, migration and scope boundaries

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained startup script/Docker packaging includes the new process; custom process supervisors must launch it and provide matching service URL/token configuration.
- Run one ASGI worker: background research tasks and short-lived scopes are process-local. Research and settings are persisted; the journey verifies recovery of paused research after restart.
- The adapter still reaches these frontend routes through the existing API control plane. Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning are **not** moved into the new service by this PR.
- Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; it does not receive provider API keys. Extracting the service does not remove that callback dependency from the wider stack.
- Prepared evidence is preserved, but this PR does not implement the artifact/provenance/CAS service tracked by #98 or change its ownership.
- This PR does not claim completion of the broader JiuwenSwarm migration or the full #101 integration acceptance matrix; full public-route differential and chat/agent trace verification remain review/validation follow-ups.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | PASS, recursive workspace build |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS, including test TypeScript configuration |
| Independent-service Python suite | 34 passed |
| `packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts` + `packages/idea-tree/src/client.test.ts` under Linux | 11 passed |
| `node test/contract/run.mjs --coverage` | Mapping check passed: 151/254 repository interface rows mapped; not 151 executed tests |
| `bash -n scripts/start-stack.sh` and `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh` | PASS |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` | PASS |

pr:261.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

pr:269.body:
CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

贡献者账号没有上游仓库写入权限，GitHub 的 `release:fix` 标签需由维护者添加。

## Summary

Fixes #264.

Make proxy setup usable from one **Network and proxy** settings entry, and keep local application transport independent of outbound proxy failures. Reuse the existing proxy registry, downloader cache/retry, and environment-readiness mechanisms rather than adding an automatic external-network startup gate.

## Changes

- Offer environment configuration, a custom HTTP(S)/SOCKS5 proxy, or direct access. Keep named proxies, bypass hosts and Web/MCP overrides under advanced settings; existing model overrides remain compatible.
- Stage proxy changes across settings tabs. The footer saves them; Cancel/X discards unsaved changes. Add an authenticated, non-persisting download-source connection diagnostic.
- Declare and lock Python HTTP/WebSocket SOCKS dependencies. Adapter loopback HTTP/WebSocket connections explicitly bypass outbound proxies; external HTTP clients are initialized lazily.
- Add small source-loadable shared routing/download helpers. Resolve model requests against their actual target, respect bypass rules, and pass the global policy to managed environment setup/create/install operations without mutating process-wide environment variables.
- Resolve environment mode on the remote Runner itself. Reject forwarding a host-local custom proxy to a remote Runner, with recovery guidance.
- Preserve underlying, redacted network errors and existing pinned versions, SHA-256/TLS verification, caches and retries. Update English/Chinese configuration, architecture and REST documentation.

## Validation

No real LLM API calls or paid tokens were used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace build and typecheck | Passed before rebase; upstream changes are E2E helpers/tests/docs only |
| Proxy transport, diagnostics and Runner environment tests | 28 passed |
| Model, downloader, Runner client and resolver regression tests | 41 passed |
| Targeted settings persistence / Runner policy propagation | 3 passed (overlaps Runner regression coverage) |
| Adapter hermetic tests | 234 passed; live gateway and real-model test files excluded |
| Proxy settings component tests | 4 passed |
| L1 checks | 4 passed on the rebased head |
| Browser settings journeys | 2 passed in 36.6s on the rebased head |
| Swarm mocked contracts | 9 passed before final rebase; unchanged product code |

The browser journeys use a real local API/Swarm stack, not mocked settings storage. They cover basic defaults; custom proxy save/cancel; cross-tab drafts; reload persistence; NO_PROXY; Web/MCP overrides and inheritance; rejection of deleting an in-use proxy; and removing references plus deleting the proxy in one save. Only the first journey's connection-test response is browser-mocked; transport ST tests exercise local HTTP/SOCKS proxy fixtures and authentication failures without external access.

The legacy layout E2E is adapted but remains quarantined and was not run. No production service was restarted.

## Scope and boundaries

- This does not grant sandbox network access or add an automatic direct fallback when a configured proxy fails.
- The manual diagnostic checks one download source, not every provider or model credentials. There is no new startup preflight framework or traffic dashboard.
- Saving multiple settings sections is sequential, not a cross-section transaction: a later failure does not roll back earlier successful requests. Unsaved changes remain drafts.
- SOCKS5 support in Undici remains experimental. Remote end-to-end proxy reachability, binary installation and real external providers have not been newly exercised by this PR.

pr:293.body:
## Summary

Add all **132 DeepResearchBench II tasks** as a release-only L5 benchmark, following the existing tagged Playwright real-E2E framework. L5 now selects **151** real cases (19 inherited + 132 DRB II); L4 remains 19. No new paid cases enter PR/L2 or merge/L3 gates.

## Design and scope

- Statically declare every task identity; collection is offline and cannot silently shrink when data or credentials are absent.
- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

Runbook: `test/benchmarks/deepresearchbench-ii/README.md`.

| Total tool rounds | 1,956 | 2,128 | **2,042** | **>=2,655** | **>=3,063** |
| Sum of research minutes | 1,223.706945 | 1,401.800000 | **1,312.753472** | **+20% (~1,575.304167 min)** | **+30% (~1,706.579514 min)** |
| P95 of task peak RSS, GiB | 15.803780 | 6.599500 | **11.201639801** | **>=13.441967761** | **>=14.562131741** |

Boundaries are inclusive, with blocking taking precedence. Resource thresholds are independent: tokens +15%/+25%, rounds +30%/+50%, research duration +20%/+30%, and memory increase max(20%, 1 GiB)/max(30%, 2 GiB). The implementation compares unrounded values; integer count limits above round up. Memory P95 uses linear interpolation, calculated separately for each historical run and then averaged for the baseline. Keep the suite maximum visible; **131.07 GiB on A3 v2 `da-17-5` is an unresolved outlier, not an accepted normal maximum baseline**.

The operator reported large per-task score spreads (maximum 76 points). Therefore temporary mode gates the **50-task mean**, not individual score drops. Low scores and resource breaches do not trigger automatic retry-until-green. Absolute case budgets/timeouts and completeness checks remain separate.

The final-result scope matches the historical A3 summaries: one final valid research result and its selected evaluation per task, excluding earlier failed attempts. Sources are `BiomniBench-L5-50-A3-监控指标.xlsx` and `biomni-l5-50-A3-监控指标-v2.csv`; the latter mixes 39 initial results, 5 regression results and 6 reference results across revisions. These are diagnostic inputs, not new paid validation of this PR head. The generation/judge splits are 185,333,947/853,327 and 203,191,614/820,536 tokens; total tool calls are 2,068 and 2,305; maximum RSS values are 31.262096 and 131.07 GiB.

Additional incomplete references remain outside baseline calibration: WSL mean 65.95 over 40 scored tasks, known tokens >=6,747,892, 1,924 rounds and 787.11 research minutes over 41 recorded tasks, maximum complete sampled RSS 14.354 GiB. CPU mean 64.45 over 38 scored tasks, 9,652,680 recorded tokens, 1,922 rounds, 1,350 research minutes and 7.58 GiB maximum complete RSS. Token accounting differs across old/new runs; these values must not be pooled into the A3 baseline.

Explicit candidate mode remains available for an unapproved complete result set, and the existing approved identity-matched compare mode remains for compatibility. No run automatically approves or replaces a baseline.

## Non-blocking serial recovery: three additional retries

`test/benchmarks/biomnibench-da/suite.py` finishes every unattempted task before starting deferred retries. Preparation errors, process failures, resource-check failures and malformed per-case metadata are recorded with reasons; they do not abort subsequent tasks. Per-case inactivity/overall deadlines prevent one stalled task holding the rest indefinitely. Execution remains serial, not unbounded parallel work.

- **Research/delivery failure:** end-to-end retry when both nonempty `trace.md` and `answer.txt` and verified completed delivery evidence are unavailable.
- **Evaluation-only failure:** use immutable completed artifacts and measured generation evidence to retry only the judge, including timeout/invalid-JSON failures rather than only `UNREPORTED_JUDGE_TOKENS`.
- Allow **three additional retries after the initial attempt**, with a single counter per task across both modes. Immediate nested judge retries are disabled inside the suite. Stop at the first valid result, never the highest score; successful tasks are skipped on same-SHA resume.
- Preserve numbered attempt directories and all failure evidence. Report first-pass completion, recovered completion, final per-task state and attempts in the serial summary. Exhausted or accounting-blocked tasks enter `tracking-required.json` for investigation and deduplicated issue tracking; the script does not automatically publish GitHub issues.
- Evaluation recovery writes a new selected metric document and artifact hashes without overwriting original research. It includes all prior recovery usage checks; a later success cannot erase unknown spend from an intervening attempt. Valid scores remain visible even when required cost accounting still blocks the gate.
- `attempt-costs.json` separately reports known generation/judge tokens, unknown-usage counters and summed attempt wall time **including failures and retries**. It is a lower bound when usage is missing, not the comparable final-result resource aggregate. Preparation, research, judging and suite wall time are not conflated.

Only verified owned descendants are stopped, with PID start-time checks. Cleanup stays within the suite-owned inactive reconstructible environments; dataset inputs, CAS records, artifacts and evidence remain intact. Low resource checks avoid starting paid work while preserving the other task outcomes.

## Runtime fixes retained from the original candidate

- Reuse verified CAS content for unchanged workspace files only while source/CAS identities remain unchanged; mutations or tampering invalidate reuse. This avoids repeated streaming of multi-gigabyte inputs after every tool round.
- Respect configured Python package mirrors and explicit sources. Bound external environment commands to 180 seconds and pip network waits/retries, retaining gateway stall detection.
- Prefer positive provider usage aliases over zero placeholders and retain the full agent-loop usage summary rather than only the last model call.
- Keep the session title visible beside the wider full-loop token summary. Give the title a 120px flex basis so a long project name shares the available width instead of shrinking the title to zero; token accounting and unrelated journeys are unchanged.

## CI verification fixes

[Run 39754274282](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39754274282) failed only `check:research-python-ut`: its artifact records the injected paper Python 3.14, source builds of NumPy 2.2.6 / SciPy 1.15.3, and missing OpenBLAS. Fix the injected default in the shared runner while retaining the interpreter override in the research script. Validate with the same paper-3.14/gateway-3.12 combination rather than two Python-3.12 environments.

Rebased onto main `f99571df6f795d6f1b20ef248195149c9cabf836` as five linear commits, with no merge commits. Removed obsolete intermediate changes to `remote-compute-prune.test.ts` from the replayed history, retaining main's complete live-process rescan and regression fixtures throughout. The old branch could merge by final tree but could not rebase because intermediate fixture changes conflicted before being reverted. Each rewritten commit now replays cleanly on this main. Server-only ARM64 and dash-path adapters are not committed.

Restore LF in files changed by the rebase, enforce LF for workflow YAML, and restore the E2E driver's executable mode. Align the token alias fixture with main's retained conflict diagnostics, and make the harness self-test use the host's actual architecture.

Sandbox tests retain their isolation assertions while respecting the configured bubblewrap path. The shell-pruning fixture retains main's copied-bash fixture, executable-readiness checks and live-binary race regressions, and the NPU negative test uses an absent device rather than assuming the host has no Ascend cards. The skill-draft API journey explicitly loads the platform-owned skill through `read_skill`, retaining its review, publication, and file-content assertions without depending on an SDK-local import alias.

The shared runner defaults `SCIENCE_TEST_PYTHON` to the prepared gateway environment (Python 3.12, pinned by `services/gateway/.python-version`) and preserves an explicit caller override. It no longer injects the paper environment, which may use Python 3.14 and cannot install the pinned scientific wheels; the RACE contract shares that dependency-aware, no-skip driver. The harness respects an explicit `UV_CACHE_DIR`. The Evolve distribution journey supports configured PyPI mirrors and checksum-verified runtime/release-source caches while still exercising real installation, quota cancellation, sandboxed PUCT improvement, and restart reuse.

Tested commit: `9ef02324e10a888d1ffedd7469e6808075ab551f`, including main `ddebc31feef2a6e1bd1197ddb5a14ca08b6d4e38`. Full workspace build and locked dependency preparation completed. All layers used the repository's `pnpm ci:*` entry points with the PR profile and JiuwenSwarm backend.

Both the default and an explicit compatible interpreter override passed the full **4468/4468** UT layer; no skip or assertion was weakened. An unprivileged Ubuntu 26.04 container reproduces the original three shell-pruning failures; after integrating main's fixture and product fix, all **13/13** pruning tests pass, including race and unreadable-process regressions. The research Python driver also executes the pinned verifier contracts with explicit dependencies and rejects skips.

Validation ran on Linux ARM64 with uncommitted execution-target adapters and a local dash-path shim; these are not included in the candidate commit. It preserved the selected test identities and assertions; the ARM64-only adapter is **not** included in this PR. These results do not replace native GitHub AMD64 checks.

### E2E user journeys

Mocked browser E2E was rerun against the same tested commit. Each planned identity was reconciled exactly once across the four repository-defined shards. Remaining failed browser journeys:

## Summary

Fix protocol-specific token usage parsing and make provider accounting non-gating in real E2E. No provider-specific workaround, Swarm source modification, or relaxation of task/delivery/quality assertions.

## Problem and evidence

The October 14 manual daily run (38546559384) completed the functional steps of seven basic journeys but failed each on `outputTokens > 0`. The preceding official-DeepSeek nightly passed the same checks.

A short Chat Completions probe returned both standard `completion_tokens: 31` and an extra `output_tokens: 0` (input 35, total 66). The shared normalizer preferred the latter. The model gateway then forwarded the incorrect zero to Swarm. No credentials or live response payloads are committed.

## Changes

- Require the requested protocol when normalizing usage. Chat Completions reads prompt/completion token fields; Responses reads input/output token fields, including its cache detail object.
- Preserve legitimate zero values. Do not reconstruct missing input/output counts from totals or fall back to another protocol's fields. Missing/invalid accounting remains unavailable and does not fail model generation.
- Remove provider token counts and usage availability as real basic-journey pass criteria. Preserve usage evidence (or an unavailable diagnostic) and the existing request ledger. Functional assertions remain unchanged; accounting does not gate scoring.
- Document this boundary. Deterministic parsing and gateway tests remain gating.

## Validation

- Model package tests: 50 passed.
- Model gateway tests: 35 passed, including streaming/non-streaming accounting propagation and completion without reported usage.
- Regression cases cover conflicting fields, null/missing/invalid values, legitimate zero, and final usage-only streaming chunks.
- Test TypeScript check (`tsconfig.tests.json`): passed.
- API dependency build: passed.
- Documentation checks: passed (126 files); `git diff --check`: passed.

The seven paid real journeys and full nightly suite have not been rerun for this PR. This fixes accounting and CI policy, not the separate evolution thinking-budget or research-team timeout failures. Token usage is provider-reported telemetry, not a guarantee of billing completeness or a reliable budget limit when the provider omits it.

## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes GitHub issue [#310](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/310).

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

pr:316.body:
Automatically generated Session titles could expose inline reasoning and were cut off at 24 characters even when that left an incomplete English phrase. This change generates complete summaries, filters reasoning, and separates stored titles from sidebar overflow styling.

## Changes

- Summarize the first message's core topic or intent in the user's language. Target 8–16 characters for CJK (maximum 24, including spaces and Latin names); target 3–6 words for other languages (maximum 8 whitespace-separated words and 80 Unicode characters).
- Regenerate once from the original message when the model exceeds the budget, returns an ellipsis, or reports truncated visible output. Preserve the complete accepted phrase instead of slicing it. Aggregate provider usage across successful responses.
- Use a neutral provisional `Session MM-DD HH:mm` title for long messages. Failed, empty, or still-invalid refinement retains that safe title; manual renames remain protected.
- Strip nested, unclosed and ordinary `<think>` blocks. Never use separate provider reasoning as the title.
- Keep sidebar ellipses in CSS; the existing full-title tooltip remains available. Existing stored titles and manual titles are not migrated.

## Policy and comparison evidence

The [title policy and acceptance examples](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/324cf7b2d0f3b2da4dc6ce7fe76674cfa3fb5346/docs/en/developer-docs/session-titles.md) document long Chinese/English cases and distinguish public evidence from assumptions. Open WebUI's public prompt and sidebar source show short topic summaries and CSS overflow; LibreChat documents a language-aware short-title prompt. Claude's help documents renaming but does not disclose its naming algorithm. The language budgets and bounded regeneration above are our own policy, not claimed competitor internals.

## Validation

Remote implementation: 324cf7b2d0f3b2da4dc6ce7fe76674cfa3fb5346. Its Git tree b8ee654a0d702a192673a8f1b7a26a7afb9d832b is verified identical to locally validated commit 1624420d544008eebc6f4c2cb856a7be85e6ff69. GitHub Git Data API was used because the Git transport was unreachable.

- Title unit suite: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Cases include long Chinese/English outputs, regeneration, language-budget boundaries, incomplete output, nested reasoning, safe rejection and aggregated usage.
- Workspace build: **32 package/service projects completed**.
- API/schema type checks and `tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Documentation: **127 files linted, 0 issues; 126 files checked for links**.
- E2E metadata: **62 spec files, 0 errors** (11 existing legacy warnings).
- Pinned Playwright discovery: **1 new journey discovered**.
- Local full UT/ST/mocked E2E layers could not complete on the available Windows host: Bash/process-spawning limitations prevent the Linux-oriented runners from reaching their cases. WSL provisioning was also unsuccessful. These are coverage limitations, not passing results. No real-model quality evaluation was run.

## E2E user journeys

**BLOCKED locally** — `test/journey-session-titles.spec.ts` uses a journey-owned loopback model and covers long Chinese and English first messages → oversized model output → shorter complete title → persisted title after reload → sidebar CSS and full-title tooltip. A third scenario covers reasoning-only output retaining a safe default. The stub is explicitly enabled only for this journey.

The added journey has been discovered and its metadata checked, but has not yet been executed successfully. The updated GitHub Actions run must establish the Linux full-layer results; no previous-tip CI result is presented as validation of this update.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (existing label retained).

User impact: Complete automatic titles without reasoning content or stored truncation ellipses. An oversized result may require one additional naming request.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration or API shape change; existing titles are unchanged.

Closes #314

pr:372.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.
- `pnpm docs:check`, `pnpm architecture:check`, and `pnpm ci:selftest` (55/55) passed. The E2E meta check reported 0 errors.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. Those layers provision JiuwenSwarm outside the repository tree, which this environment does not allow. This pull request is a draft until those layers have results.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the connector journey on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`. Local stack, native executor, runner and API on ports 4480 and 4481.

`test/journey-custom-mcp.spec.ts`: 3 passed, 0 failed. Two custom MCP servers are used, one healthy and one that exits during the handshake. Both appear, and only the failing one shows its error. Turning the healthy server off removes its connector from the picker and from the next run's tool list; the settings row and switch remain. Turning it on brings the connector back, still selected.

`journey-plugin-composition`: the connector-panel step passed. A later step expects `todo_create`, which the native executor does not provide. That failure is outside this change.

The mocked `pnpm ci:e2e` layer was not run.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: connectors whose MCP server is off disappear from the picker and are not offered to the agent. A connector whose enabled server fails to connect stays listed and shows the connection error.

Compatibility and migration: callers that treated "missing from an applied catalog" as `unavailable`, or that expected those connectors to remain in `GET /api/connectors`, need to handle `disabled` and the shorter list. No configuration change is required.

![Connector picker when enabled servers fail to connect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a977f904-fd31-4182-8cef-5656492cd825)

![The same failure text at a narrow width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/388977e4-55bc-42b8-9d6d-961c87f31353)

pr:390.body:
This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.

## Validation

- `node --test --experimental-test-coverage scripts/repo-issue-pipeline.test.mjs`: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Host line coverage **97.64%**, branch coverage **96.00%**, function coverage **50.00%** in this direct Node report. Do not interpret these as repository-wide coverage.
- Coverage gaps: the real SDK dynamic import/constructor and CLI signal callback wiring were not exercised through a live Codex process. CLI child-process coverage is not merged into the parent report. Factory injection verifies start/resume/options/event/failure behavior, but does not prove account/CLI compatibility or model scheduling quality. No paid Codex smoke, actual OS-signal integration or service-manager installation test was run.
- Skill metadata validation, JavaScript syntax check, architecture check and CI catalog check passed.
- Markdown lint: **0 issues**. Documentation links: **141 tracked Markdown files checked**, no broken targets.
- Full local UT/ST/browser E2E are **not claimed passed**. The clean checkout has not been provisioned with all package-local dependencies/build outputs: shared UT collection stopped at missing `react` in an existing web test. Initial pnpm entry-point checks also encountered dependency-layout verification; no shared dependency tree was purged. The host's serialized heavy-test lock was occupied by an existing worker, so this PR does not interrupt that task or start competing full-stack runs. Full CI remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

ScienceDiscovery product E2E: **not applicable to the changed product path**, because there is no application UI/API/agent-runtime behavior change. Full browser-suite execution is nevertheless unverified as noted above. The new contributor tool is covered by offline request-to-session/output tests; a real Codex-account-to-fork-PR journey remains an explicit integration gap and must not be represented as a mocked product E2E pass.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: optional contributor tooling only; no automatic process or new application dependency.

Compatibility and migration: none for application users. SDK dependencies are isolated in the skill's optional host package. Existing private pipeline state is neither imported nor modified.

## Follow-up: Issue-as-Interface + OSS ops skills

Added on top of `repo-issue-pipeline` (commit `01f1df6`):

- **IAI delivery:** `issue-as-interface-contract`, `issue-review-agent-ready`, `iai-developer-patrol`, `iai-worker-implement`, `iai-reviewer-patrol`, `iai-reviewer-execute`, `magpie-pr-review-pipeline`
- **OSS ops (parallel):** `oss-ops-newcomer-gfi`, `oss-ops-stale-sweep`, `oss-ops-maintainer-stats`, `oss-ops-repo-health`
- **Docs:** [zh](docs/zh/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) / [en](docs/en/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) (+ links from CONTRIBUTING and issue-pipeline pages)

Still opt-in documentation/skills only — installing does not start bots. Reviewer execute authority is skill text for hosts that enable it; this PR does not merge or change CI policy.

  本 PR 接入 `/idea-tree` 完整执行流程，支持主 Agent 创建探索树、派发设计与评估 Subagent、
  回传评分和 insight，并在页面查看树结构与节点结果。树状态使用本地文件持久化，无需 Neo4j。

  ### 主要变更

  1. **提取 Tree / Node 基础结构**
     - 在 Python 中定义基础节点及树查询能力，由 IdeaTree 和 PuctTree 分别继承。

  2. **实现 Idea Tree 的 Python 状态管理与本地持久化**
     - 在 Python 中实现节点操作、执行领取、结果提交、失败重试和 insight 回传。

pr:408.body:
Closes #309.

The artifact viewer was a small card — 1080×758 inside a 1920×1080 window — with a 560px preview inside it, so a report, a table or a plot was read through three nested scrollbars. It is now a large-screen content window whose content actually fills it.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css` | `.artifact-modal-panel` → `width: min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`, `height: min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`. `.artifact-modal-body` gets `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0` (it owns the leftover height and the scroll), header and mode tabs are pinned with `flex: 0 0 auto`. Markdown prose keeps a readable measure: `.markdown-body > :is(p, ul, ol, dl, blockquote) { max-width: 76ch }`. |
| `apps/web/src/styles/artifacts.css` | Inside `.artifact-modal-panel .artifact-modal-body` only: `max-height: none` for `.manuscript-preview`, `.artifact-source-preview`, `.dataset-table-wrapper`, `.notebook-cells`, and `.annotatable-figure img { max-height: min(760px, calc(100vh - 240px)) }`. Inline and timeline previews share those classes and keep their 560/460/420px caps. `.manuscript-preview pre` (fenced code blocks inside a report) deliberately keeps its 460px cap so a huge source file cannot stretch the panel into one endless column. |
| `apps/web/src/styles/memory-graph.css` | Stale comment on `.evidence-title` that still described the old fixed viewer size. |
| `apps/web/tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx` | The #309 test now asserts the panel size, the 76ch measure, the body flex rule, the pinned header/tabs and the whole in-modal override block — plus counter-assertions that the base 560px / 460px caps survive. |

Review follow-up (HongyeZhou, `38a46e01`) is included: the taller window alone added blank space, so the rest of this PR is about making the content use it.

## Verification (specific to this change)

Measured on the **real `ArtifactModal` component** built from this branch with the repo's Vite config, served at a 1920×1063 viewport (the 1600×960 window), in headless Chromium:

| | Panel | `.artifact-modal-body` | Preview | Scrollbars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (`f47ff584`), long markdown | 1600×960 | 614px tall, flex `0 1 auto`, ends 206px above the panel bottom | `.manuscript-preview` 560px, capped at 560px, scrolls inside itself | 2 (preview + body) |
| **Before** (`f47ff584`), source file | 1600×960 | 534px tall, ends 286px above the bottom | `.artifact-source-preview` 460px, self-scrolling | 2 |
| **After** (`38a46e01`), long markdown | 1600×960 | 818px tall, flex `1 1 auto`, bottom edge at 1011 vs panel bottom 1012 | 8865px tall, `max-height: none`, does not self-scroll | 1 (body) |
| **After** (`38a46e01`), source file | 1600×960 | 818px tall, same 1px gap | 15697px tall, `max-height: none` | 1 (body) |

Also measured after the change: `.annotatable-figure img` → `min(760px, calc(100vh - 240px))` = 753px at this viewport; fenced `pre` inside a report still 460px; and in a non-modal container the computed caps are still 560px (`.manuscript-preview`), 460px (source / table / notebook) and 420px (figure image), so inline and timeline previews are unchanged. Smaller windows behave as before: 1280×800 → panel 1200×633 with the same fill (body 491px, bottom 1px above the panel edge); `<=900px` still goes full screen.

### Screenshots (real component, 1600×960 window)

Long markdown report — top of the document:

![markdown preview, top](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/after-md-top.png)

The same report scrolled to the bottom: the document runs to the panel's bottom edge, no empty band:

![markdown preview, scrolled to the bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pr-assets-408/pr-assets-408/after-md-bottom.png)
