pr:412.body:
Explicit delegated tasks can now use Codex as a Specialist runtime while keeping ScienceDiscovery's child Workspace, Brief, execution permissions, timeline and Artifact publication paths. Missing credentials pause the child and show an in-conversation API-key config card, backed by the platform encrypted secret channel.

Refs #385. This is only the locked 2026-10-19 MVP; it does not close the full issue.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Specialist create/update/read accepts credential-free `runtime: {kind: "codex", model?: string}`. Omitted or native runtime keeps existing behavior and the exact legacy configuration hash; only non-native runtime enters the hash.
- Explicit `task(specialistId=…)` replaces the child's model-loop factory with the pinned official Codex SDK. Structured Codex decisions request validated platform tools; its native shell is disabled, its sandbox is read-only, and it runs in fresh private scratch/HOME directories. Product commands still use platform execution bindings, never a Codex host shell.
- Normalized started/progress/tool_call/file_change/need_input/done events map to existing child timeline/results, including usage and Codex thread ID. Artifacts come only from platform declaration receipts.
- Config credentials never enter Specialist metadata, argv, model prompts or chat. The dedicated authenticated endpoint stores a Session-scoped encrypted key; Session/Project deletion removes it. Always-allow does not supply credentials. Codex children use platform permission decisions even when their lead uses JiuwenSwarm.

## Validation

Candidate: `88a936f7`.

- Focused runtime UT/ST: **21 passed, 0 failed/skipped** (20 UT + 1 ST). Includes official SDK transport with a synthetic executable, real pinned SDK/CLI against a loopback Responses fixture, platform execution/Artifact handoff, event mapping, invalid decisions/arguments, cancellation/deadline, encrypted-secret/reload/hash behavior, mixed Swarm/Codex permission routing and preservation of the frozen Brief/platform history on continuation. No vendor/model traffic.
- Adjacent regression: **115 passed, 0 failed/skipped** across Store, built-in specialists, Subagent lifecycle, AgentRun and Idea Tree composition.
- Full workspace + test TypeScript checks passed; API/test checks repeated after the permission fix.
- L1: **4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed**, including architecture, docs, catalog and E2E metadata.
- Broader ST: initially **17 planned / 17 executed / 16 passed / 1 failed**. The failure is `check:swarm-sdk-contract` → `test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once` (3-second timeout). The changed branch has no changes to those Python tests, adapter sources or Swarm patches. Unmodified main passed **16/16** planned ST checks; its standalone Python contract passed **66 tests + 3 subtests**. An isolated candidate rerun at `9f96171d` passed **17/17**, with no intervening product changes. The initial timeout remains disclosed; its exact cause was not established. The final follow-up only preserves continuation context in the adapter and is covered by the 21 focused checks.
- Full UT was interrupted by the host reboot and has no final verdict. Focused checks above were rerun afterward; the complete UT and mocked-browser suites are not claimed.

Node UT/ST coverage of new executable runtime modules: **99% lines / 95.20% branches / 87.50% functions** (`agent`, `codex`, `config`, `permissions`; the contract file is types only). Node/tsx reports the closing sink block in `agent.ts` as uncovered (lines 36–37); done-event behavior is asserted. Remaining branches/functions include optional compatibility/default-factory paths and defensive error handling. These measurements do not quantify all added lines in the existing Store/HTTP/run/UI files; those have targeted regression/browser evidence rather than a full added-line coverage claim. Real CLI cancellation after spawn/descendant shutdown and provider-auth success are not established by the synthetic stream cancellation checks.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS**, tested `88a936f7`: normal product startup with isolated data/ports, loopback-only scripted lead and public browser/API path. The focused journey registers a Codex specialist, explicitly delegates under Always-allow, observes the interactive password config card, checks input bounds at **390×900 and 1440×900 (DPR 1)**, cancels the child, and verifies stale secret submission returns 409.

- Native lead: **1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed/skipped**.
- Default JiuwenSwarm lead: **1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed/skipped**, plus **9/9** supplemental backend checks.
- Commands: `CI_E2E_BACKEND=legacy CI_E2E_GREP='Show Codex auth card' bash .ci/run-e2e.sh mocked`, and the same command with `CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm` (prepared dependencies and separate run-owned data/ports).

Successful card-to-vendor authentication/model completion was not exercised; secret acceptance and SDK/CLI completion are covered separately with synthetic credentials and a local provider. No paid provider validation is claimed.

## Later phases

Host-process confinement/hardening, durable Codex thread continuation and crash recovery, browser/device OAuth and broader credential management, ACP, additional SDKs, runtime picker/probe UI, #64, and full Skills/MCP bridging remain outside this PR. The adapter exposes a focused platform tool subset. Existing platform execution/artifact semantics are reused; this does not implement the earlier broad Runner/ACP prototypes.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: explicit Codex-backed Specialist delegation and an in-conversation credential card.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing native specialists and clients; new runtime metadata is opt-in.

pr:421.body:
Refs #385.

Codex Specialist tasks now run the model transport inside the Runner's Bubblewrap/seccomp launch boundary, with inner Codex `danger-full-access`. Platform tools keep their own Runner execution and offline/allowlist network permissions. Explicit declarations are the only deliverable handoff: undeclared files do not create Artifacts, file-change steps, generated-file provenance, or execution Workspace snapshots/diffs.

**Dependency:** stacked on the still-open MVP #412. This PR targets `main` and currently includes the MVP commits. Resolve that dependency and rebase when appropriate; do not merge #412 as part of this work. This PR does not close #385 or implement Phase 3.

**Draft / DoD gap:** successful live Codex authentication is blocked by the absence of an approved API key. Do not merge until the remaining live-auth matrix is verified.

## Behavior

- Same-channel Specialist chat can apply validated model, reasoning, wall-clock timeout and fallback settings through `configure_specialist_runtime`. The existing secret card remains the configuration fallback and can disable native recovery before startup. Credentials stay outside chat, catalog metadata and argv.
- Each task has an independent Workspace and private `CODEX_HOME`. The pinned CLI uses the Runner launch implementation locally on the API host; native Codex shell/MCP/search/subagents are disabled or rejected, and project `.codex` configuration is masked. There is no shared sandbox. Linux/local Bubblewrap is required for the model-process sandbox.
- `declare_artifact(path|paths)` is the explicit handoff API; only successful platform receipts enter `artifacts[]`. Commands, execution status and logs remain auditable.
- Runtime startup/auth/tool unavailability defaults to a visible `builtin-code-engineer` fallback, with opt-out through profile/chat/card. Cancellation, deadlines, turn limits, ordinary task failures, denied direct consent and failures after potentially dispatched work do not replay work through fallback. Confirmed pre-dispatch tool blockers remain recoverable.
- Direct model execution requires explicit `runtime.execution=direct` plus separate `direct_code` consent. Tool direct execution uses the existing request/execute consent pair; sandbox Always Allow does not authorize it.

## Validation

- Focused UT: **169 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** across Specialist runtime, workspace bindings, shell observation, Runner lifecycle/sandbox/direct execution, CAS leases and provenance.
- Focused ST: **2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**: official pinned Codex SDK/CLI through outer Bubblewrap + inner full access against a local Responses fixture; filesystem/environment/project-config isolation and nested-userns denial probe.
- L1: **planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4**, no failures/skips.
- Type checks: test sources, API, Runner and web passed. Build passed; subsequent changes were rebuilt for affected packages.
- Browser: **1 passed, 0 failed/skipped; 4/4 journey steps**, password/config fallback and cancellation. Screenshots inspected at **390×900 and 1440×900**. The browser run used `d19dfc17`; later changes affect the launcher/docs/CLI driver, not the web bundle.
- Public API/production CLI journey: **5 scenarios passed**, plus startup (6/6 steps): explicit delegation/configuration and advanced settings/handoff, cancellation, timeout, fallback enabled, fallback disabled.
- Live invalid-key invocation: **2 scenarios passed**, plus startup (3/3 steps), using the actual pinned CLI/started Codex threads and the default live provider endpoint. This run used `ce7503de`; the final cancellation-race check is covered by focused UT and the repeated local API matrix. This exercises recovery on/off with deliberately invalid credentials; it does **not** certify successful authentication or provider work.

Commands: `node --import tsx --test <focused suites>`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`, package typechecks/builds, `pnpm ci:l1`, `SPECIALIST_BROWSER=1 node test/api/specialist-runtime-journey.mjs`, and `SPECIALIST_REAL=1 SPECIALIST_CASES=fallback-on,fallback-off node test/api/specialist-runtime-journey.mjs`.

Full `pnpm ci:ut` was attempted but blocked **before discovery**: the local JiuwenSwarm checkout lacks patch target files (`agent_ws_server.py`, `call_timeout_patch.py`). The same setup failure was reproduced with detached upstream/main `a0cf9c77` and the same fixture. No full-UT test counts are claimed. Full ST and full browser layers were not completed; targeted suites were used. Swarm-backend execution, remote model-process placement, macOS, successful live authentication and the remaining live scenarios are unverified. GitCode CodeCheck is ignored.

## DoD matrix

| Required path | Deterministic product coverage | Real Codex-auth coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit task | PASS: explicit Specialist ID, frozen hash, separate Workspace/thread | Invalid-key invocation exercised; successful auth/work BLOCKED |
| Config card / same channel | PASS: browser password/opt-out/cancel; API key submission; settings applied by Specialist | Invalid-key config submission exercised; valid-key continuation BLOCKED |
| Cancel / timeout | PASS: active CLI/provider wait cancelled; deadline terminal status; no fallback/replay | BLOCKED without approved valid key |
| Explicit handoff | PASS: declared result only; scratch output omitted; execution snapshots suppressed | BLOCKED without approved valid key |
| Fallback enabled / disabled | PASS: terminal native recovery versus surfaced failure | PASS: started live CLI/thread with deliberately invalid key, recovery on/off |
| Nested sandbox probe | PASS: outer isolation + inner full access; nested userns denied | Live invalid-key CLI launches through the same outer sandbox |

Run the full successful-auth matrix with `SPECIALIST_REAL=1 SPECIALIST_KEY_FILE=<private-file> SPECIALIST_MODEL=<model> node test/api/specialist-runtime-journey.mjs`. The key is submitted through the private config endpoint and never put in argv.

## Phase 3 residuals

Durable provider-thread continuation beyond a task, additional runtimes/ACP, shared sandboxes, remote model-process scheduling, full observability, and full Skills/MCP bridging remain deferred. No Phase 3 work was started. Host ChatGPT OAuth is not imported; this configuration surface supports API keys.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
User impact: sandboxed Codex delegation, explicit deliverable handoff and configurable runtime recovery.
Compatibility and migration: native/omitted runtime behavior and legacy hashes are retained. Codex defaults to an outer sandbox; direct execution requires separate consent.

pr:426.body:
Draft: please do not review or merge yet. Validation is incomplete; this PR records the current candidate for follow-up.

When the real research-team E2E polling budget expires, a run that is still running can be classified as a failed delivery solely because it has not cited a final artifact. This change keeps active delivery status as `running` and records budget exhaustion separately as integration `timed_out`, including elapsed time, the last polled run state, and the cancellation request result. The timeout still fails the test explicitly; successful runs must still deliver a readable, nonempty final artifact.

Refs #239. Partial fix; keep #239 open.

## Scope

- Preserve active delivery status for queued, running, and blocked runs, with or without cited artifacts.
- Retain terminal delivery validation, including missing/unreadable output and partial delivery on failed runs.
- Record budget exhaustion and cancellation HTTP/transport results, including cancellation races with terminal transitions.
- Preserve safe timeout/cancellation fields in public score artifacts; keep raw cancellation errors and delivery text in diagnostic evidence.
- Keep the existing run budget. Real BRCA1 execution and full local gates remain unverified.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe`.
Candidate: `55ae8b4b07ff69e63b9bd50c13ce330a8e832c56`.

This reproduces the reported classifier input, not the historical 55-minute browser run. The additional team-result helper cases exercise newly introduced code and are not claimed as baseline failures.

The collector/helper tests use simulated API responses. They do not establish the complete browser, model, orchestration, or finalizer journey.

## Validation

pr:440.body:
JiuwenSwarm's background Skill-index requests were counted as Session turns by both cancellation-test gateways. This produced false queue-ordering failures (`2 !== 1`) and could leave an active or blocked run hanging after an assertion failed. The fixtures now answer no-tools housekeeping requests without counting them, and both queue tests cancel remaining work in `finally`.

Refs #251. Partial fix; keep #251 open pending repository-wide validation follow-up. All issue-specific scenarios below pass; the broader gates are not fully green. The default `/llm/default` ownership issue remains outside this change.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe`.
Tested candidate: `1b34a9c5a7ca8d30205995459b3157c64530c072` on Linux with real JiuwenSwarm.
Review candidate: `674fd641b0906594d79c055c441cf6d905f41321` — the same patch merged with upstream main `9ff02721`; see [Current integration status](#current-integration-status) for what that merge changed and how far it is revalidated.

| Scenario | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Both fixtures ignore background requests before and after a Session turn, including streamed requests | Both new regression cases fail with the original fixtures | 2/2 pass; tool-enabled turns are still counted |
| Cancelling queued work never admits its prompt to the Session | Vulnerable fixture counted all requests | Pass in the full cancellation file |
| A blocked run holds its queue despite Skill-index background work | Real baseline emitted a no-tools request followed by a 68-tools request; assertion failed `2 !== 1`, then required a 60-second external timeout | Pass with real Swarm |
| Assertion failure cleans up queued and active/blocked work | Baseline failure left the worker hanging | Injected assertion failures in both queue cases: all runs cancelled, complete TAP output, normal exit 1 for the two intentional failures; no guard timeout |
| Skill changes trigger incremental indexing without invalidating queue assertions | Reproduced background-call interference after a Skill change | Blocked-queue case passes after adding another Skill to an isolated instance |

The patch changes only `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`.

## Validation

Final candidate:

- Full cancellation file through real Swarm: 11 executed, 11 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The same file also passes 11/11 within the full UT run.
- L1 (`pnpm ci:l1`): 4 planned/executed/passed, 0 failed/skipped.
- UT (`pnpm ci:ut`): 3724 planned, 3685 executed, 3678 passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped; 39 NOT_RUN after a server-test worker failure. Full typecheck and tagged self-tests pass.
- Three remote-binary-pruning failures also reproduce on the unchanged baseline (4 pass / 3 fail). An abort-signal timing failure and two server failures (queued-run completion timeout and Skill draft assertion) remain unattributed. None of their source files is changed. The seventh failure is the research-Python check, which could not clone its external evaluator because the configured proxy was unreachable.

Earlier candidate `cf93212f` (before replacing dynamic regression registration with static declarations):

- ST native smoke passes; standalone SDK contract suite: 66 executed, 65 passed, 1 failed. The 100-concurrent-call case also fails on unchanged baseline with its 3-second timeout. This is not a green ST gate.
- E2E: 70 planned, 44 executed, 39 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped; subsequent backend startup was blocked. Logs include Swarm filesystem-lock release errors. No complete passing E2E run exists, and these earlier results are not claimed as final-candidate validation.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the relevant real-service API journeys on `1b34a9c5`: queued cancellation, blocked queue ordering, assertion-failure cleanup, and incremental Skill indexing. The full file ran through `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` against an isolated instance; cleanup fault injection used a temporary test copy. The repository browser E2E gate remains FAIL/BLOCKED as described above. Follow-up is to resolve or attribute the remaining gate failures before closing #251.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: reliable cancellation-test assertions and worker cleanup; no product behavior change.
Compatibility and migration: none.

## Current integration status

The conflict reported at creation is resolved in `674fd641`, a merge of upstream main `9ff02721` into this branch. Two upstream commits met here. `345bb1c8` made the shared model gateway reject a stream that never reports a completion event (`Model stream ended without a completion event`), and `3d5cb622` answered that by giving every scripted gateway fixture a closing `finish_reason` event. That landed in the same `startBlockingPermissionGateway` this branch rewrote, because `isSessionTurn` now drains the request body and the reply no longer sits inside `request.on("end", ...)`.

The merge keeps this branch's structure and carries the upstream event over, so the permission gateway still reports `tool_calls`. The background housekeeping reply in `isSessionTurn` gets a closing event of its own: those requests reach the gateway as well, so leaving them unterminated would fail the same way. `upstream/main` is now an ancestor of the branch, so GitHub no longer reports a conflict.

Revalidated on the merge commit through the in-process fixtures only: `node --import tsx --test src/run-cancel.test.ts` in `services/api` reports 11 executed, 11 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, and the package typecheck passes. The real-JiuwenSwarm evidence above still belongs to `1b34a9c5` and has not been rerun against `674fd641`.

pr:441.body:
Researchers can now inspect and retrieve structured scientific data from five built-in database connectors, then download selected files through governed artifact jobs. GEO uses actual provider file listings and bounded sample metadata queries; AlphaFold DB adds retrieval of existing predictions and confidence files. The change also strengthens ChEMBL measurement filtering, ClinVar submission preservation and experimental PDB provenance.

Refs #420. **Partial fix; keep #420 open.** This is a draft because broad verification is not green and provider failure-path coverage remains incomplete.

## Scope

- GEO: discover real matrix/SOFT/supplementary files, validate download selection, preserve study/sample/platform metadata, paginate sample annotations and avoid bulk-query timeouts. Correct accession request parameters and GEO directory buckets.
- ChEMBL: validate measurement constraints and preserve units, relations, target/molecule/assay identifiers and assay confidence. Advance pagination over scanned provider rows even when local confidence filtering returns an empty page.
- ClinVar: retrieve versioned VCV/RCV records and preserve individual SCV assertions and conflicting classifications, without inventing a consensus. Reject oversized XML explicitly.
- RCSB PDB: preserve experimental-method/revision evidence and include it with structure download candidates.
- AlphaFold DB: add existing-prediction lookup by UniProt accession and governed model/confidence downloads, with explicit predicted status and model version. This does not run prediction software.
- Reuse the existing Inspector for built-in sources, using the same broker/audit path; preserve AlphaFold selections across store reloads, refresh changed connector caches, register evidence graph tools and document all five sources in English and Chinese.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe` (GitHub history). Product-validation candidate: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`. PR head: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034`. The final commit only relocates the unchanged connector-persistence test to avoid an append-at-end conflict with current main; production code and other tests are identical to the product-validation candidate.
The requester explicitly waived baseline reproduction for this feature. The baseline capability/gap assessment was source inspection, not a baseline live-service result. The candidate journeys below used built production API/Runner entry points, the bundled stdio MCP server, isolated Session/data state and official live providers. Agent validation used the native executor and a deterministic local model stub; it does not certify JiuwenSwarm or real-model behavior.

| Acceptance area | Candidate evidence | Status / remaining limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five sources discoverable, enabled and callable | Production sources API, saved Session selections, five live Inspector calls; browser Inspector journey | PASS for representative paths; Agent tool execution exercised with AlphaFold, not every source |
| GEO metadata/files/verified matrix | GSE1000, sample annotations and actual directory listing; completed matrix download, SHA-256 and parsed 22,283 probe rows × 10 samples | PASS; identify expression profiling by array and avoid assuming raw counts |
| ChEMBL constrained measurements/pagination | CHEMBL203 activity query, two distinct provider pages, units/relations/assay metadata/confidence retained | PASS for representative query |
| ClinVar individual assertions/conflicts | Versioned VCV000014206 live lookup with distinct SCV submissions; structured XML/conflict fixtures | PASS for selected live record and fixture contracts; not an exhaustive clinical interpretation |
| Experimental structure and downstream reading | 1CRN completed download and checksum, parsed 327 atoms in chain A | PASS |
| Existing prediction/model/confidence | P69905 model CIF and confidence download, checksums, predicted marker/version, 142 pLDDT values | PASS |
| Evidence retained after analysis | Actual files read and analysis output persisted with source IDs/URLs/retrieval metadata | PASS in native product journey |
| Invalid/missing inputs and provider/download failures | Gateway/domain boundary tests, broker/artifact tests; invalid Inspector accession rejected and next turn usable | PARTIAL: full representative rate-limit/download-failure and all-backend coverage not established |
| Setup, supported operations and scientific limits | English/Chinese guides and reproducible examples; L1 documentation check | PASS |

## Validation

Previously executed local checks at the product-validation candidate are reported below; no unexecuted check is counted as passing. At the final PR head, the relocated persistence test was rerun (1 passed), L1 was rerun (4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped), and `git diff --check` passed. A three-way merge-tree check against upstream main `9191d552d649612a81ec5852638020bcc1f30b7e` completed without conflicts; the merge result has not been executed. The earlier broad and product journey results remain attributed to their original tested SHA.

SDK contract suite failed: 33 passed / 33 failed out of 66, with test-server startup reporting `self.server.started == False`. The exact failing `TransportTests::test_concurrent_results_remain_correlated` was rerun on both the pristine baseline and candidate with the same SDK interpreter and failed identically (1 failed each). This establishes that representative startup failure on the baseline; it does not independently attribute every SDK failure.

pr:460.body:
An embedded JiuwenSwarm instance named `sciencediscovery` can reuse a standalone instance's registry and configuration. This change gives the embedded runtime its own default namespace, so setup and lifecycle commands operate on the selected instance.

Refs #257. **Partial fix; keep #257 open.** Local isolation is verified; Docker persistence still needs a real container journey, and the complete local check suites are not green.

## Changes and compatibility

- Default local runtime: `$HOME/.sciencediscovery/jiuwenswarm`. Registry, named workspaces and logs use this root; the process `HOME` is unchanged. Absolute and repository-relative `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` overrides remain supported, independently of the SDK installation.
- Start the selected instance before reading its endpoints, so SDK port reallocation cannot leave startup using a sibling's old ports. Launch preinstalled Swarm from its runtime root even when the default installation directory is absent.
- Preserve Docker's persisted HOME namespace explicitly. Document the safe legacy opt-in, fresh isolated state and log paths in the deployment guide. No ambiguous standalone data is automatically moved, adopted or deleted.

pr:470.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Validation
Focused checks on `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928`:
- `node --test .ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`: 24 passed, 0 failed. After the TAP summary the process aborted with status 134. That abort is a host behavior and not a failed assertion.
- Static collection of `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs` reported no dynamic registration.

Earlier local layers were run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`, before the exemption was narrowed. They were not rerun on `3bde9d39`. This follow-up does not change product code.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4453, executed 4453, passed 4452, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure is `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.test.ts` (the scratch directory was already 86 bytes, so the fitting socket path could not be constructed). That case passed when rerun with a shorter temporary directory. The CLA file in that run had 19 cases.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5, skipped 0. All five failures are in `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts`. That file matches baseline `7ee6c1d0`. Pre-existing host `PATH`.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked): planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure is `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. The spec matches baseline `7ee6c1d0`. Pre-existing.

A later local `pnpm ci:ut` was reported as planned/executed/passed 4456/4456/4456 after the three allowlist cases were added. This pull request does not attach that run's logs, so the reproduced check on the current head is the 24-case file above.

## E2E user journeys
FAIL for one pre-existing layout assertion on `92b8022`. The other mocked journeys in that run passed. The suite was not rerun on `3bde9d39`. This change does not alter product UI or product behavior. Real-model journeys were not run.

Tested SHA for that run: `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`. Browser journeys, mocked model, isolated local stack. Scenario: open the model registry in the empty state and use the connect control as the only create entry. Expected: that control is narrower than 580px. Actual: 601.23px. Counts: planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0.

## Release
Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. Only `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` can merge when `license/cla` is present and not success. Other bots and human authors stay blocked in that case. A CLA check that never appears does not block anyone.

Compatibility and migration: none. `license/cla` stays off the required status checks on purpose. This workflow change needs a human review; merge-when-ready is not enabled.

`scripts/check-architecture.mjs` 在 Windows 环境下会因为 `path.join()` 产生反斜杠路径，而 `component-boundaries.mjs` 使用 `node:path` 的 `posix` 模块处理路径，导致在 Windows 上查找不到对应文件。

## 改动

将 `path.join(path, entry.name)` 替换为模板字符串，确保生成正斜杠路径。

```diff
- const sourceFiles = entries.filter(...).map((entry) => path.join(path, entry.name));
+ const sourceFiles = entries.filter(...).map((entry) => `${path}/${entry.name}`);
```

## 影响范围

- `scripts/check-architecture.mjs`
- `scripts/build-windows.md`（Windows 构建指南）

## 测试

- [x] Windows 本地验证 `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` 通过
- [ ] CI 通过

## 关联 Issue

- Fixes #476

pr:498.body:
Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and the scientific memory graph.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy with the imported conversation and evidence. New research preserves the original snapshot. The compact continuation action appears beside the composer notice; the copy-origin notice disappears after 10 seconds.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies; complete exports include broader history and trajectory details. File selections, export profiles, counts, and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- User messages have a copy action; the existing assistant copy action is retained. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply, including after restart and for branches of branches.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence and discloses unavailable history; it never replaces a missing historical file with a later version. Busy sessions are rejected, request retries are idempotent, and imported snapshots remain protected.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the local graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration.

## Validation

Tested commit: `4e198ebe9ea9161d826827af816df59a09d02fb1`, based on official `main` at `9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`. Exactly one feature commit; author and committer are `zhaochen39 <zhaojichenjc@126.com>`.

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Targeted feature regressions: 50 Node tests passed (21 package/API/import/branch cases and 29 UI-control/trajectory cases), plus 2 scientific-memory Python tests passed. These are targeted results, not a passing full UT layer.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: failed during Node collection with `NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED` after the collector's 120,000 ms timeout; no plan was produced and no tests executed. The same full-layer command on pristine official `main` failed at the same collection timeout.
- `pnpm ci:st`: 24 planned, 24 executed, 17 passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped. Pristine official `main` has the same counts and the same seven failed planned identities: five specialist-runtime/ACP cases, the Evolve Python-runtime download reaching the worker timeout, and the Swarm SDK contract command. Nested SDK results differ: the candidate reports 26 failed / 53 passed / 1 teardown error, while main reports 25 failed / 54 passed; both also report 20 passed subtests. The candidate has an additional timeout in `test_http_disconnect_propagates_cancellation_to_adapter`; this runtime validation difference remains unresolved. The SDK check completed normally before the local wait limit; it was not reported as a pass or skipped.
- No test assertions were weakened or cases skipped to obtain a passing result. Runtime failures and browser coverage gaps remain open; this PR stays Draft.

## E2E user journeys

**FAIL / incomplete coverage**, on the tested commit above, using the shipping JiuwenSwarm backend and local mocked models. `pnpm ci:e2e` reports 103 planned, 9 reported/executed, 7 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped; 94 identities were not run. One of the two reported failures is an interrupted case, not a completed assertion failure.

Command: `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 CI_RESULTS_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/results CI_RUNTIME_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/runtime pnpm ci:e2e`, after dependencies, full build, bubblewrap, and the pinned Chromium were prepared in an isolated detached worktree.

| Batch | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research, 20 planned | Healthy isolated stack, then research journeys | BLOCKED before browser execution: scientific memory did not become healthy within the startup script's 10-second wait. |
| Standard, 77 planned | Healthy gateway, valid serialized ordering, then UI journeys | Reporter raised `FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST`; the gateway also timed out during WebSocket opening handshake. Network guard passed, the first inline-card case failed, and the unhealthy run was manually interrupted: 1 passed / 1 failed / 1 interrupted / 74 not run. The tagged summary counts the interruption as FAIL. Supplemental Swarm `history` recorded FAIL; remaining supplemental checks were stopped. |
| Literature, 6 planned | Offline literature-source contracts complete through the local product stack | 6 executed, 6 passed. |

The changed user goals are importing and inspecting evidence, continuing a snapshot in a writable session, previewing/downloading workspace files, inspecting trajectory/export scopes, copying a user message, and branching from a reply with navigation back to its source. Expected outcomes are persistent inspectable evidence, original-name downloads, complete selected detail payloads, independent writable branches, and return to the source reply. These changed UI journeys remain **unverified by browser E2E** because of the blocked/interrupted batches. The targeted package/API tests are regression tests, not external-client API or local-stack journey certification; that additional journey coverage also remains open.

Baseline: the same full E2E entry point on pristine official main reports 101 planned, 0 reported/executed/passed/failed/skipped, with all identities unreported and the layer FAIL. Research and standard failed JiuwenSwarm AgentServer startup. Literature collided on a dynamically chosen Swarm port with the concurrent candidate startup; this is a test isolation limitation, not evidence of identical product failures. Dead baseline startup waits were manually terminated after logs established that their apps had exited. No assertions, retries, or case selectors were weakened to produce these results. No real/paid model journey was run.

## Scope and release

Local startup changes in `scripts/start-stack.sh`, `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts`, and `.env` are excluded. These files and the existing local stash are preserved.

Release category: `release:feature`.
Compatibility: legacy evidence packages remain importable; absent historical evidence is disclosed rather than invented. Keep this PR as a draft pending complete runtime validation and review.

## Summary

Add `apps/desktop`, a React/Vite workbench built from the v0.1 design. This is the layer every later desktop change builds on:

- **Boot gate** — token entry, health check, offline screen and the first-run wizard, which configures a provider, tests a model and writes the global default before the shell is reachable.
- **Session workspace** — one flat, recency-ordered session list; click-time session creation; rename and delete through the row menu; a transcript that keeps the run in flight after the persisted messages.
- **Stream handling** — `fetch`-based SSE with frame buffering and a replay cursor; the reducer folds deltas, snapshots, terminal status and failures into one run state.
- **Bilingual infrastructure** — `TEXT` is a proxy over the active dictionary, `zh.ts` is the source of truth for the English dictionary, and `<html lang>` is set before the first paint.
- **Test wiring** — `apps/desktop/tests` joins the shared tagged runner, and `tsconfig.json` at the repository root gives tsx the `react-jsx` transform the app uses, so component tests render under collection instead of falling back to the classic runtime.

The workspace panel, settings dialog, permissions, run folding, previews, the language selector and launch resume are deliberately not part of this change.

## Stack

Part **1 of 6**. Later PRs build on this branch. Since the intervening branches live in the fork, every PR in the stack targets `main` and is cumulative; review this one on its own, and read the later ones through their incremental compare links.

## Summary

Turns the transcript into a live run view and lets a finished run be read back:

- **Permissions** — a run that stops for approval renders a card with the pending request, so the decision is made in the conversation rather than in a side channel.
- **Tool cards** — each tool call shows its input, its result and its status; a result that is not in the run state is read from the tool's own substream the first time the card is opened, keeping progress frames and the final result as separate sections.
- **Run folding** — completed steps fold into a summary row, keeping a long run readable while every step stays one click away.
- **Replay** — a finished turn is reconstructed from the persisted run records (`foldRunRecords`, `replayRun`, `RunReplay`, `placeReplays`), so reopening a session shows the same steps, tool output and permission decisions.
- **Reducer and stream** — permission state, tool traces and replay cursors are folded into the existing run state.

## Summary

Resumes the most recent session when the app starts.

- `resumeSession` in `session-order.ts` returns the most recently updated session, or `undefined` when a session is already open, so the decision is testable on its own.
- `resumeOnBoot` carries the decision out against the first listing: it acts once, skips a failed read (which is not an empty workspace), and opens a resumed Session the same way a clicked one does. The bootstrap effect is only its caller.
- The resumed session's Project is adopted before it opens. The listing spans every Project, so without this the app could show one Project's conversation while filing the next 新增会话 or upload under another.

Daily research workers stopped before model calls when `ubuntu-latest` moved to Ubuntu 26.04 / CPython 3.14.4: NumPy 2.2.6 and SciPy 1.15.3 have no matching wheels, and the fallback SciPy build fails looking for OpenBLAS. Keep the new Ubuntu and Python, and install supported wheels instead.

Closes #514.

## Changes

- Share the seven benchmark dependency pins between real preparation and offline research regression checks. Update only NumPy to 2.3.5 and SciPy to 1.16.3; retain pandas 2.3.3 and the other existing direct versions.
- Default both benchmark entry points to Python 3.14, with a dedicated `SCIENCE_RESEARCH_PYTHON` override. The PR research check previously inherited the gateway's Python 3.12, which could hide this failure. Product service environments keep their existing interpreters and dependencies.
- Require wheels in both entry points so missing wheels fail during resolution instead of starting native builds.
- Add a Biomni preparation regression that resolves the installed Hub API, supplies local download fixtures, verifies the pinned files and rejects corruption.

[NumPy 2.3.5](https://pypi.org/project/numpy/2.3.5/#files), [SciPy 1.16.3](https://pypi.org/project/scipy/1.16.3/#files) and [pandas 2.3.3](https://pypi.org/project/pandas/2.3.3/#files) publish CPython 3.14 Linux AMD64/ARM64 wheels. These pins satisfy the fixed DRB revision's [dependency lower bounds](https://github.com/Ayanami0730/deep_research_bench/blob/852f4022d1f98fb707222e395405136e8f0e8d52/requirements.txt). The Biomni upstream environment files remain verified provenance inputs, not an installed evaluator environment. Benchmark revisions, scoring and real-case evidence assertions are unchanged.

Includes numerical clustering/association checks and the fixed upstream RACE/FACT pipeline with mocked model/fetch responses |

## GitHub CI

[PR run 40060251093](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40060251093) completed successfully for PR head `916c190b63635581df14ef43aa7938771a8189b3`, tested as GitHub's PR merge candidate `f823875ea77975e228b4009f2fdc813dddc82379`.

L1, Coverage and `merge-gate` also passed. The uploaded UT evidence confirms `research test Python: 3.14`, with Biomni 19/19 and DRB 16/16 passing. Real/distribution jobs are outside the PR profile and were not run.

## E2E user journeys

The research worker accounted for 20/20. This dependency-only change introduces no new product journey; the existing product assertions remain intact.

closed_recent.body:
## Problem

Daily real-research shards fail during dependency preparation on the current `ubuntu-latest` image (Ubuntu 26.04, CPython 3.14.4), before any model calls. `.ci/prepare-real-research.sh` creates a venv using the runner interpreter and installs `numpy==2.2.6` and `scipy==1.15.3`. These versions fall back to source builds; SciPy then fails with `ERROR: Dependency "OpenBLAS" not found (tried pkg-config and cmake)`.

The same main commit (`7ee6c1d0bcc8374062364d51b3f4dfdf87a1396d`) passed dependency preparation on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12.3 on October 20 and failed on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14.4 on October 21. The October 22 and 23 scheduled runs repeat this failure. Current main (`0b74e53b`) still has the same numerical dependency pins.

Evidence: [October 21 run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39666641312), [October 23 run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40014929958).

## Required behavior

Support the new Ubuntu image and Python 3.14 rather than downgrading the runner or interpreter. Update the benchmark dependency preparation to a compatible, reproducible dependency set and check its direct consumers.

## Acceptance criteria

- The benchmark numerical dependencies install successfully on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 without an accidental source-build requirement for the obsolete pins.
- DRB and Biomni benchmark preparation and evaluator imports remain compatible with the selected dependencies.
- Add focused validation that catches this compatibility failure without making model calls.
- Keep the real-case assertions and evidence requirements intact. Model gateway billing failures and previously fixed runner cleanup behavior are outside this change.

### Checklist

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Description

When a session is deleted, a confirmation dialog is shown that asks the user to type the session name and click the permanent-delete button. After entering the correct session name and clicking the permanent-delete button, the frontend reports a request error:

```
session not found
```

However, the session is in fact already deleted on the backend (it is gone from the session list after refreshing). In addition, the confirmation dialog does not close after the error is shown, so the UI is stuck on the dialog and the user has to dismiss it manually, and it is unclear whether the deletion actually succeeded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start ScienceDiscovery and open a project that contains at least one session.
2. Trigger the delete action on a session so that the delete confirmation dialog appears.
3. Type the exact name of the session to be deleted into the input of the dialog.
4. Click the permanent-delete button.

### Expected behavior

- The session is deleted without any error.
- The delete confirmation dialog closes automatically after the deletion succeeds.
- The session list refreshes and no longer shows the deleted session.

### Actual behavior

- A request error `session not found` is shown in the UI.
- The session is nevertheless deleted (it disappears from the list / after refreshing the page).
- The delete confirmation dialog stays open and is not dismissed.


### Detailed Environment Information Description

- OS: Windows (x86_64)
- Deployment: local source mode, running from the latest main branch source (not the prepackaged binary)
- Service started with `./ScienceDiscovery serve`, UI accessed at http://127.0.0.1:4310
- Browser: Chromium-based desktop browser

### Additional Information

- The session is gone after refreshing the page, so the deletion itself succeeds on the backend; the `session not found` error and the fact that the dialog stays open appear to be a frontend state/refresh issue after the delete request returns.
- Expected fix: treat the response as success (or refresh the session list) and always close the confirmation dialog once the delete request completes.

### Version Information

ScienceDiscovery: latest main branch (built and run from source)

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
Follow-up discovered during the repository-wide review of #295; related to #288 and #291. Suggested priority: **P2**.

A failed model connection can silently undo a successful settings change made by another tab or API client while the connection test is running. The wizard restores the entire global-settings snapshot captured before the attempt, including fields it did not change.

This is **pre-existing**, not a regression introduced by #295. The same browser/API reproduction failed on both the base commit `4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310` and PR revision `45366a904edc7c57e69d36ce79b944e75b382d45`. The rollback code remains unchanged in the latest PR revision `d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635`.

## Reproduction

Use an isolated instance, the real API/store, and a local model endpoint that returns an authentication failure. No real provider credentials are needed.

1. Start with no registered models and persist these global overrides through `PUT /api/settings`:
   ```json
   {
     "enabledConnectorIds": [],
     "semanticReviewEnabled": true,
     "thinkingEffort": "high"
   }
   ```
2. Open System settings → Models and connect a custom provider. Let the wizard successfully read global settings, create the provider, and register its first model. The backend automatically selects this first model as the global default.
3. While `POST /api/models/:id/test` is pending, use a second API client to read the current overrides and successfully write them back with only `thinkingEffort` changed to `"low"`. Preserve the current temporary `modelId` in this write.
4. Let the connection test return an authentication failure.
5. Read back `GET /api/settings`.

Observed interleaving, with the generated model ID abbreviated:

| Stage | Persisted overrides |
| --- | --- |
| Initial state / wizard snapshot | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |
| Successful concurrent write | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"low","modelId":"temporary-model"}` |
| Wizard rollback | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |

**Actual:** the concurrent `"low"` setting is silently replaced by the old `"high"` value.

**Expected:** undo only this attempt's default-model change when it is still owned by the attempt; preserve the other client's `"low"` setting and every other unrelated override.

The browser reproduction intercepts the model-test request only to schedule a second, successful write through the real settings API before allowing the failing model test to proceed. It uses the actual App, wizard, HTTP API, and store.

## Cause and implementation boundary

[`ModelConnectWizard.restoreSavedOverrides`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L360-L377) calls `replaceGlobalSettings(savedOverrides)` on failure. This replaces the whole settings object with a snapshot taken before provider creation and model testing.

The backend needs the attempt's automatic default cleared before it can delete the temporary model, but restoring unrelated fields is unnecessary. The same unconditional rollback also runs when existing models meant the attempt did not change the default.

The [documented settings boundary](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md#L220-L232) already provides a catalog-level settings mutex and revision-checked plugin writes. Classic PUT intentionally remains last-writer-wins. This issue concerns the wizard's stale whole-object compensation; it does not require changing all classic PUT semantics.

A frontend-only fresh GET followed by another whole-object PUT still leaves a read/write race. Use an atomic conditional undo or equivalent version/ownership check at the existing server-side settings boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed connection preserves unrelated global-setting changes committed while that connection is in progress, including explicit empty connector selections.
- [ ] Rollback changes `modelId` only if the current default still belongs to this attempt; a newer default chosen by another writer is not overwritten.
- [ ] If the attempt never changed the global default, cleanup does not restore the old global-settings snapshot.
- [ ] In the uncontended first-model failure case, the temporary automatic default is safely undone and only the attempt's provider/models are deleted; existing references remain protected.
- [ ] Add a deterministic integration regression test using real settings persistence and an interleaved second writer. Check persisted settings after rollback and reopening the store, rather than only asserting mock delete calls.
- [ ] Cover both an unrelated-field edit and a concurrent default-model change, while retaining #295's test that a failed initial settings read creates no provider/model.

This is separate from #291: here the wizard's initial settings read succeeds, and the loss occurs during later failure rollback after another writer has saved successfully.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Model connection rollback overwrites concurrent global settings changes

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
## Problem
The sandbox network consent card added in #381 (Fixes #324) offers **Allow once / Allow same type / Deny**. For a `sandbox_network` request the second button doesn't say what it covers. I checked on #381 head `fb2fe785`: choosing **Allow same type** for `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443` does **not** widen to other hosts. A later request for `api.crossref.org:443` in the same run still raised its own card, because the resource is a per-host/run digest. Users can still reasonably read "same type" as "all sandbox network access", which is broader than what is actually granted.

## Expected
For `sandbox_network` cards, the user can tell exactly what each button grants. Either:
- rename the button for this action (e.g. "Allow these hosts for this conversation"), with a short scope hint, or
- hide it, if repeat consent for the exact same host set isn't a useful flow.

## Context
- Refs #381, #324.
- The button label comes from the shared key `permissions.allowMatching`, which every permission type uses. The fix should be action-specific, not a global rename.
- Repro: Ask approval mode → model calls `request_sandbox_network` for host A → **Allow same type** → model requests host B in the same run → a new card appears for B.

## Verification cases
1. **Label reads its real scope**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; sandbox network `none`; the model calls `request_sandbox_network` with `hosts: ["eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443"]`.
   - Steps: Open the pending card in the conversation.
   - Expected: The card shows exactly one card for that host. The second button is either missing or its label names the host scope (not "Allow same type"). Allow once and Deny are unchanged.
2. **Grant never widens to another host (regression)**
   - Preconditions: As in 1.
   - Steps: Click the second button (whatever it is called) for `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443`. In the same run the model then requests `api.crossref.org:443`.
   - Expected: A **new** card appears for `api.crossref.org:443`. The second host is not auto-allowed, and there are 2 `sandbox_network` permission requests in total.
3. **Other permission types unaffected**
   - Preconditions: Ask approval mode; the model calls `run_shell`.
   - Steps: Open the "Run a shell script" card.
   - Expected: Its buttons keep the current labels (Allow once / Allow same type / Deny) and behaviour.
4. **Global settings untouched**
   - Steps: Run case 2. Compare `GET /api/sandbox-network-settings` before and after.
   - Expected: The settings are identical.
closed_recent.title: Permission card: "Allow same type" is unclear for one-shot sandbox network grants

closed_recent.author: sciencediscovery-bot[bot]
closed_recent.body:
## Correction (2026-10-22T04:2xZ)

This issue was first filed as an "intermittent CI load flake". **That was wrong.** The failure is deterministic and the root cause is a runner image change. The earlier hypothesis (concurrency/load) is withdrawn, and the "same test passes in the CI-test run" evidence was also invalid — `UT` was skipped in that run.

## What actually happens

GitHub rolled `ubuntu-latest` from **ubuntu-24.04** to **ubuntu-26.04** between 2026-10-21T10:15Z and 2026-10-22T02:22Z. The pruning path builds its "busy" set from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe`:

```
packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:106
busy=$(for process in /proc/[0-9]*; do readlink "$process/exe" 2>/dev/null || true; done)
```

On ubuntu-26.04 that link no longer reports the binary a live process is executing, so the pruning pass sees an **in-use binary as stale and deletes it**. This is product code, not only a test helper: on 26.04 the same logic would delete a binary that is currently running.

## Evidence

| when (UTC) | job | runner image | `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-21T10:16Z | `119165996742` (#467 merge group) | **ubuntu-24.04** | 2661 ms, all tests pass |
| 2026-10-22T03:31Z | `119621422198` (#468) | **ubuntu-26.04** | 3 `/bin/sh`, `/bin/dash`, `/bin/bash` cases fail |

- Runner version is `2.338.0` in both jobs; only the image changed.
- Failing run [39716847675](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39716847675), job `119621422198`, step `Run UT`: planned 4441 / executed 4441 / passed 4438 / **failed 3** / skipped 0.
- Failure artifact `ut/tagged/group-141/worker-1-events.jsonl`: actual has an extra `'b' x 64` — the busy binary was pruned. The other 4 tests in the file pass.
- `merge-gate` (job `119626303432`) only aggregates: `CI gate failed: ut: failure`.
- Every PR after the switch shows the same signature: #269 #316 #460 #463 #465 #466 #467 #468.

## Impact

`UT` is a required check, so **no PR can enter the merge queue** for reasons unrelated to its own diff — the pipeline is blocked repo-wide.

## Suggested fix

1. Short term (unblocks the queue): pin the UT job to `ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:194` uses `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`).
2. Correct fix: stop deriving "busy" from `readlink /proc/<pid>/exe` alone. Compare device+inode via `stat -L /proc/<pid>/exe` against the file being pruned (works when the link target is not readable), and log the observed `busy` set when a removal is skipped, so the next platform change is diagnosable from CI logs.
3. Add a regression test that fails if a running binary is pruned — the existing test is the right shape, but it needs to run on the platforms we actually support.
closed_recent.title: bug(executor): pruning treats live binaries as stale on ubuntu-26.04 runners (busy detection uses readlink /proc/<pid>/exe)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from [#276](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/276) (closed). Recovery `direct_code` when sandbox is unavailable on local (#361) and reachable remote (#363) is done. This Issue tracks **agent-first direct execution**: the Agent may choose direct execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox (or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable). The framework should **suggest** sandbox by default and keep the `direct_code` consent gate — not hard-require “sandbox already unavailable” before direct tools can be used.

## Background / decisions (from #276)

- Unreachable Runner / SSH repair: **out of scope** (user/network admin).
- Managed environment: **Agent decides**; ask the user when needed; **no** complex Settings for this.
- Architecture target recorded on #276: drop precondition `Runner reachable + sandbox unavailable` as the only path into `requirePrivilege({ action: "direct_code" })` → user allow → `run_direct_*`.

## Goal

Give the Agent policy control over sandbox vs direct; framework = suggestion + authorization, not a failure-only gate.

## Acceptance

1. Agent can initiate direct-execution consent while the sandbox is still available, when the user requested skip-sandbox or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable (prompt/tool guidance makes sandbox the default preference).
2. Hard gate removed/replaced: reachable Runner (or local) still required; unreachable → clear failure + admin guidance; **no** requirement that sandbox be unavailable to *request* `direct_code`.
3. `direct_code` stays separate from sandbox `code` Always Allow (no silent carry-over); consent remains per command + scope + Agent run; no auto-replay / silent execute from chat text alone.
4. Sandbox tools and direct tools are peers; sandbox-failure errors may *suggest* direct but must not be the only way direct appears.
5. Tests/journey cover: user-predeclared direct while sandbox still “ready”; recovery path when sandbox unavailable still works; unreachable runner still blocked without SSH-maintenance feature.
6. Docs/prompt/tool copy updated for “prefer sandbox; direct needs explicit user consent.”

## Non-goals

- SSH maintenance for unreachable hosts
- Complex Settings for managed-environment presets
- Closing product gaps already accepted as out of scope on #276

## Related

- Parent: #276
- Delivered recovery: #361, #363
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Agent-first direct execution (skip-sandbox by Agent + user consent)

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

原生主 Agent（`runtime-core` AgentLoop）支持一轮多个 `tool_calls`，默认可并行约 10 路（`SCIENCE_AGENT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS`）。

Codex / Claude / ACP **specialist-runtime** 则走结构化 `platformDecision`：schema 只有单个 `tool` 字段（`string | null`），文案与循环均为「Request ONE platform tool → 校验 → 执行一个 → 回灌 → 下一轮」。这不是全平台总契约，只是 specialist 路径约定。

体验后果：自由 brief（尤其 DSV 兼容端点）易报 `Codex returned an invalid platform decision`；任务被拆成多轮，延迟与首败噪音上升。

## 目标

放开 specialist 路径「一轮只能一个平台工具」的硬限制，使其更接近主 Agent 的多工具能力；同时保留权限总线（原生 shell/改文件仍应走平台工具，不得悄悄打开 `shell_tool` 绕过）。

## 建议方向（实现可选，验收看行为）

- Schema 支持一轮多个 tool 请求（数组或等价结构），执行循环按序或可并行（exclusive 工具同轮串行即可）。
- 非法/半合法输出：纠错重试或自动拆轮，减少 `invalid platform decision` 首败。
- 若需分档：可按 runtime kind / 兼容端点默认保守，官方端点更宽；**不要**仅暴露一个无说明的全局布尔就结束。

## 验收标准

- [ ] specialist decision 契约允许多 tool（文档 + schema + 执行循环一致）。
- [ ] 至少一条自动化测试：一轮 decision 含 ≥2 个合法平台工具时可完成执行（或明确的有序执行），且权限/审计仍走平台路径。
- [ ] 非法 JSON / 多意图胡写时有明确失败或纠错，不静默丢工具。
- [ ] 不恢复 Codex 原生 `shell_tool` / 未授权改文件作为捷径。
- [ ] 与 DSV 等兼容端点联调：自由 brief 的 `invalid platform decision` 首败率相对现状有可描述改进（测试或手测步骤写清）。

## 非目标

- 不改主 Agent 并行上限策略（已有）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 runtime 选择 / 加密配 key / Specialist CLI 卡片（见 #455）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/codex.ts` — `decisionSchema`（单 `tool`）
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/decisions.ts` — `platformDecisionSchema`
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts` / `tool-scheduler.ts` — 主 Agent 多 tool
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts` — `maxParallelToolCalls`

## 背景

Phase2/3 合入后，旧版 `normalizeSpecialistInput` 白名单重建会**静默丢掉** `runtime`（HTTP 仍 201，看起来像创建成功但没有 Codex）。当前源码已修复：`store` 会保留并校验 `runtime`，非法则 400（`SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`）。

日常 CI 已有 UT 覆盖（`services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` 的 create/update/reload 保留 `runtime`；`phase3.test.ts` 多 kind 保留 + 拒凭据字段）。但 **HTTP 层契约偏薄**：没有断言 `POST/PATCH /api/specialists` 响应里的 `runtime`，也没有断言非法字段 → 400。Journey 脚本能间接暴露问题，但默认不进可重复 CI。

## 目标

补上可进 CI 的 HTTP（或等价集成）用例，防止后续改动再次把 `runtime` 从 create/update 路径丢掉。

## 验收标准

- [ ] `POST /api/specialists` 带合法 `runtime: { kind: "codex" }`（及/或 `claude-code` / `acp`）→ **2xx**，且 **响应 body 含同等 `runtime.kind`**（及已声明的非密钥元数据）。
- [ ] `PATCH`（或 update）只改 `description` 等无关字段后，**`runtime` 仍保留**。
- [ ] 带未知凭据字段（如 `apiKey`）或非法 `kind` → **400**，错误可识别为 runtime 配置无效（与现有 `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID` 对齐）。
- [ ] 用例挂在默认可重复门禁（UT/集成，**非**仅手工 journey）；失败条件明确、可本地复现。
- [ ] 不把真实密钥写进测试；不依赖外部 DeepSeek/Codex 网络。

## 非目标

- 不解决「旧 dist / 缓存包缺 `specialist-runtime`」的运维错配提示（可另开）。
- 不在本 issue 做配置页 UI / 主 Agent 代配 / Specialist CLI 卡片（见姊妹产品 issue）。

## 参考

- `services/api/src/store.ts` — `normalizeSpecialistInput` → `normalizeSpecialistRuntime`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/config.ts` — `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`
- `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/runtime.test.ts` / `phase3.test.ts`
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts` — 该 code → 400

## What happened

On a session that is still open, the Tasks panel shows `Session not found`, and the same string appears as a request-error toast.

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` polls `getAgentActivity(sessionId)` every 2 seconds. On failure it sets the panel alert to the error message and leaves the previously loaded execution list in place. The screenshot matches that: the session heading is visible, the execution list is populated, and an alert says `Session not found`.

Failure pages from 2026-10-06:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288), DRB-59. Heading `DRB-59 autonomous research` was visible. The Tasks panel showed `Executions 32` and an alert `Session not found`. A second toast was the invalid `run_shell` arguments error. The needs-attention banner also said `Session not found`.
- Same run, DRB-62. Heading `DRB-62 autonomous research` was visible, with `Executions 20` and the same alert, plus the `interaction round execution failed` toast.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020), TC-E2E-01. Heading `BRCA1 team signoff` was visible, with 17 artifacts, `Executions 115`, and resume buttons for stopped subagents. The only request-error toast was `Session not found`.

Many API handlers return 404 `Session not found` when `store.getSession` misses. Which of those handlers the poll hit is not in the Actions log.

## Expected

While the session page is open and its execution list is shown, the activity poll does not report `Session not found` for that session. A 404 for a different id is attributed to that id.

## Evidence limits

This alert was on the failure screens above. The benchmark metrics for DRB-59 and DRB-62 say the main run status was `failed` for a different recorded request error. The team case was still `running` when its budget expired. This issue does not claim that the 404 is what stopped those runs.

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
`pnpm ci:ut` starts one JiuwenSwarm instance for the whole slice and then runs every API test file one at a time. Unit tests should start independently and run in parallel. Only a test that declares a real JiuwenSwarm instance should use one, and those tests should take that instance from a single queue.

## What happens now

`scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` installs the pinned JiuwenSwarm, starts one instance and one adapter, and exports `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` plus `SCIENCE_AGENT_ADAPTER_URL` to every process in the slice. One instance has one tool server, so a second adapter would take it from the first.

`createApiServer` reads that process environment. When the variables are set, starting the server syncs web settings to the shared adapter (up to five attempts, three seconds apart). The UT scheduler then marks every file under `services/api/` as one resource, so those files never overlap. The default worker count is 2, and the scheduler rejects a count above 4.

Of the 112 API test files, two wait on a real gateway turn (`services/api/src/server.test.ts` and `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`). Five more start the production server and reach the adapter only because the environment is process-wide (`dashboard.test.ts`, `mcp/source-api.test.ts`, `model-usage-api.test.ts`, `npu-selection-api.test.ts`, `ssh-host-api.test.ts`). The other 105 do not start that server. On one warm run the API lane took 519 seconds, which was the entire UT test wall clock, while the machine had 14 CPUs. GitHub Actions runs this job on a public `ubuntu-latest` runner.

Cases tagged `status:unreviewed` are already outside the plan. They stay there.

## Required behavior

- A unit test that does not declare a JiuwenSwarm instance starts on its own and may run at the same time as other such tests. It must not see `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` or the shared adapter URL, even if it boots `createApiServer`.
- A test that needs a real instance declares that on the test. The directory of the file is not a declaration.
- The UT layer owns one generic startup and one queue for that instance. Declaring tests run on it one at a time. The queue covers only the declaring test, not the other tests in the same file.
- Non-declaring tests use as many workers as a public GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner can sustain. Local `pnpm ci:ut` and the UT job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` use that same number. Do not take the default from the workstation CPU count. Public `ubuntu-latest` runners have 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM; confirm the current size and pin one shared default. If that width is killed for memory, lower the shared default and record why. The two environments must not diverge.
- Do not weaken an assertion, delete a test, or move a `status:unreviewed` case back into the plan to make the run green.

## Done when

- A scheduler test shows non-declaring work overlapping up to the shared worker count, and declaring work never overlapping, including across files.
- `pnpm ci:ut` passes at that worker count, and the GitHub Actions UT job runs the same entry point without a second worker override.
- The pull request names the worker count, lists the tests that declare an instance, and reports the UT numbers.
closed_recent.title: [Internal]: Run unit tests in parallel and queue only cases that declare a JiuwenSwarm instance

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Background

A mocked end-to-end turn that changes the shared tool catalog spends a long time before the model is called. Measured on 2026-10-20, commit `d245cec8d9df52e0b3a99dd5bb236507ec73746d`, journey J3 (prepare a named environment and run one calculation):

- The scripted turn is two beats: one `run_shell` (stub delay 500 ms) and one closing text. Those beats, two rejected model calls, approval, and the shell finished in about 4 seconds.
- After `POST /agent/runs` and before the first `POST /mcp`, about 20 seconds pass. The run carried 44 tools. The MCP HTTP handshake itself, once started, was 7 ms (`platform_mcp_transport_open` to `platform_mcp_connect_ready`).
- After MCP is connected and before the first `chat/completions`, about 16–18 seconds pass. No model HTTP and no `/llm/default` call happen in that window.

Across the three mocked shards that day, the pre-MCP gap appeared on 21 runs (standard 12, research 8, literature 1) and added up to about 264 seconds. The post-connect, pre-model gap on those same runs added up to about 236 seconds. Most runs do not pay this, because their tool catalog does not change. Re-check both gaps on current `origin/main` before changing code; do not treat the old timestamps as a new measurement.

## Change 1: register tool permissions once

`AgentRunner.ensure_shared_tools` calls `_apply_approvals`, which sends `permissions.tools.update` once per tool. `gateway.rpc` opens a new management WebSocket for every call. On the Swarm side each update rewrites `config.yaml` under the config lock. A new shared-server generation name (`sci` plus ten digits) makes every `(server, tool)` key look new, so none of the 44 updates are skipped. `mcp.connect` runs only after that loop, and its live probe is the first `POST /mcp`.

Required behavior:

- Persist the approval map for one generation in one write, and do not open one management WebSocket per tool.
- If the shared tool catalog is unchanged, keep the MCP server that is already connected. Do not disconnect, register, or connect again.
- Leave the MCP handshake and live probe as they are.
- Keep each tool's approval level (`allow` / `ask` / `deny`). Do not widen access.
- Do not drop an in-flight tool call. A bare `mcp.disconnect` is global; reuse must not disconnect a server that still serves a run.
- Keep retiring inactive generations so `config.yaml` does not grow without bound.

## Change 2: skip unchanged per-turn prepare

The 16–18 seconds are work inside JiuwenSwarm after the tool server is connected and before the first model request. They are not time spent writing logs.

`_update_runtime_config` runs on every user message entering the runner. It already times stages (`cwd_seed`, `rail_setters`, `tools_for_mode`, `session_tools`, `prompt_for_mode`, `memory_tools`, and the smaller switches between them) and, after they finish, logs one line when the total is at least 50 ms:

```text
[AgentServer] runtime config applied: session_id=... mode=... total_ms=... <stage breakdown>
```

The threshold override is `JIUWENSWARM_SLOW_STAGE_MS`. A new session also logs `[AgentServer] session adapter created` with `create_instance_ms` and `start_interaction_ms`. After runtime config, `sync_agent_observability` runs: unchanged config is a no-op; a config change restarts the trajectory runtime and joins writer threads.

Required behavior:

- On one slow mocked journey with a new project and session and a single shell beat, capture those existing Swarm log lines. Do not add a second logging system to measure this.
- If `total_ms` is the bulk of the gap, skip the dominant stage when cwd, tools, prompt, and memory tools are unchanged for that session. Still run it when any of those inputs change.
- If `total_ms` is only tens or hundreds of milliseconds, the gap is session-adapter creation or observability sync. Shrink that work under the same rule: unchanged inputs are not prepared again.
- Do not delete the stage log line.
- Do not change the turn's result: same tools, same prompt when inputs changed, same shell cwd when the workspace changed.

If the captured log shows the time is necessary work that cannot be skipped without changing results, stop and report the line. Do not delete that work to make the clock smaller.

Ship a JiuwenSwarm change through the mechanism this repository already uses to patch JiuwenSwarm. Do not open a pull request against the upstream JiuwenSwarm or agent-core repositories from this issue.

## Look only: other mocked end-to-end waste

Look for other mocked end-to-end time that is startup or repeated rejected work, not the scripted beats. Report the cause, a rough saving, and whether removing it would change what a test proves. Do not implement those extras in this pull request.

Out of scope unless the report shows it is the same bug:

- HTTP 400 responses from the model gateway (unsupported parameters, images, token ceiling, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls=false`). The gateway body already states the reason; the access log keeps only the status. There were 216 such responses across the three shards. They return immediately.
- J3's environment clone, about 17 seconds, which is a separate step.
- The reviewer quiet-window wait.
- Deleting long journeys, raising end-to-end workers, or changing `slowMo`.
- Unit-test scheduling (tracked separately).

## Non-goals

- Do not weaken assertions or rewrite a test to avoid a real failure.
- Do not use the local trial port 4310 or its data directory.
- A formal pull request, not a draft. Exactly one label: `release:performance`. The body includes `Fixes #<this issue>`.
- Push the branch only to the operator fork. Do not push it to the upstream repository or to the GitCode mirror.
closed_recent.title: [Performance]: Register run tools once and skip unchanged per-turn prepare

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #93](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/93) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Use the app full-screen on a 13–14" laptop, or in a side-by-side split (window width ≈ 900px, paper on one side, ScienceDiscovery on the other).

## What I saw instead

Instead of a collapsible drawer, the left sidebar (projects, sessions, search, system settings) turns into a full-width block occupying the top half of the viewport. The conversation is pushed to the very bottom and the composer is no longer in the middle of the first screen — you have to scroll to start typing (the composer bar is still visible at the bottom edge; it is not gone entirely).

*(A screenshot of the stacked layout at a ~900px viewport is available in the cross-tracked GitCode issue above.)*

## Why this is confusing

A new user opening the app in this viewport first looks for the input box, cannot find it in the visible area, and assumes the app has no input at all. It violates the common responsive-design rule that primary actions stay in the visible viewport.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

Below ~1024px width, collapse the sidebar into a drawer navigation by default so the central conversation area and composer always fit in the first screen.

## Reproduction

Set the browser window (or DevTools viewport) to ~900px wide and observe the sidebar vs. conversation/composer layout.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.8), Chrome, verified against `main` @ 9b3d2e48 (v0.2.0).
