closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Request

Integrate DeepSeek's official Search and Fetch APIs so ScienceDiscovery agents can search the web and retrieve page content from a specified URL through DeepSeek.

The providers listed in the current [Web tools documentation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/docs/zh/reference/web-tools.md) do not yet include DeepSeek.

## Expected support

- Add DeepSeek to the Web provider settings, with API key configuration and an enable/disable option.
- Integrate Search via `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search`, mapping titles, URLs, summaries, and other relevant results to the existing tool format for agents to use and cite.
- Integrate Fetch via `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch`, returning the page title and Markdown content.
- Reuse the existing Web permission, credential protection, caching, and audit mechanisms. Document how the integration works with both the default JiuwenSwarm backend and the product's own Web tools.
- Provide clear errors for missing credentials, authentication failures, insufficient balance, rate limits, timeouts, and fetch failures. Handle empty search results through the existing fallback logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- After DeepSeek is configured, an agent can complete the workflow: search the web → fetch a result page → answer using its content.
- No DeepSeek requests are made when it is disabled, and existing provider behavior is unchanged.
- Add tests for successful requests, empty results, and major error cases, along with configuration examples.

Reference: [DeepSeek's official Search and Fetch documentation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/search/).

closed_recent.body:
## What is wrong

On a large screen the artifact viewer is still a small card. It is the dialog opened from an artifact (`artifact-modal-panel` in `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css`):

- width `min(1080px, 100%)`
- only a max height, `calc(100vh - 56px)`, so a short file stays as short as its content

On a 1920px-wide window that width is about 56% of the viewport. On a 2560px window it is about 42%. Plots, tables, notebooks, and source previews then sit in a column that does not use the screen the user is looking at.

The same class is the shell for the evidence viewer and the node-detail viewer (`ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, `EvidenceModal.tsx`, `DetailModal.tsx`). They should grow with it. Confirmation dialogs and settings panels use other classes and stay small.

## What a reasonable size is

A decision dialog and a content viewer are different objects.

- Material’s dialog cap (560dp wide, 48dp from the screen edge) is for a question or a confirmation. Applying it here would make the viewer smaller.
- A content viewer should take most of the viewport and leave a visible margin, so the dimmed page and the click-outside close still read as a layer. A hard pixel cap still matters on a 4K display, or a paragraph becomes one very long line.
- WorkBuddy opens an artifact as a tab in the right-hand pane, and that pane can go fullscreen. This product’s right pane is 390px, which is too narrow to become the viewer. Growing the existing dialog is the change; do not move artifact viewing into that pane.
- This repo already treats specialized viewers as large windows: the CSV workspace is `min(1480px, 97vw)` by `min(920px, 95vh)` (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/styles.css`), and the molecule window is `min(1360px, 96vw)` by `min(880px, 93vh)`. The generic artifact dialog is the one that did not follow that pattern.

## Target

On a wide screen, size the artifact viewer like those content windows, one step larger:

- width `min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`
- height `min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`

That is 1600×960 when the window is large enough, and it shrinks with an 80px total margin when it is not. It does not go edge to edge. At `max-width: 900px` the existing rule already makes this panel full viewport; leave that rule alone.

Inside the window, prose stays readable. Markdown body copy keeps a measure of about 76ch. Tables, code, images, and plots use the window width. Do not widen a paragraph to 1600px.

The evidence title already ellipsizes at `min(560px, 60vw)`. That cap can stay. The comment above it still says the panel is about 1080px; update the comment if that block is touched.

## Out of scope

- Settings, creation, and deletion dialogs.
- The CSV workspace and the molecule window. They are already larger than 1080px.
- The 390px workspace panel.
- The conversation column width.

## Acceptance

- At a desktop width of about 1920px, the artifact viewer is 1600px wide and 960px tall, centered, with the page still visible around it.
- At a width between 900px and 1600px, the viewer is the viewport minus about 80px, not stuck at 1080px.
- At 900px and below, the viewer is still the full viewport, as it is today.
- A markdown artifact’s paragraphs do not run the full 1600px. A wide table or source preview does use the window.
- Evidence and node-detail viewers use the same size. A settings dialog does not.
- A render test, or a CSS assertion next to the existing dialog styles, locks the new width and height.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Make the artifact viewer use a large screen

## Summary

Follow-up from [#276](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/276) (closed). Recovery `direct_code` when sandbox is unavailable on local (#361) and reachable remote (#363) is done. This Issue tracks **agent-first direct execution**: the Agent may choose direct execution when the user asks to skip the sandbox (or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable). The framework should **suggest** sandbox by default and keep the `direct_code` consent gate — not hard-require "sandbox already unavailable" before direct tools can be used.

## Background / decisions (from #276)

- Unreachable Runner / SSH repair: **out of scope** (user/network admin).
- Managed environment: **Agent decides**; ask the user when needed; **no** complex Settings for this.
- Architecture target recorded on #276: drop precondition `Runner reachable + sandbox unavailable` as the only path into `requirePrivilege({ action: "direct_code" })` → user allow → `run_direct_*`.

## Goal

Give the Agent policy control over sandbox vs direct; framework = suggestion + authorization, not a failure-only gate.

## Acceptance

1. Agent can initiate direct-execution consent while the sandbox is still available, when the user requested skip-sandbox or the Agent judges sandbox unsuitable (prompt/tool guidance makes sandbox the default preference).
2. Hard gate removed/replaced: reachable Runner (or local) still required; unreachable → clear failure + admin guidance; **no** requirement that sandbox be unavailable to *request* `direct_code`.
3. `direct_code` stays separate from sandbox `code` Always Allow (no silent carry-over); consent remains per command + scope + Agent run; no auto-replay / silent execute from chat text alone.
4. Sandbox tools and direct tools are peers; sandbox-failure errors may *suggest* direct but must not be the only way direct appears.
5. Tests/journey cover: user-predeclared direct while sandbox still "ready"; recovery path when sandbox unavailable still works; unreachable runner still blocked without SSH-maintenance feature.
6. Docs/prompt/tool copy updated for "prefer sandbox; direct needs explicit user consent."

## Non-goals

- SSH maintenance for unreachable hosts
- Complex Settings for managed-environment presets
- Closing product gaps already accepted as out of scope on #276

## Related

- Parent: #276
- Delivered recovery: #361, #363
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Agent-first direct execution (skip-sandbox by Agent + user consent)

closed_recent.author: ink999107
closed_recent.body:
## Environment

- Release package `sciencediscovery` **0.3.0-beta** (x86_64), started with `ScienceDiscovery serve`, Linux

## Symptom

Soon after startup the right-side task panel in the web UI shows `invalid internal token`, and the **Retry** button never recovers — the same error returns every time. Chat and agent runs work normally.

## What the shipped package does

1. The payload contains no evolve sidecar, and the launcher neither starts one nor passes `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` / `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to the API (confirmed in the running API process' environment). Memory-graph gets the opposite treatment — the launcher seeds it with a per-run random token (`services/launcher/src/memory-graph.ts:27`).
2. With both variables unset the API falls back to `http://127.0.0.1:4313` with the constant token `sciencediscovery-evolve-local` (`services/api/src/bootstrap/config.ts:253-256`).
3. Whatever process happens to hold `127.0.0.1:4313` therefore receives the API's evolve traffic. In my case that port was held by another process running an evolve sidecar configured with its own token, so the calls came back `401 {"detail":"invalid internal token"}` — and the frontend relayed that raw `detail` string into the task panel, where Retry just re-issues the same call.

I verified the error did not come from my own stack's memory-graph: the launcher-generated token matches the API's on both sides, and its access log shows zero 401s. The string is in fact the loopback-auth rejection detail shared by both sidecars (`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/auth.py:40`, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/auth.py:40`) — which is why it reaches users with no hint of which service or token failed.

## Why the fallback itself is the problem

- The API ends up calling an arbitrary process that happens to bind a fixed port, authenticating with a token guessable from the public source. A sidecar that rejects it produces the unrecoverable raw error above; a process that accepts it (or runs an evolve sidecar with the token unset — auth is permissive then) would be silently used by this installation.
- Run specifications sent to the sidecar carry the LLM proxy URL and token (`llm`, `judge` fields in `services/api/src/evolution/sidecar.ts`), so whatever holds the port also receives those credentials.

## Suggestions

- Give evolve the same launcher treatment as memory-graph: start it from the payload with a per-run random token, or explicitly disable it / point the API at an operator-configured URL, so the constant fallback is never reached.
- When a sidecar call fails, report which sidecar failed instead of relaying the raw `detail` to the UI.
- Prefer per-installation fallback credentials over source constants, and avoid fixed default sidecar ports (related: #267).

Workaround I applied locally: launch with `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` pointing at an unused loopback port, so the API no longer calls whatever holds 4313.
closed_recent.title: Hardcoded evolve sidecar fallback (127.0.0.1:4313 + fixed token) surfaces raw "invalid internal token" in the UI

## Summary

Every new session defaults to **Ask for dangerous actions**, even inside a project where the user already set **Always allow** on prior sessions. There is no project- or global-level default, so demos and repeated analysis require toggling the composer control every time.

## Observed

ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0 local demos (Scenarios 1–3, 2026-10-15/16):

For trusted local sandboxes and scripted demos, re-confirming every session adds friction and invites accidental runs still on Ask (more interrupt cards) or forgetting to tighten back later.

## Expected

- Remember last choice per project, **or**
- Offer a project/global default (Ask / Always allow) that new sessions inherit, with a clear per-session override.

**Medium** usability — repeated friction, not a functional blocker.

Distinct from sandbox egress solicitation (#324).

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Allow an Agent, with explicit user authorization, to execute commands and scientific code directly on a local or remote machine when sandbox execution is unavailable. Keep the decision and recovery flow in the conversation, and preserve execution traces and artifact provenance.

This is a follow-up to #265 and PR #275, **not a requirement blocking their closure**. #275 addresses readiness, actionable failures and Agent-controlled waiting; it deliberately does not implement unsandboxed execution.

## Problem

A connected Runner may be unable to create the sandbox because of missing dependencies or namespace restrictions. Today the user can repair the environment, switch Runner, or cancel, but cannot explicitly authorize direct execution on an otherwise usable machine. This blocks both environment maintenance and scientific computation in restricted environments.

A generic permission to run sandboxed code is not consent to expose the host's files, processes, network and credentials. Direct execution must therefore be an explicit, governed execution path, never a silent retry after sandbox failure.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Conversation-first consent.** When blocked, the Agent may propose direct execution, explaining the target machine, execution identity, command/purpose, working directory and loss of sandbox isolation. The user can authorize or decline without first visiting Settings. Do not introduce a mandatory extra global toggle merely for this interaction.
2. **Explicit authorization scope.** Extend the existing permission framework with an execution-mode/target scope. Support a clearly bounded one-operation authorization first; discuss optional reusable grants, expiry and revocation. Existing sandbox-oriented Always Allow settings must not silently authorize host execution. Child Agents may only inherit explicitly granted scope.
3. **Local and remote execution.** Reuse the current task/executor flow and select the direct backend at the execution boundary. Operate only with the configured OS account's privileges; do not implicitly elevate to root or change host security policy. A Runner's direct HTTP connection is not the same as unsandboxed execution.
4. **Actual reachability and recovery.** Probe the selected target's direct-execution capability separately from sandbox readiness. If the remote Runner is unreachable, remote maintenance requires an independently configured and authorized connection such as SSH; do not assume one exists. Initially, a reachable Runner's direct backend may be delivered separately from this maintenance transport.
5. **Keep lifecycle and audit guarantees.** Retain progress/output, timeout, cancellation and artifact handling. Record target, execution mode, user/account, authorization reference, command, timestamps and outcome with the run/agent/tool-call identity. Explain that unsandboxed host-side effects cannot all be confined to the workspace or rolled back; existing workspace artifact tracking is not comprehensive host auditing.
6. **No duplicate or implicit replay.** Returning a decision to the Agent must not automatically replay the blocked command. The Agent confirms the target/workspace and submits a new authorized execution. If dispatch outcome is unknown, reconcile it rather than blindly retrying side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With sandbox unavailable but target reachable, an explicitly approved harmless shell/Python operation can execute locally and on a configured remote target.
- [ ] Without direct-execution consent, execution remains blocked; refusal/cancellation produces no host command or silent fallback.
- [ ] Authorization cannot leak across targets, execution identities or child Agents; reusable grants have defined expiry/revocation semantics.
- [ ] Progress, cancellation, timeout and final errors remain visible in the conversation; the execution mode and authorization are auditable alongside resulting workspace artifacts.
- [ ] Tests cover sandbox failure, consent/deny, scope changes, remote disconnect, uncertain execution outcome and cancellation without duplicate side effects.

## Design questions

Define the minimum authorization scope/lifetime, whether direct execution is also available by explicit request before sandbox failure, and the first-version boundary for SSH maintenance. Any unavailable resource/network isolation or process-tree cancellation guarantees must be documented rather than presented as equivalent to sandbox execution.

Out of scope: silently disabling isolation, bypassing OS/platform restrictions, provisioning credentials, or automatically granting administrative privileges.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Authorize direct execution on local and remote machines when sandbox execution is unavailable

closed_recent.body:
## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session **timeline is too engineering-oriented**. Parallel tool cards, subagent workspace paths, and token/turn counters dominate the main pane, so a researcher cannot quickly see *what is happening for the research task*. Progress that does exist is buried (e.g. a sidebar tooltip like `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`) while the main area stays on a large **INPUT** dump.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, ~7 min raw screen recording):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards filled the timeline with long specialist prompts (INPUT), UUIDs / `subagents/…` paths, model name, turn counts, and token usage.
- Primary status was often just `Running` / `Tool is running…`.
- The more human-readable status (`PubMed search … · running`) appeared mainly as a **sidebar hover tooltip**, not as the main-pane headline.
- Researchers scanning the UI struggled to answer: which searcher is doing what, what failed, how many papers so far, when synthesis starts.

## Why this is a serious usability problem
This is a research workbench UX issue, not mere polish:

1. Cognitive load: engineering telemetry (paths, tokens, raw INPUT) competes with the research narrative.
2. Progress opacity: meaningful status is secondary (tooltip / deep in cards) while the main column looks like a developer console.
3. Trust: when retrieval degrades (no MCP tools, sandbox/network failures), the timeline does not make the failure mode obvious at a glance.

Related but distinct from #327 (no incremental progress at all). Here the problem is **information hierarchy / audience**: even when something is updating, the wrong details are foregrounded.

## Expected behavior
For literature / research sessions (and ideally by default for non-debug users):

1. Timeline cards should lead with a **human-readable phase** (e.g. “Searching PubMed for clinical CRISPR/SCD papers”, “Source unavailable”, “Synthesizing 5 papers”).
2. Keep subagent paths, full INPUT blobs, token/turn stats behind an expand/debug control — not the default above-the-fold view.
3. Surface parallel branches as short labeled lanes (clinical vs mechanism) rather than two giant opaque tool cards.
4. Put the same status that today only appears in the sidebar tooltip into the main timeline card header.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Default “Researcher” timeline vs optional “Developer / debug” density.
- Collapse tool INPUT by default; show a one-line summary + live status.
- Promote connector/search failures into the card status line as soon as they happen.

## Priority
**High among usability issues** for research users (serious scanability / trust problem), though not a functional crash.

## Related
- #327 — long runs only show `Tool is running…` (progress missing)
- #325 — connectors enabled but MCP tools omitted (functional bug that makes the opaque timeline worse)
- #324 — sandbox egress should ask for permission
closed_recent.title: Usability: session timeline is too engineering-heavy for researchers (tool cards, subagent paths, tokens)

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
Cancelling or disconnecting a sandboxed execution can leave that execution running until the script exits, when the machine is under CPU pressure. The caller already sees an abort error.

## Expected

After the client disconnects or the run is cancelled, the Runner kills the sandbox process group promptly. The execution leaves `activeExecutions` in a short time that does not grow with the payload.

## Actual

On an idle machine, aborting `time.sleep(30)` or `time.sleep(60)` cleared `activeExecutions` in about 75 ms. With the Runner and busy loops pinned to the same core, the same abort often took about 30250 ms for a 30-second sleep and about 60238 ms for a 60-second sleep. One 60-second case was still running after 120 seconds. The sandbox had not been killed; it ran to completion, and only then dropped out of `activeExecutions`.

`services/runner/src/executor.ts` registers the abort listener after `spawnSandboxProcess` resolves. `killSandboxProcess` then sends `SIGKILL` to the process group, which is the right signal once it runs. The kill does not run until the event loop observes the abort. A starved loop still lets the payload finish. The same path is what the product uses when a person cancels a long run in the interface.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/71
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Cancelling a run under CPU pressure can leave the sandbox running until the script exits

closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Complete model API compatibility across ScienceDiscovery by strengthening protocol tests, reusing the existing model adapters throughout the framework, and checking endpoint compatibility during configuration. This is an extension of existing support, not a new parallel model-client implementation.

## Current situation and problem

The main Agent model client already implements OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. Swarm communicates with an internal Chat Completions gateway, which adapts requests to the configured upstream protocol. However, auxiliary paths such as Evolve, session naming and paper-related model calls still contain direct Chat Completions requests; inventory and verify their current behavior before changing them.

An endpoint or model name does not uniquely identify a protocol. Aggregators can expose several protocols, and apparent compatibility can conceal lost tool-call, stop-reason or reasoning state. Missing/malformed usage is a separate accounting problem and must not fail an otherwise successful task or prevent benchmark scoring. Existing usage work, including PR #304, should be reused rather than duplicated.

## Proposed scope

### 1. Strengthen UT/ST/Mock E2E coverage

Use deterministic local provider fixtures for all three supported protocol families. Cover request/history/system/tool translation; streaming text and fragmented tool arguments; tool IDs, parallel calls and result round-trips; required protocol-specific reasoning/signature state; completion versus truncation; cancellation, errors and malformed responses. Cover valid, missing and malformed usage separately, preserving unknown values rather than inventing zero usage or exact costs.

Include end-to-end mocked journeys through the Swarm gateway and affected auxiliary callers. These tests require no real model tokens. Newly added production code should in principle have 100% combined UT/ST coverage; document exact uncovered paths, reasons, risks and alternative verification. Passing Mock E2E is not UT/ST coverage proof.

### 2. Reuse existing adapters across framework callers

Inventory direct model HTTP calls, then route the in-scope Agent and auxiliary calls through the existing protocol-aware model boundary. Start with Evolve, session naming and paper-related calls, verifying actual capability and integration needs rather than blindly replacing URLs. Keep internal Chat Completions compatibility where components require it, with explicit upstream adaptation. Reuse Swarm/agent-core clients where applicable; avoid another provider router or duplicated protocol implementation.

Preserve system instructions, tool semantics, termination/truncation and error causes. Where a function genuinely cannot support a configured capability, surface a precise limitation; do not silently discard tools/parameters, change models or degrade to text-only execution.

### 3. Add configuration-time compatibility checks

For the supplied endpoint/model/credentials, expose an explicit compatibility-check action and detect which of the supported protocols work. Check actual response structure, not merely HTTP 200. Return per-protocol outcomes and independently report basic response, streaming, tool-call/result round-trip and usage availability. An endpoint may support multiple protocols; retain user selection/manual override and persist the chosen protocol rather than guessing each turn.

Use minimal bounded synthetic requests, timeouts and output limits; disclose that checks may consume paid tokens and obtain explicit user initiation/consent before requests. Separate confirmed incompatibility from authentication/authorization, rate limits, network failures and inconclusive responses. Nonstandard proxy prefixes and provider-specific headers must follow existing explicit configuration rather than guessed hostname/model rules. Recheck upon relevant endpoint/model/protocol configuration changes without silently starting chargeable probes.

## Acceptance criteria and boundaries

- Main Agent/Swarm and inventoried in-scope auxiliary callers use a shared, tested protocol adaptation path for Chat Completions, Responses and Messages; existing default configurations remain functional.
- Deterministic UT/ST/Mock journeys verify full tool-call round-trips, streaming, truncation and original error propagation, including auxiliary callers; no new paid real-LLM PR gate.
- Configuration checks show supported protocols and capability/unknown/error details; users can explicitly choose or override a result. No silent runtime protocol switching or fallback that could replay requests or corrupt history.
- Missing usage does not block Agent progress, success assertions or scoring. Usage unavailability remains visible for accounting.
- Probes, fixtures and logs redact credentials and do not send research task content; no secrets in URLs, public artifacts or browser persistence outside existing credential policy.
- Document supported protocols, configuration checks, costs, limitations and troubleshooting. Protocol compatibility does not certify the upstream model's identity, quality or routing, and cannot fix arbitrary supplier-side corruption.
- Gemini-native and Bedrock-native protocols are outside this initial scope. Automated probing does not guarantee compatibility with every nonconforming provider.
closed_recent.title: Feature: complete model API protocol compatibility and add configuration-time checks

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary
When a literature / research task needs outbound network (PubMed, arXiv, skill scripts, etc.) and the sandbox blocks egress, the agent should **ask the user for network permission** (or guide them to grant Sandbox network allowlist access) rather than proceeding blocked and falling back without a clear permission request.

## Observed behavior
On a literature-research run (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0):

- Global `/api/sandbox-network-settings` was `mode: "none"` with empty `allowedDomains`.
- Skill scripts and direct HTTP inside the sandbox failed with DNS / network denial (`Temporary failure in name resolution` to NCBI / arXiv hosts).
- The run continued without a user-facing “please grant sandbox egress for these domains” step; retrieval degraded to `web_search` only.

## Why this is a usability problem
Users who enable PubMed/arXiv connectors or kick off a literature task reasonably expect the product to either:

1. already have the needed egress, or  
2. **prompt them once** to allow the required hosts / switch Sandbox network mode,

not silently hit fail-closed sandbox policy and produce a weaker report.

## Expected behavior
When the agent (or a skill/subagent) hits a sandbox egress block that is required for the current task:

1. Surface a clear permission / settings request to the user naming the needed domains (or Sandbox network mode change).
2. Pause or offer a retry path after the user grants access, instead of only recording failures in artifacts.
3. Prefer asking over silent degradation when the user’s prompt explicitly asked for PubMed/arXiv (or similar) retrieval.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Detect sandbox network denials that match known research hosts and open a UI affordance tied to **System configuration → Sandbox network** (domain-allowlist / mode).
- Or have the control plane preflight: if session has PubMed/arXiv enabled and sandbox mode is `none`, warn or solicit allowlist before the run starts.

## Environment / repro sketch
- Product: ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Settings: sandbox network `mode: none`
- Task: CRISPR / SCD literature research requesting PubMed and/or arXiv
- Outcome: DNS/network failures in sandbox; no user prompt to grant egress; fallback to web_search

## Related
See also the review auto-run usability gap (#323).
closed_recent.title: Usability: when sandbox egress blocks research, ask the user for network permission instead of silently failing

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
A parent run that launches several `task` subagents in one turn can fail while persisting the children's results, even though the children themselves finish.

## Expected

A completed subagent handoff is stored, and the parent run stays successful. Nested fields inside the child snapshot are not treated as content-addressed references.

## Actual

The parent run ends with `Agent run failed` and the UI reports `Invalid or cross-pool reference`. The children have already finished. A later user message can receive their completion notices, but that is a new run, not a resume of the failed one.

The `task` tool returns `details: { subagent, summary }` from `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts`. The native agent writes that object into a `ToolObservation` in `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts`. `ContentStore.putRecord` in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts` walks every nested object that has both `pool` and `digest`, and rejects a value that is not a complete object in the current pool. A real subagent snapshot can contain those shapes from another pool, or an incomplete reference, so the parent fails at the result boundary.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/87
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Parallel subagent results can fail the parent run with Invalid or cross-pool reference

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Enabling scientific connectors (`arxiv`, `pubmed`) on a Session persists `enabledConnectorIds`, and `/api/connectors` lists those sources, but the live agent tool set can still contain **no** `mcp__arxiv__*` / `mcp__pubmed__*` tools. Literature runs then fall back to `web_search` only. This breaks the documented contract that Session-enabled MCP sources become governed agent tools (control-plane MCP, outside the sandbox).

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** local instance.
2. Session with `enabledConnectorIds: ["arxiv","pubmed"]` (and typically `web`).
3. Confirm `/api/connectors` returns arXiv/PubMed manifests (`enabledByDefault: false`, `requestedCapabilities: ["mcp"]`, NCBI/arXiv `networkHosts`).
4. Run a literature workflow that activates `literature-searcher` (or ask the main agent to search PubMed/arXiv via MCP).
5. Observe run events / agent reports: **no** literature MCP tool calls; agent/subagent states that no literature-search MCP tool is present; only `web_search` (and failed `web_fetch`) are used.

Observed on session `27148ad0…`, run `dad3a25d…`.

## Expected

- If a connector id is in the Session’s effective `enabledConnectorIds` and the MCP source is **ready**, the corresponding tools (`mcp__<sourceId>__<toolId>`, e.g. `mcp__pubmed__search`, `mcp__arxiv__search`) must appear in the agent/subagent tool set (native: deferred directory + promotion; JiuwenSwarm: promoted at start per docs).
- If the underlying MCP server/catalog is **unavailable** or **degraded**, enabling the connector must not look “on with tools”; the run/UI/agent should surface catalog status (or refuse the enablement path) instead of silently omitting tools while checkboxes stay enabled.

## Actual

Session JSON and connector catalog UI/API show arXiv/PubMed enabled/listed, but `createMcpWorkspaceTools` injects nothing for those sources when `McpSourceCatalog.getStatus(...).availableTools` is empty. The agent proceeds with an empty MCP tool list and no hard error tied to the enabled connectors.

## Code pointers

Injection chain (also documented in `docs/zh/developer-docs/science-connectors.md` §3):

1. **Session enablement** → `services/api/src/runs/index.ts` passes `enabledSourceIds: settingsSnapshot.enabledConnectorIds` into `createMcpWorkspaceTools` (after `filterEnabledMcpSources` for plugin master/per-connector switches).
2. **Catalog gate** → `packages/artifact-manager/src/mcp-workspace-tools.ts` (`createMcpWorkspaceTools`): keeps only tools in `catalog.getStatus(sourceId).availableTools`. Empty `availableTools` ⇒ no tools for that source.
3. **Why `availableTools` can be empty** → `packages/data-source/src/catalog.ts` (`statusFor` / `getStatus`):
   - Catalog never refreshed → status `unavailable`, `availableTools: []`, error *"MCP catalog has not been refreshed"*.
   - MCP server `biomed` missing/disabled/errored → same empty list (`transport.mcpServerId: "biomed"` in `packages/mcp-sources/src/public-biomed.ts`).
   - Remote `listTools` missing or schema-incompatible with local `mcpToolName` (e.g. `pubmed_search`, `arxiv_search`) → `degraded` / tool omitted.
4. **Startup soft-fail** → `services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`: `mcpCatalog.refresh().catch(...)` only warns; API keeps running with an empty/failed catalog while `/api/connectors` still lists manifests from the registry (no status). Status lives on `/api/mcp/sources` instead.
5. **Deferred visibility** (native) → `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` marks MCP tools `deferred: true`. That only applies to tools that survived step 2; it does not explain a completely empty MCP set.

Related but separate: skill scripts under `skills/literature-searcher/scripts/*` need `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXTERNAL_URLS_PATH` / `config/external-urls.json` in the sandbox; that does **not** replace MCP injection. Skill docs say to use session MCP tools and not bundled scripts for literature search.

## Impact

- Users believe PubMed/arXiv are connected; retrieval silently degrades to web snippets.
- `literature-searcher` cannot fulfill its MCP-first contract.
- Hard to debug without checking `/api/mcp/sources` status vs Session checkboxes.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Treat “enabled but catalog unavailable/degraded” as a first-class Session/run signal (surface status next to connector toggles; emit a run warning or block start when every enabled literature source has zero `availableTools`).
- Ensure bundled `biomed` stdio MCP from `extensions_config.json` is healthy before advertising connectors as usable.
- Optionally include catalog status in `/api/connectors` so the UI cannot show “enabled” without readiness.

## Labels

bug, needs triage
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Session enabledConnectorIds (arxiv/pubmed) does not expose MCP tools to the agent

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
Revising a Markdown report can drop its Evidence chips, so the next review treats the same citations as unresolved and starts another revision loop.

## Expected

If a new version of a report still contains an `[evidenceN]` marker, and this run did not publish a replacement mapping, keep the version-scoped Evidence reference from the previous version. Do not keep a marker that the new text deleted. The first revised version should still open the Memory chips, and a quick evidence check should not report `CITATION_EVIDENCE_ALIAS_UNRESOLVED` for citations that did not change.

## Actual

After Reviewer returns `REVISE_AND_RETRY`, the lead edits the same report and declares a new artifact version without calling `declare_claim` again for the unchanged citations. The new text still shows `[evidenceN]`, but that version's `references` can be empty. The next quick check then flags every remaining marker.

`SessionStore` copies the base version's references only when `baseVersionId` is set and the caller does not pass its own `references` (`services/api/src/store.ts`). `declareWorkspaceArtifact` otherwise attaches only the references drained from this run's claim calls (`packages/provenance/src/recorder.ts`). A declaration that names the artifact and omits `base_version_id` therefore stores no references. When `base_version_id` is set, every previous reference is copied, including aliases the new text removed.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/108
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: A revised report can lose Evidence chips unless base_version_id is set

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) (`90db5b8e`), three tool calls from `deepseek-v4-flash` had arguments that `JSON.parse` rejected. None of them was truncated. #236 describes what each one did to its run. The upstream answered each of these requests with a complete response (the gateway logged its token usage), none of the three ended with `finish_reason: "length"`, and the server log has no 5xx or 429 on model calls during the journeys.

| Journey | Agent | Gateway request | Tool-call id | Tool |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DRB-64 | main run | `chatcmpl-2c3cbc55-d420-4a0e-ab0f-f460883c3061` | `call_f86a6970436f4559a83bd896` | `run_shell` |
| TC-E2E-01 | delivery-signoff subagent, 1st attempt | `chatcmpl-34b150cd-8aa4-478d-8c60-f6b6de204c62` | `call_00_7q1ei5oo6oy4v6d6mobdo6rw` | `run_shell` |
| TC-E2E-01 | delivery-signoff subagent, 2nd attempt | `chatcmpl-f980e9ac-a76a-422a-af31-11a515383f8f` | `call_00_f9fauxgae0v8n954s1db7ijo` | MCP `deliverable_check` |

From this evidence nobody can tell whether the model produced invalid JSON or our client lost part of the streamed arguments. The `[model-arguments]` line in the server log carries only the request id, tool name, tool-call id, usage and the truncation flag. The opt-in file `SCIENCE_AGENT_INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS_FILE` keeps the parser message and the assembled arguments (see "Invalid tool argument diagnostics" in `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`), but Nightly real E2E does not set it.

The pattern fits both explanations:

- Each failing call carried a long text in a string argument: the DRB-64 main agent had just said it would write the report, the first signoff attempt was writing `signoff.json`, and the second was passing the full 26,226-byte report as `report_text`. Long strings are where a model is most likely to mis-escape JSON. They are also where a stream has the most fragments.
- In the same TC-E2E-01 run, the first signoff attempt had passed the same 26,226-byte `report_text` to `deliverable_check` successfully about five minutes before the second attempt failed on it.
- The tool-call ids come in two formats (`call_<24 hex>` and `call_00_<id>`), so at least two upstream channels behind the same endpoint showed the symptom. That does not separate the explanations either: the client is the same for both.

## Stream-assembly paths that would leave no trace

In [`packages/model/src/client.ts`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts) at `90db5b8e` (the file is unchanged on main at `9189206d`):

- [L536-L540](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L536-L540): a `data:` payload that fails `JSON.parse` is skipped with `continue`. Nothing counts or logs it. If the skipped chunk was in the middle of a tool call, the call keeps its name, the response still ends normally, and the arguments have a gap.
- [L232-L249](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L232-L249) (`sseData`): every `data:` line is yielded as a complete payload. An event whose data spans several `data:` lines would be split, and the rule above would then skip the parts. A last line without a trailing newline is never yielded.
- [L587](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L587): a tool-call delta without `index` is stored under `fragments.size`, i.e. as a new call. A continuation fragment without `index` would be separated from its call, and the named call would keep only the other fragments.

Nothing shows that any of these happened. The problem is that if one did, today's evidence would look exactly like a model error.

## Expected

For every invalid-arguments event in CI, the evidence says which side broke the JSON:

- The parser message and the assembled arguments (or their head and tail when long) are kept in the diagnostic evidence artifact, not in the score artifact. A message such as `Bad control character in string literal` points to the model; a missing span points to assembly.
- The model client counts, per request, the SSE payloads it skipped as unparseable and the tool-call deltas that had no `index`, and the `[model-arguments]` line includes those counts. A failing request with zero skipped payloads and zero index-less deltas rules out the assembly paths above.

Related: #236 (an invalid call ends the run or subagent) and #233 (the E2E log does not print the run error).
closed_recent.title: bug: Malformed tool-call arguments cannot be traced to the model or the stream assembler

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

During the same DRB-59 run, a subagent's `declare_artifact` call was rejected before the run later stopped on invalid `run_shell` arguments.

Nightly: main [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`). The tool error was:

```text
[182301] execute invoke failed, error='[189002] format data with schema failed, error='1 validation error for DynamicModel
artifacts
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value=[{'path': 'navigation_cues_sources.json', 'name': 'navigation_cues_sources.json', 'description': '...'}], input_type=list]
```

`declare_artifact` in `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` accepts `path`, `paths`, `name`, `description`, `artifact_id`, and `base_version_id`. It does not accept an `artifacts` array. The model sent `artifacts: [{path, name, description}]` instead of `paths` (an array of path strings) or a single `path`. The schema rejects the extra field, and the tool result is that raw validation error.

The subagent still finished `completed`. The required report `deepresearchbench-59.md` was never declared. This tool error is not the request error that ended the run; that later error was invalid `run_shell` arguments.

## Expected

A `declare_artifact` call that puts the file list under `artifacts` gets a tool result that names the accepted fields (`path` or `paths`) and can be retried. The raw `extra_forbidden` dump is not the only feedback. The required final report is still declared when the files already exist in the workspace.

## Evidence limits

Only this one call was captured. It does not show that every `declare_artifact` batch fails. The description already tells the model to use `path` or `paths`.
closed_recent.title: bug: declare_artifact rejects an artifacts array with a raw schema error

closed_recent.author: Birfy
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

The tutorial section is a single page, and it stops right where a new user needs the most help. I would like the **tutorial series filled out** and a set of **short, runnable quick-start cases** with concrete inputs and described outcomes.

## Current state

- `docs/en/tutorial/` and `docs/zh/tutorial/` each contain exactly one file: `01-quick-start.md` (62 and 64 lines). The `01-` prefix promises a series; nothing follows it.
- Of those ~62 lines, sections 1–3 are environment prep, starting the stack, and pasting a model key — setup, not learning. The section that actually matters, "Run a first scientific task", is seven lines:

  > Create a Project and Session. Enter a focused scientific question, such as "Summarize the current research objective and propose the next analysis steps." To analyze local material, upload a CSV or PDF that you are authorized to use […] Review and approve the permission card […] Inspect tool calls and execution results in the message timeline.

  No dataset, no concrete prompt worth typing, no description of what the reader should end up looking at.
- "Next steps" links to deployment, configuration, runtime behavior, built-in tools, and architecture — all reference and explanation material. **There is no next tutorial to go to.**
- The only end-to-end walkthrough in the repo, `how-to/literature-research-case-guide.md` (212 lines), is filed under how-to and covers a single domain. Nothing in the tutorial points to it.
- **11 of the 18 skills shipped in `skills/` are not mentioned anywhere in `docs/`** (checked case-insensitively, including spaced forms): `assessment-screening`, `citation-reviewer`, `code-engineer`, `computation-reviewer`, `creative-material-design`, `evidence-extractor`, `insight-aggregator`, `literature-searcher`, `report-writer`, `result-evaluator`, `science-research-team`. A new user cannot discover that `literature-searcher` or `report-writer` exists, let alone how to drive them.

## Why this matters

A tutorial's job is to walk someone to their first success. Today the path ends at "enter a focused scientific question" — the reader is handed a blank box immediately after paying the setup cost. [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) reported this same class of problem from a real 0.2.0 trial: the user got through the interface but never reached the product's value.

The reference material is genuinely thorough (`rest-api`, `configuration`, `builtin-tools`, `runtime-behavior`). The missing piece is the learning path, not the specification.

## Proposal

### A. Finish the tutorial series

Numbered pages, each completable in ~15 minutes, each ending with something the reader can point at:

1. **`01-quick-start.md`** — keep, but replace §4 with one concrete first task: a named input, the exact prompt, and a description of the result.
2. **`02-analyze-a-dataset.md`** — upload a small CSV, ask a question, approve the first code-execution permission card, read the resulting chart or table, find it in the Artifact area.
3. **`03-literature-search-and-report.md`** — `literature-searcher` → `evidence-extractor` → `report-writer`, ending in a cited report. The existing 212-line case guide is good source material, trimmed to tutorial length.
4. **`04-use-and-write-skills.md`** — enable a bundled skill, then build one with `skill-creator`.
5. **`05-connect-a-tool.md`** — add an MCP connector and use it in a session. `how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md` covers the settings screen; the tutorial covers the round trip.
6. **`06-trace-a-result.md`** — approvals, provenance, and where a conclusion's evidence lives (pairs with `explanation/review-provenance.md`, and with ScienceMemory where enabled).

### B. Add quick-start case examples

Short, self-contained, copy-pasteable. Each case states: the input file, the prompt to type, what the reader should see, roughly how long it takes, and which skills/connectors it needs. Ideally shipped with a tiny sample dataset — the repository currently has no `examples/` or sample-data directory, so every walkthrough starts by asking the reader to supply their own file.

The current quick start rightly notes that outputs "are not fixed-output promises" since they depend on the model. Tutorials should therefore describe the **shape** of the expected result ("a chart appears in the Artifact panel; the timeline shows a code execution you approved") rather than promising exact text.

### C. Make the bundled skills discoverable

A `reference/skills.md`, or a tutorial appendix, listing all 18 skills in `skills/`: what each does, when to enable it, and which tutorial exercises it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/en/tutorial/` and `docs/zh/tutorial/` contain more than one page, and each page links to the next.
- [ ] Every tutorial states a concrete input, the prompt to type, and what the reader should see.
- [ ] At least one tutorial runs end to end on a sample file shipped in the repository.
- [ ] Every bundled skill is named in at least one document.
- [ ] `01-quick-start.md` ends by pointing at the next tutorial, not only at reference pages.
- [ ] English and Chinese versions land together.

## Open questions

- Which domain should the flagship case be: general CSV analysis, or the literature survey that already has a case guide?
- Can a small, license-clean sample dataset be committed for tutorial use?
- Should tutorials assume the prepackaged binary (the README's primary path) and mention source/Docker only in passing?
- Screenshots: worth the maintenance cost? `docs/images/` already holds 15 UI captures, so the precedent exists.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) covers building and publishing the docs site and completing the reference/explanation gaps; this issue is specifically the tutorial and case-example side.
closed_recent.title: [Docs]: Expand the tutorial series and add runnable quick-start cases

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

The Biomni real E2E currently waits for only the first foreground Run returned by `sendUserMessage`. That Run can become `completed` after it starts a managed background shell Execution. When the Execution finishes, the product delivers its result to the main Agent in a later automatic wake Run. The E2E may check final artifacts and clean up the Session before that wake Run finishes, reporting an incomplete delivery as a failure.

This was observed during local Biomni DA-13-3 and DA-14-1 investigations: the first Run's terminal status was not a reliable signal that the entire request had produced its final answer. The fix is limited to the test harness; the product's separate Run and Execution lifecycles are intentional.

## Expected

- Follow the initial Run, main-Agent background Executions, and subsequent automatic main-Agent wake Runs before asserting final delivery.
- Ignore unrelated subagent Executions and wakes when deciding whether the main request is complete.
- After all observed work is terminal, use a short quiet window to catch a wake Run created just after an Execution finishes.
- On budget expiry, distinguish timeout from a completed run with missing artifacts and cancel active Runs in the Session.
- Cover the settling rules with deterministic unit tests. Keep the existing manual Biomni entry point and quarantine unchanged.

Related: #233 concerns the missing error text in a delivery assertion; this issue concerns checking delivery before the complete Run chain finishes.
closed_recent.title: bug(e2e): Biomni delivery is checked before automatic wake Runs finish

closed_recent.author: Birfy
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

ScienceDiscovery ships a real command-line client — `ScienceDiscovery run` — that can drive a full agent task, stream JSONL, read from stdin, and be scripted. **The README never mentions it in either language.** A researcher who wants to batch a hundred runs from a job script has no way to learn the capability exists short of running `help`.

## What already exists

From `services/launcher/src/cli-options.ts` (the binary's own `help` output):

```text
Commands:
  serve                    Start the Web UI, control API and sandbox runner
  run [input] [options]    Run an agent task via a running serve (CLI client)
  extract --to <dir>       Unpack the embedded runtime payload without starting it
  version                  Print the release version and bundled runtime versions
  help                     Show this message
```

`run` takes 13 options: `--content`, `--stdin`, `--session`, `--project`, `--model`, `--skills`, `--connectors`, `--approval`, `--auto-approve`, `--review`, `--token`, `--output <jsonl|text>`, `--timeout`.

`services/launcher/src/run.ts` documents the behaviour that makes it scriptable:

- **text mode** (default on a TTY): the answer streams to stdout, status and progress to stderr — so `run "question" > answer.md` yields a clean file.
- **jsonl mode** (default when piped): every event is one JSON line on stdout, errors included, so a downstream `jq` never meets a non-JSON line.

This is a genuinely useful capability for the target audience: reproducible batch runs from a job script, a run per dataset, output piped straight into an analysis pipeline.

## The gap

1. **Neither README mentions it.** `README.md` and `README_zh.md` contain no occurrence of "CLI", "command line", "命令行", "headless", `jsonl`, or `ScienceDiscovery run`. Quick start shows only `./ScienceDiscovery serve`.

2. **The English deployment guide omits the command entirely.** The two guides disagree:

   | Guide | Commands listed |
   |---|---|
   | `docs/zh/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, **`run`**, `extract`, `version`, `help` |
   | `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` | `serve`, `extract`, `version`, `help` |

   The Chinese guide also carries a worked example and the mode/approval rules; the English guide has none of it. So today the CLI is documented **only in Chinese**.

3. There is no `reference/cli.md` in either language — raised separately in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).

## Proposal

Add a short **Command line** section to `README.md` and `README_zh.md`, after Quick start — four or five lines, not a manual:

````markdown
## Command line

Besides the Web UI, a running `serve` can be driven from the terminal:

```bash
./ScienceDiscovery serve &                      # start the stack
./ScienceDiscovery run "Summarize these results" > answer.md
cat prompt.txt | ./ScienceDiscovery run --stdin --auto-approve | jq .
```

`run` connects to the same control plane as the browser and reads the token
from the data directory, so no extra setup is needed when `run` and `serve`
share a `--data-dir`. On a TTY the answer goes to stdout and progress to
stderr; when piped it emits JSONL, and a non-interactive run must pass
`--auto-approve` because it cannot answer permission prompts.
See [CLI reference](docs/en/reference/cli.md) for every command and option.
````

And alongside it:

- Add `run` to the command list in `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` so the two languages match, porting the example and the text/jsonl and approval rules from the Chinese guide.
- If the README grows a feature table ([#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27)), give scripted/batch use a row of its own — it is a differentiator worth stating, not a footnote.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both READMEs introduce the CLI with at least one runnable example.
- [ ] The README states the TTY/pipe output-mode difference and the `--auto-approve` requirement for non-interactive runs, so a first scripted attempt does not fail unexplained.
- [ ] `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` lists `run` alongside `serve`, `extract`, `version`, and `help`.
- [ ] The English and Chinese command lists match.
- [ ] The README links to a CLI reference once one exists.

## Open questions

- Does the README keep a short teaser and delegate details to the deployment guide / CLI reference, or carry a slightly fuller example?
- Should the example use the binary (`./ScienceDiscovery run`) only, or also show the source-mode equivalent?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (a `reference/cli.md` and the docs site), [#27](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/27) (README rework).
closed_recent.title: [Docs]: Introduce the command-line interface in the README

closed_recent.author: Birfy
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

The README is the first and often only page a visitor reads, and right now it does not do the three jobs it should: **say clearly what this is and who it is for, summarize the core capabilities in a scannable form, and hand the reader a path into the tutorials.** I would like it reworked around those three.

## Current state

`README.md` and `README_zh.md` are 57 lines each: intro sentence → security warning → Project positioning → Features → Related documents → Requirements → Installation → Quick start → License.

Concrete problems:

1. **The pitch is one sentence, and the second thing a visitor reads is a disclaimer.** Line 3 carries the whole value proposition; lines 7–8 are a `[!WARNING]` block about loopback binding, bearer tokens, TLS termination, and sandbox boundaries. That warning is correct and should stay in the README — but placing it above everything else means a first-time reader meets the caveats before they have any idea what the product does.

2. **"Project positioning" does not describe positioning, and the two languages disagree.** The English section is an architecture paragraph ("A browser UI communicates with a Node control API. Each agent run is driven by a Python Gateway…"). The Chinese section at the same position is a **verbatim copy of the intro sentence at line 12**. So one language repeats itself and the other answers a different question entirely.

3. **The feature list is dense prose with no links and an unsourced number.** Four bullets, each a 2–3 line paragraph. None of them links to anything — not a doc, not a tutorial, not a screenshot. The claim "over 300 cross-domain Skills" appears **only in the two READMEs and nowhere else in the repository or docs**, while `skills/` ships 18. Whatever the 300 refers to, a reader cannot verify it or find out how to reach those skills.

4. **No visuals at all.** Both READMEs contain zero images (`grep -c '!\['` → 0), while `docs/images/` already holds 15 UI captures — `project.png`, `task.png`, `model.png`, `skill.png`, `connector.png`, `permission.png`, `memory.png`, `quotas.png`, `evidence1–4.jpg`, and more. A product whose pitch is "watch the whole research workflow and trace every deliverable" shows the reader nothing.

5. **Exactly one tutorial link, buried at line 51 of 57**, mid-paragraph, after a `curl` health check. Nothing in the Features section points at how to actually try any of those features.

6. **The Installation section is a stub.** In full: "Prepare a ScienceDiscovery executable for the host architecture. Binary packaging, source mode, and Docker procedures are documented in the deployment guide." It never says where to get an executable — which is precisely what [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) asked.

## Proposal

Restructure both READMEs to this order:

1. **Title + one-line pitch + badges.** One sentence a researcher recognizes themselves in. Keep the existing positioning sentence if it tests well; just make it the hero line, not a paragraph competing with three other paragraphs.
2. **One screenshot or short GIF** of a real session — timeline, a generated artifact, the provenance view. Reuse what is already in `docs/images/`.
3. **"What you can do with it" — a scannable feature table**, one row per capability, each row linking to the tutorial or how-to that exercises it. Sketch:

   | Capability | What it means | Try it |
   |---|---|---|
   | Literature and data connectors | One-click access to paper and data repositories | `how-to/configure-custom-mcp.md`, literature tutorial |
   | Sandboxed code execution | Agents write and run Python/R/shell in a fail-closed sandbox | dataset-analysis tutorial |
   | Task decomposition and skills | Complex tasks broken down and dispatched across skills | skills tutorial |
   | Full-chain traceability | Code, environment, logs, and evidence for every deliverable | `explanation/review-provenance.md`, tracing tutorial |

   The "Try it" column is the part that matters: every claim becomes something the reader can go do. The tutorial targets come from [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26); until those pages exist, the column points at the pages that do.
4. **Get started in three steps** — download, run, first task — with a real download location, then straight into the quick-start tutorial.
5. **Then** requirements, deployment paths, the security warning, contributing, and license. Keep the warning prominent and unsoftened, just below the getting-started path rather than above the pitch.

Also: either source the "300+ Skills" claim (link to wherever that library lives) or restate it in terms a reader can check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visitor can tell within the first screen what the product does, for whom, and what it costs them to try.
- [ ] Every feature claim links to a page that demonstrates or documents it.
- [ ] At least one screenshot or GIF of the product appears above the fold.
- [ ] The tutorial entry point is a prominent link, not a clause in a paragraph.
- [ ] "Installation" says where to obtain a binary.
- [ ] The security warning is still present and unsoftened.
- [ ] `README.md` and `README_zh.md` have the same structure and make the same claims; the Chinese "项目定位" section no longer duplicates the intro verbatim.
- [ ] The "300+ Skills" figure is sourced or restated.

## Open questions

- Is there a public download or release page the README can link to, or is distribution internal for now?
- Screenshot or animated GIF — and can one be captured from a build that is safe to publish (no tokens, no internal hostnames)?
- What does the "300+ Skills" number count?
- Should the README carry the feature table, or stay short and delegate to a docs landing page once [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) publishes one?

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (docs site + content completeness), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (tutorial series), [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) (onboarding experience), [#1](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1) (finding the download).
closed_recent.title: [Docs]: Rework the README — clear pitch, summarized core features, and links into the tutorials

closed_recent.author: Birfy
closed_recent.body:
## Summary

When a dependency is missing, `scripts/start-stack.sh` prints one sentence naming the requirement and exits. It never says how to satisfy it or where to read more, so the first thing a new user meets is a dead end.

## Current behaviour

`scripts/start-stack.sh` (lines 212–250):

```bash
require_command() { # <command> <failure message>
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null || { echo "$2" >&2; exit 1; }
}

require_command node   "Node.js 22.19+ is required."
require_command pnpm   "pnpm 11.1.2 is required."
require_command python3 "Python 3 is required for workspace analysis."
require_command uv     "uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments."
require_command curl   "curl is required for local service startup checks."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_BWRAP_PATH:-bwrap}" "bubblewrap is required for isolated Linux execution."
require_command "${SCIENCE_AGENT_SEATBELT_PATH:-/usr/bin/sandbox-exec}" "macOS sandbox-exec is required for isolated execution."
```

So on a fresh machine the entire output is:

```
pnpm 11.1.2 is required.
```

and the process exits 1.

One check already does better and is worth copying — the Node version gate reports what it found:

```
Node.js 22.19+ is required; found v20.11.0.
```

That is the right shape; it is just missing the "and here is how to fix it" half, and the other seven checks do not even report the found version.

## Why this matters

The target audience is researchers, not Node developers. "pnpm 11.1.2 is required" assumes the reader knows what pnpm is, that it is installed through corepack or npm, and that the version is pinned deliberately. `uv` and `bubblewrap` are worse — neither is something a scientist would have encountered, and `bwrap` is not even the name printed in the error, so searching for "bubblewrap" and searching for the binary give different results.

The information exists: `README.md` has a requirements table, and `docs/*/how-to/deployment.md` has per-platform install commands. The failure message just never points there. This is the same class of stumble reported in [#22](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/22) — the product is reachable but the path to it is not explained.

## Proposal

Extend `require_command` to take a remedy, and print three things on failure: what is missing, what was found (when anything was), and one concrete next step.

```
uv 0.9+ is required for the Python service environments; not found on PATH.
Install:  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
Details:  docs/en/how-to/deployment.md#local-mode-host-processes
```

Specifically:

- **node / pnpm** — name the version manager the project expects (corepack, `npm i -g pnpm@11.1.2`, or whatever is canonical here) rather than leaving the reader to pick.
- **uv** — the official install line, plus the note that it is only needed for source mode.
- **bubblewrap** — the package name per distro (`apt install bubblewrap`, `dnf install bubblewrap`) and the fact that the binary is `bwrap`, since the error names one and `command -v` looks for the other.
- **sandbox-exec** — say it ships with macOS, so "missing" almost always means a restricted parent sandbox rather than something to install; `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` already explains this, and the error should link to it.
- Report the found version wherever a version gate exists, as the Node check already does.
- Collect all failures before exiting instead of stopping at the first one, so a user on a bare machine learns everything they need in one run rather than in five.

Keep each message to two or three lines — this is not a place for a wall of text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every preflight failure names the missing dependency, what was found (if anything), and a concrete install step or doc link.
- [ ] The doc link resolves to a section that actually covers that dependency.
- [ ] The bubblewrap message reconciles the package name with the `bwrap` binary name.
- [ ] A machine missing several dependencies reports them all in one run.
- [ ] The messages stay short enough to read in a terminal.

## Open question

Should the install commands live in the script, or should the script print only a doc anchor and keep the platform-specific commands in the deployment guide? Inline commands are more immediately useful; a single doc anchor is easier to keep correct.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Dependency preflight failures should say how to fix them, not just what is missing

A JSON artifact, especially a large one, is still shown from a truncated preview, so the document looks incomplete.

## Expected

The artifact viewer shows the full JSON document, or it states the preview limit and offers the complete file. A large file should not look like part of the data is missing.

## Actual

In `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`, a JSON record array uses the table preview and other JSON uses `JsonSourcePreview`. Both paths carry a `truncated` flag. The raw fallback renders `source.slice(0, 100_000)`. A large artifact therefore cannot be read in full in the viewer. The original report was that this incompleteness showed up intermittently, and was most visible on large JSON files.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/69

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
## Description

When the Nightly workflow runs UT and ST with the `daily` profile, both test jobs produce raw coverage data, but the Coverage job does not receive the corresponding artifacts. As a result, coverage merging fails and the coverage summary is not updated.

Affected run:

- Nightly run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35919083156
- Commit: `9c5a5097336ab5342050dc07f9b14c3ccfce9cd0`
- Actual UT output: `.ci-results/daily-ut/tagged/coverage`
- Actual ST output: `.ci-results/daily-st/tagged/coverage`

The UT and ST jobs themselves completed successfully and wrote coverage data. The failure occurs while handing that data off to the Coverage job.

## Root cause

`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` includes the profile name in the output label for profiles other than `pr`:

```js
const label = dimensions.length
  ? 'query'
  : profileName === 'pr'
    ? slice
    : `${profileName}-${slice}`;
```

This produces the following paths:

- `pr + ut` → `.ci-results/ut/tagged/coverage`
- `daily + ut` → `.ci-results/daily-ut/tagged/coverage`
- `daily + st` → `.ci-results/daily-st/tagged/coverage`

However, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` still uses profile-independent upload paths:

```yaml
path: .ci-results/ut/tagged/coverage
```

and:

```yaml
path: .ci-results/st/tagged/coverage
```

When Nightly selects the `daily` profile, neither hard-coded path exists. `actions/upload-artifact` therefore reports that no files were found and does not create the `ut-coverage` or `st-coverage` artifact. The Coverage job cannot download those artifacts, merges zero Node.js and Python files, and fails.

This is not a dashboard input-path issue. The data is never uploaded as a workflow artifact, and a later job cannot access the previous job's local workspace directly.

## Regression timeline

- PR #148 introduced the `daily` profile and the `daily-ut` / `daily-st` output naming:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/148
- PR #150 changed Coverage to reuse data produced by the UT/ST jobs, but used hard-coded `ut` / `st` upload paths that do not account for non-`pr` profiles:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/150
- PR #158 enabled hidden-file uploads for the result artifacts, but did not update the coverage artifact paths:
  https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/158

The previous successful Nightly run was:

- https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35782010015

That run started before PR #150 was merged, so it did not use the current UT/ST coverage-artifact handoff. The `daily-ut` naming introduced by PR #148 is intentional; the regression is the profile-independent artifact path added by PR #150.

## Suggested fix

Avoid hard-coding the `ut` and `st` result directories in the workflow. Possible approaches include:

1. Compute the actual result directory from `${{ inputs.profile || 'pr' }}` and upload coverage from that directory.
2. Have the test runner expose the resolved coverage path as an explicit step output.
3. Use a constrained glob that covers `ut`, `daily-ut`, `st`, and `daily-st` without mixing data from unrelated profiles or slices.

An explicitly computed path is preferable because it avoids accidentally merging data from multiple profiles.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `pr` profile continues to upload and merge UT/ST coverage.
- Nightly with the `daily` profile uploads coverage from `daily-ut` and `daily-st`.
- The Coverage job downloads `ut-coverage` and `st-coverage` and generates non-empty Node.js and Python summaries.
- If UT or ST produces no coverage, the summary identifies the missing layer instead of reporting a misleading zero-file merge.
- The Release workflow continues to skip coverage generation and upload.
closed_recent.title: bug(ci): Nightly coverage artifacts are not uploaded for the daily profile

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## Problem

Pushing a version tag starts `.github/workflows/release.yml`. After the L5 gate passes, the `publish` job runs `gh release create` and the GitHub Release becomes public immediately. Nobody reviews the gate result, the generated notes, or the attached binaries before the release shows up on the Releases page.

## Desired flow

Keep the current order up to the gate: tag push, resolve the version, run the release gate. When the gate is green, create the GitHub Release as a **draft** (`gh release create --draft`). A person with write access reviews that draft and publishes it from the Releases page. That publish action is the human review. Do not add a GitHub Environment required-reviewer gate.

## Behavior to preserve

- The tag filter, version parsing, and the hyphen-means-prerelease rule stay. When the version contains a hyphen, pass `--prerelease` together with `--draft`. Publishing the draft later must leave that prerelease flag in place, so a prerelease still does not become Latest.
- A failed gate still creates no Release and uploads no assets. The git tag remains.
- If a release for that tag already exists, whether it is a draft or already published, keep today's path: `gh release upload --clobber` only. Do not publish a draft from the workflow, do not turn a published release back into a draft, and do not run `gh release edit --draft=false`.
- The publish job stays idempotent. A re-run after a failed upload must not be blocked by a draft the first attempt already created.
- Keep publishing the binaries the gate already smoke-tested. Do not rebuild them in the publish job. Keep the SHA256 check and the requirement that both architectures are present.
- Do not add required reviewers to the `nightly-ci-ds` environment. Merge-queue, nightly, and release real-E2E jobs share it for model credentials. Putting a reviewer on it would pause those jobs.
- `scripts/release-notes.mjs` already skips drafts when it chooses the previous release (`previousTagFrom` drops `isDraft`). Leave that unless a test shows this change breaks note generation. A draft must not become the comparison baseline for a later release.

## Docs that currently describe immediate publication

Update only the sentences that say a successful gate publishes a public, downloadable Release:

- The header comments in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a tag push "publishes" the release, and assets "become downloadable" once the called workflow is green).
- The L5 row in `.ci/README.md` ("Blocks Release/assets").
- The L5 row in `.agents/skills/ci/SKILL.md`, which says failure blocks Release/assets publication.

New meaning: the gate blocks creating the draft Release and its assets. The draft is not a public release until a person publishes it. The tag is still created before the workflow runs, and a failed gate still does not delete that tag.

## Out of scope

- Do not move, delete, or re-push existing tags, including `v0.3.0-rc1`.
- Do not re-run or edit a Release workflow run that has already started.
- The new behavior applies to tag pushes after this change is on the default branch.

## Acceptance

- `gh release create` in the publish job includes `--draft`.
- The already-exists branch only replaces assets with `gh release upload --clobber`.
- Prerelease detection is unchanged, and a hyphenated version is still created as a prerelease draft.
- The three docs above match this behavior.
- `nightly-ci-ds` has no new protection rules.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Create the GitHub Release as a draft after the release gate

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` is still locked below the fix for CVE-2026-104850, and this repository uses the affected OAuth client.

## Current pin

`services/api` depends on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `^1.30.0`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `1.30.0`. The advisory is fixed in 1.31.0 on the 1.x line, and in `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.2.0 on the 2.x line.

## What the advisory covers

From 1.12.0 until those fix versions, the SDK's OAuth client lets the MCP server it is talking to choose which authorization server receives stored credentials. Stored credentials are not bound to the authorization server they belong to. A malicious or compromised MCP server can name its own authorization server in protected-resource metadata. Without another user step, the client can send that server the `refresh_token` and `client_secret` saved from an earlier sign-in.

## Why this tree is in scope

`services/api/src/mcp/oauth.ts` builds an `OAuthClientProvider` for custom MCP servers. The provider persists client information and bearer tokens, and it keeps a refresh token across token refreshes. That is the client shape the advisory describes.

## Expected

Upgrade `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to 1.31.0 or newer and keep custom-MCP OAuth sign-in working. Until that upgrade, connect OAuth-enabled MCP clients only to servers the operator trusts.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/134
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-104850
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: MCP TypeScript SDK 1.30.0 is below the OAuth credential-binding fix

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
`katex` is still locked below the fix for CVE-2026-103923.

## Current pin

`apps/web` depends on `katex` `^0.16.47`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `katex@0.16.47`. The advisory is fixed in 0.18.2.

## What the advisory covers

From KaTeX 0.11.0 until 0.18.2, ordinary property access treats inherited properties on the renderer options, the trust setting, and namespace lookup as values the caller set. KaTeX does not itself pollute `Object.prototype`, and rendering an expression alone does not run script. If the prototype is already polluted, or an attacker controls the options object's prototype, a math expression can inherit a trust flag and emit links that a page then inserts.

## Expected

Depend on KaTeX 0.18.2 or newer.

## Source

https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/133
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-103923
