148 个 `ReqMethod` · 自动更新 | | `extensions/` | 16,525 | **5%** | 应用扩展、Rail 插件、扩展包 | | `server/runtime/skill/` | 14,727 | **6%** | Skill 包管理、归档、热更 | | `server/runtime/session/` | 14,217 | 18% | 会话持久化、**项目 Git 与按轮次 diff** | | `agent_ws_server.py` | 12,076 | — | WS 服务端，处理 106 个 ReqMethod | | `marketplace/` | 4,690 | 15% | Skill Hub 客户端 | | `a2ui/` | 2,691 | **0%** | 生成式界面 | | `instance_manager/` | 2,539 | **0%** | 单机多实例 | | `channels/` | 15,979 + 216,621(前端) | — | Web / TUI / IDE / 浏览器扩展 / 桌面 / CLI / ACP | *agent-core 适配层（高依赖率）* | 模块 | 行数 | 依赖率 | agent-core 对应物 | |---|---:|---:|---| | `agents/swarm/` | 6,066 | **87%** | `harness/manifest` + `agent_teams/rails` | | `agents/harness/common/tools/` | 19,006 | **74%** | `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `server/runtime/agent_adapter/` | 36,050 | **65%** | `harness` + `agent_teams` | | `agents/harness/common/rails/` | 27,211 | **50%** | `harness/rails` 28,250 | | `agents/harness/team/` | 14,301 | 48% | `agent_teams` 81,969 | | `agents/harness/common/rsi/` | 11,862 | 46% | `rsi/` 86,605 | | `symphony/`（Swarm 侧） | 8,142 | 36% | `symphony/` 51,049 | | `agents/harness/common/auto_harness/` | 6,761 | 33% | `agent_evolving/` 56,772 | ### 1.2 七条容易记错的归属 | 能力 | 常见认知 | 实际 | |---|---|---| | 浏览器自动化 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `harness/tools/browser_move` **25,026 行**；Swarm 的 `channels/browser` 是浏览器扩展前端 | | Symphony 技能编排与检索 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `symphony/` **51,049 行**；Swarm 侧 8,142 行是服务化封装 | | RSI / Skill 自演进 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `rsi/` 86,605 + `agent_evolving/` 56,772 | | TTSE | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `agent_evolving/ttse`；Swarm 侧是配置开关 | | 四套记忆体系 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `core/memory` 18,149 + `harness/personal_context` 24,351 | | 多 agent / swarmflow 引擎 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `agent_teams/` 81,969，引擎在 `workflow/engine` | | 上下文压缩 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `core/context_engine` 23,999（6 个压缩器 + 4 个卸载器） | ### 1.3 JiuwenSwarm 相对 agent-core 的净溢价，对本项目是否用得上 | 自有实质 | 行数 | 用得上？ | |---|---:|---| | `agent_adapter` + `agent_ws_server` | 48,126 | ◐ 仅在「整进程复用 AgentServer」时白拿 | | 内置 35 个 Skill | 41,847 | ◐ 部分（xlsx/pdf/doc 等通用 Skill） | | jiuwenbox 沙箱 | 36,396 | ✅ | | Skill 包管理 | 14,727 | ✅ | | 会话存储 + 项目 Git | 14,217 | ✅ | | cron 调度侧 | 3,558 | ✅ | | Skill Hub | 4,690 | ✅ | | A2UI | 2,691 | ✅ | | gateway 渠道适配 + IM | 54,123 | ❌ 本项目有自己的 HTTP/SSE 控制面 | | 多端（TUI/IDE/桌面/浏览器） | 232,600 | ❌ 前端固定用 `apps/web` | **用得上的约 156,000 行。** --- ## 二、结论一：复用边界划在 agent-core，JiuwenSwarm 按块复用 四条理由： 1. **能力在 agent-core。** 只依赖 agent-core 就能拿到 agent 循环、上下文引擎、记忆、检索、47,454 行工具库（含 25,026 行浏览器自动化）、rails 机制、agent_teams 与 swarmflow 引擎、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving，约 64.8 万行。 2. **替换缝在 agent-core。** 想改上下文组装或多 agent 探索，用到的是 `ContextEngine.register_processor`、`ContextEngine.register_window_mutator`、`agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 的 `use_provider()`、`register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider`、`ModelContext(ABC)`、`AgentRail`——**没有一个在 JiuwenSwarm**（详见第五节）。 3. **穿过 JiuwenSwarm 会造成双层 pin。** JiuwenSwarm 的 `pyproject.toml` 把 agent-core pin 在一个 git rev 上（当前 `d0bd8335`），并有 `make update-openjiuwen` 滚动跟随 agent-core `develop`。若我们经 JiuwenSwarm 间接依赖 agent-core，就**不能自己决定 agent-core 版本**——而所有替换缝都在 agent-core，这是结构性矛盾。 4. **装配成本没有想象中高。** agent-core 的 `openjiuwen.harness` 导出公开工厂 **`create_deep_agent(...)`**（约 30 个关键字参数）与 `DeepAgentConfig`（50+ 字段，全部带文档）。JiuwenSwarm 的 `agent_adapter` 36,050 行里，`interface_code.py`（2,809，code 模式）、`team_helpers.py`（4,411）、`evolution_*`（1,347）、`browser_runtime_security`、`statusline_setup_agent` 等是 **JiuwenSwarm 的产品特性**，不是 agent-core 装配。按本项目自己的产品面（无 IM、无多端、无 code 模式、无 team 模板）重估，**自建装配层约 4,000–8,000 行**。 **与 #84 的差异**：#84 把 JiuwenSwarm 作为复用单位、adapter 接 Gateway WebSocket。本方案把 agent-core 作为硬依赖、JiuwenSwarm 按块可选。两者不是互斥的实现路径，而是**依赖方向的取舍**，建议在第 0 阶段 spike 里一并验证后再定。 --- ## 三、目标后端架构 ### 3.1 三层依赖与一条铁律 | 层 | 内容 | 依赖性质 | |---|---|---| | **L0 agent-core** | `openjiuwen`：agent 循环、ContextEngine、memory、retrieval、tools、rails、agent_teams、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving | **硬依赖，本项目直接 pin 版本** | | **L1 JiuwenSwarm 可选块** | Skill 包管理、Skill Hub、jiuwenbox、cron 调度、A2UI、内置 Skill | **可选依赖，每块一个 port，rev pin** | | **L2 本项目自有** | 科学 rails/tools/explore、科学域服务、科学侧车、runner、产品控制面、Web | 自有 | > **铁律：本项目业务代码不得直接 `import jiuwenswarm`。每块 JiuwenSwarm 能力先定义一个 `Protocol`（port），再在 `adapters/swarm/` 下写适配器实现。** 理由：JiuwenSwarm 是产品不是 SDK（包名 `workswarm`，版本 `0.2.5.beta1`，无公开 API 声明）。把 import 点收敛到一个目录，漂移的爆炸半径就是那个目录；每块可以独立决策、独立回滚；agent-core 保持独立可见。 ### 3.2 进程拓扑 ```mermaid flowchart TB UI["apps/web（React，不变）"] UI -->|"REST + SSE，37 类事件"| API subgraph API["sd-api（Node，:4310，保留）"] A1["http/ · store.ts · 静态托管"] A2["设置 / 模型 / 用量 / MCP 治理 / 权限 / 插件"] A3["agent-client（新增）：驱动 sd-agent"] A4["internal（新增）：科学域服务路由"] end subgraph AGENT["sd-agent（Python，新增）"] L0["L0：import openjiuwen
create_deep_agent · ContextEngine · AgentRail
agent_teams · swarmflow seam"] L2["L2：科学 rails / tools / explore"] L1["L1：ports ← adapters/swarm ⁄ adapters/native"] end API -->|"窄契约：环回 NDJSON + 内部 token"| AGENT subgraph SVC["科学域服务"] R["sd-runner :4311（micromamba · NPU · SSH · kernel）"] E["evolve / memory-graph / paper"] end API -->|"环回 HTTP + token"| SVC AGENT -->|"环回 HTTP + token"| SVC AGENT -.->|"可选，本机 HTTP"| BOX["jiuwenbox"] ``` 四条边界：前端与 `sd-api` 的 REST/SSE 契约**不变**；`sd-api` 与 `sd-agent` 之间用**本项目自定义的窄契约**（不实现 JiuwenSwarm 的 148 个 `ReqMethod`）；科学域服务沿用现有的环回 + 内部 token；JiuwenSwarm 的接触面只有 `adapters/swarm/`。 --- ## 四、代码结构与迁移映射 ### 4.1 新增 `services/agent/` ``` services/agent/ ├── pyproject.toml │ dependencies = [ "openjiuwen==" ] ← L0 硬依赖 │ optional-dependencies: │ swarm-skill / swarm-hub = [ "workswarm==" ] ← L1 按块可选 ├── scripts/check_layers.py ← 分层护栏 └── src/sciencediscovery_agent/ ├── runtime/ ═ L0：只 import openjiuwen ═ │ assembly.py（DeepAgentConfig → create_deep_agent） │ session.py · events.py（→ 37 类 SSE）· model.py · permissions.py ├── context/ ═ L0：上下文三语义 ═ │ processors.py（register_processor） │ window.py（register_window_mutator） │ projections.py（active_skills / plan_state / trust 标注） ├── science/ ═ L2：只依赖 ports/ ═ │ rails/（证据门禁 · 评审检查点 · 溯源记录） │ tools/（执行 · 证据 · 图谱 · 论文） │ explore/（Provider 实现：PUCT / idea-tree） ├── ports/ ═ L1 抽象：纯 Protocol，零依赖 ═ │ skill_store · skill_hub · sandbox · session_store · scheduler ├── adapters/ │ native/ ═ 兜底实现，不依赖 JiuwenSwarm ═ │ swarm/ ═ ★ 唯一允许 import jiuwenswarm ═ └── transport/ ═ 与 sd-api 的窄契约 ═ ``` `check_layers.py` 六条断言进 CI： 1. `runtime/` `context/` `science/` 不得出现 `import jiuwenswarm` 2. `ports/` 不得 import `openjiuwen` 与 `jiuwenswarm`（纯 Protocol） 3. `adapters/native/` 不得 import `jiuwenswarm` 4. `adapters/swarm/` 是唯一允许的目录 5. **每个 `adapters/swarm/.py` 必须有同名的 `adapters/native/.py` 兜底** 6. `science/` 不得 import `adapters/` 第 5 条是关键：没有兜底，「可选」就是假的。 ### 4.2 迁移映射 | 现有 | 行数 | 去向 | 替代者 | |---|---:|---|---| | `packages/runtime-core` | 626 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/single_agent` + `core/runner` | | `packages/context` | 2,439 | ❌ 删，语义迁 `sd-agent/context/` | L0 `core/context_engine` 23,999 | | `packages/model` | 1,465 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/foundation/llm` | | `packages/tools` + `workspace`（工具部分） | 约 3,400 | ❌ 删 | L0 `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `packages/specialist` + `orchestration` + `plan` | 3,190 | ❌ 删 | L0 `agent_teams` + `harness/rails` | | `packages/governance` | 227 | ◐ 策略留 Node，审批迁 `sd-agent` | L0 `harness/security` | | `packages/provenance` `idea-tree` `memory` `cas` `artifact-manager` `data-source` `trajectory` | 13,675 | ◐ 加 HTTP 外壳成为 `internal/` 域服务 | — | | `packages/schema` `mcp` `mcp-sources` `skill` `plugin-sdk` `executor` `sandbox-capability` | 约 13,000 | ✅ 保留 Node | — | | `services/api/native-agent` | 1,121 | ❌ 删 | — | | `services/api/{runs,agent-run,bootstrap}` | 5,112 | ◐ 改写为 `sd-agent` 客户端 | — | | `services/api` 其余 | 约 25,000 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `services/runner` | 8,798 | ✅ 保留（M2 可选把隔离原语换成 jiuwenbox） | — | | `services/{evolve,memory-graph,paper,gateway}` | 23,045 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `skills/` 17 个 | 3,641 | ✅ 保留，经 `ports/skill_store` 读取 | — | | `services/launcher` + `scripts/binary-release` | 3,203+ | ◐ payload 增 Python 运行时 | — | | **新增** `services/agent/` | 约 8,000–13,000 | ➕ | — | | **新增** `services/api/src/{agent-client,internal}` | 约 3,500–6,000 | ➕ | — | **后端非测试 TypeScript 82,367 行中，保留约 66,400 行（约 81%）。** --- ## 五、改基础算法的路径（这些缝全部在 agent-core） ### 5.1 上下文组装 `openjiuwen/core/context_engine/` 是完整插件架构：`ModelContext(ABC)`（抽象方法含 `get_context_window()`）、`ContextProcessor`（钩子 `on_add_messages` / `on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `sys.path` 不同。`get_config` 被 185 个文件使用。 **(2) `common/utils.py`（2,954 行）假定 `~/.jiuwenswarm` 工作区布局**：解析顺序 `JIUWENSWARM_DATA_DIR` → `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` → `~/.jiuwenswarm`，并期望其下有 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `chromadb`、`faiss-cpu`、`playwright`、`tree-sitter`、`sqlite-vec`、`pgvector`、`opentelemetry-*`，以及对本项目完全无用的 `python-telegram-bot` / `discord.py` / `slack-bolt` / `dingtalk-stream` / `wecom-aibot-sdk`。 ### 6.2 C 型按块实测 | 块 | 依赖 `common.config` | 依赖 `common.utils` | `sys.path` 副作用 | **C 型等级** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **Skill Hub**（`marketplace/hub_client` + 3 个兄弟文件） | **0** | **0** | **无** | **无** | | **Skill 文件/归档原语**（`skill_files` `archive_store`） | 0 | 0 | 无 | **无** | | **jiuwenbox** | 0 | 0 | 无（本机 HTTP 服务） | **无** | | cron store | 0 | 1（一个路径函数） | 无 | **低** | | **Skill 包管理**（`skill_manager.py` 8,841 行） | **4** | 1 | **有** | **高** | | 会话存储 / 项目 Git | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高**（且与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 双主） | | 产品 rails / tools | 多 | 多 | 有 | **高** | 由此修订接入策略： - **Skill Hub**：四个文件干净到可以直接 import，也可以照抄（Apache-2.0）。零 C 型侵入。 - **jiuwenbox**：**它已经是独立组件**——自带 `pyproject.toml`（`name = "jiuwenbox"`），依赖只有 pydantic/pyyaml/httpx/fastapi/uvicorn/python-multipart/mcp，**不依赖 `workswarm`**，Python 代码对 `jiuwenswarm` 零引用；JiuwenSwarm 自己也是通过 HTTP 调它。我们可以 `pip install "jiuwenbox @ git+#subdirectory=jiuwenbox"`，零侵入。 - **cron**：只要一个路径函数。建议照抄 cron 表达式与 store 语义到 `adapters/native/`，不为一个函数引入 `common.utils`。 - **Skill 包管理**：8,841 行会带来全套 C 型侵入。三个选择：① 在 `sd-agent` 独立进程里接受它；② 只取 `skill_files` + `archive_store` 两个干净原语，打包逻辑自己写；③ 不接。 - **会话存储**：明确不接，避免与我们的 `catalog.sqlite` 形成双主；会话回溯用 L0 的 `core/session/vcs` 底座自己做产品化。 **新增设计约束**：`adapters/swarm/` 每个适配器要在文件头声明它拖进来的 C 型侵入，由 `check_layers.py` 校验声明与实际 import 一致；未声明的 import 直接失败。 ### 6.3 A 型：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 源码的场景，已缩到 2 条 本方案下**不再适用**的四条：新增 `ReqMethod`（我们不跑 AgentServer）、改 `agent_adapter`（我们自己装配）、换协作调度内核（走 agent-core 的 seam）、复用 JiuwenSwarm 前端组件（前端用我们自己的）。 仍然适用的： | # | 场景 | 触发条件 | 处置 | |---|---|---|---| | **A1** | jiuwenbox 增加 macOS 隔离后端 | 要保住 macOS 源码模式**同时**采用 jiuwenbox（jiuwenbox 目前 Linux-only；我们的 `seatbelt.ts` 在 47 个文件被引用） | 上游 PR；或不采用 jiuwenbox，继续用 `services/runner` | | **A2** | `skill_manager` 解耦工作区与全局 config | 要接 Skill 包管理，且不接受 6.1 的 C 型侵入 | 上游 PR（改为构造参数注入）；短期用 6.2 的选择② | 另有 A3（`common/config.py` 去掉导入期 `sys.path` 变更）只在「后端完全合并为单一 Python 进程」的形态下出现；本方案的 Node + sidecar 形态天然规避。 ### 6.4 B 型：建议向上游提出的扩展点 | # | 对象 | 诉求 | 不给的代价 | |---|---|---|---| | B1 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider` 与 `ContextEngine.register_processor` 的**覆盖生效时机窗口** | 改基础算法只能依赖未文档化的时机 | | B2 | **agent-core** | 明确 `register_window_mutator` 在处理器链中的**执行点** | 窗口权威降级为尽力而为 | | B3 | JiuwenSwarm | 给出**可外部复用模块清单**并脱离 beta | `adapters/swarm/` 全部建立在内部模块上 | | B4 | JiuwenSwarm | **Skill Hub HTTP API 版本化**（现有 `hub_asset_port.py` 是 Python 端口稳定声明，HTTP 层无版本） | 被动跟随；最坏退回本地库 | | B5 | JiuwenSwarm | `skill_manager` 路径/config **改为注入式** | 见 A2 | | B6 | JiuwenSwarm | `common/config.py` 提供**无副作用导入模式** | 单进程形态下有静默 shadow 风险 | | B7 | JiuwenSwarm | jiuwenbox 发布到 PyPI | 便利性诉求，可用 git 子目录安装替代 | **B1、B2 最该优先推动**——「改基础算法」的能力完全取决于它们。 ### 6.5 反向：我们会不会侵入 JiuwenSwarm 不会，且是结构性的：单向依赖（`workswarm` 按 extra 引入、jiuwenbox 按本机服务引入），JiuwenSwarm 对我们零依赖；我们不跑它的进程、不实现它的协议、不改它的配置语义。若要贡献科学能力，走 Rail 插件 / Skill / MCP 的正向 PR，对它是加法。 --- ## 七、工作量 估算口径：同语言搬运约 800–1,500 行/人周；跨语言重写含测试约 250–400 行/人周；协议与语义对齐按耦合点计。不含产品需求变更与跨团队协同开销。**未做原型验证，第 0 阶段完成后需重新校准。** | 阶段 | 内容 | 乐观 | 可能 | 悲观 | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | M0-a | 证伪 spike（四个判据，见第八节） | 2 | 3 | 5 | | M0-b | `sd-agent` 骨架 + `sd-api` 的 `agent-client` + 37 类事件映射 | 10 | 14 | 22 | | M0-c | 分层护栏、`ports/` 定稿、`adapters/native/` 兜底 | 3 | 4 | 6 | | M1-a | 工具面迁移 + 13,675 行域包加 HTTP 外壳 | 12 | 17 | 26 | | M1-b | 上下文三语义 + 证据门禁与评审检查点 | 6 | 9 | 15 | | M1-c | 科学探索 Provider（PUCT / idea-tree） | 8 | 12 | 20 | | M2-a~d | 按块接 JiuwenSwarm（Hub / Skill 包 / jiuwenbox / cron） | 15 | 22 | 36 | | M3-a | 分发：Python 运行时进单可执行文件 payload（双架构）、Docker | 8 | 11 | 17 | | M3-b | 测试与 CI：增 Python 层；E2E 大部保留（REST/SSE 与 Web 不变） | 6 | 9 | 14 | | **合计（M2 全接）** | | **70** | **101** | **161 人周** | | **不接任何 JiuwenSwarm 块** | | **55** | **79** | **125 人周** | **M2 各块彼此独立**，可以只接 Skill Hub 不接 jiuwenbox，或反过来。这是本方案与「整体二选一」的主要差别：**JiuwenSwarm 从一次性决策变成逐块定价**。 **不可逆点**：M1-a 完成后，工具实现不再留在 Node 侧。M0 全程可回滚。 --- ## 八、第 0 阶段的证伪判据 | # | 判据 | 决定什么 | |---|---|---| | ① | `create_deep_agent()` 跑通一次带工具调用 + 审批中断 + 流式的会话，并映射成现有 37 类 SSE | 自建装配的 4,000–8,000 行估算是否成立 | | ② | `register_window_mutator` 注入的受保护段，能否存活到最终 LLM 窗口（构造一个会被内置压缩器改写的长会话） | 上下文三语义能否等价迁移，还是要接受行为回退 | | ③ | 实现一个最小 `Provider` 并 `use_provider()`，验证 workflow 原语被整体替换后行为正确 | 科学探索能否成为多 agent 范式 | | ④ | `pip install workswarm` 后做依赖裁剪试验，量出可接受的最小依赖集 | M2 各块的分发成本 | 判据 ①③④ 直接决定路线，判据 ② 决定产品行为是否回退。**在第 0 阶段之前讨论总工期意义不大。** --- ## 九、待决定事项 1. **复用边界**：agent-core 直接依赖（本 issue）还是经 JiuwenSwarm Gateway（#84）。建议在 M0-a 一并验证后再定。 2. **是否采用 jiuwenbox**：采用则获得 Landlock、cgroup、推理隐私代理，但 **macOS 源码模式会失去沙箱**（jiuwenbox Linux-only）。需要产品明确。 3. **是否接 Skill 包管理**：涉及 6.2 的高 C 型侵入，三个选择需要拍板。 4. **控制面语言**：本方案保持 `services/api` 为 Node（保全约 81% 后端代码）。若未来要合并为单一 Python 后端，M0–M2 完成后可平滑过渡，但会额外触发 A3。 5. **差异化定位**：如果本项目的差异化主要在科学域能力（工具、连接器、证据溯源、科学环境、NPU），现有分层足够；如果在 agent 算法本身（上下文、探索、检索、演进），则应进一步收紧对 agent-core 的直接控制。这决定第 5 节各层级的使用频度。 --- ### 补充说明 - 本 issue 的全部结论来自上述基线 commit 的只读代码盘点，**未改动任何仓库**，未建分支、未提 PR。 - 归属用的「依赖率」是「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件数 / 该模块 `.py` 文件总数」，是**代理指标**而非逻辑占比的精确度量；每条归属结论另有行数对照或具体文件路径佐证。 - C 型侵入的判定口径是「模块文件是否 import `jiuwenswarm.common.config` / `jiuwenswarm.common.utils`」，是传递依赖的一级近似；真正接入前应在 M0/M2 用一次真实 import 验证完整传递闭包。 - 与 #84 互为补充，不替代。

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

Nightly trial run [38107013490](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38107013490) (real model, built-in agent loop) was cancelled by hand during its fourth journey. By then three of its ten journeys had already failed: DRB-59, DRB-64 and DRB-58, each after 83–90 minutes. Nothing that was uploaded says why:

- The job log (and `run.log`) has one `✘` line per journey, and no error.
- Each journey report says **FAIL** with "0 / 0 steps passed", and no error.
- `test-results/` is missing. That is where `benchmark-metrics.json` (run status, delivery, error, sub-agents), `error-context.md` and the trace would be. `summary.txt` is missing too.

What could be reconstructed from `stack.log` timing alone: DRB-58 used up its 90-minute run budget. DRB-59 and DRB-64 ended on their own after 83–84 minutes, well inside their 120-minute budget, and then failed at the delivery assertion. Whether those two runs failed, or completed without a readable report, can no longer be told.

## Why

1. **Per-test evidence is copied only on exit.** Playwright writes `test-results/` to `.e2e/test-results`, which is outside the uploaded results directory. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` copies it there only in its EXIT trap. When a job is cancelled, the runner sends SIGINT, then SIGTERM about 7.5 s later, then kills the process tree about 2.5 s after that. bash runs the trap only once Playwright has exited, and Playwright was still tearing down the running journey: its `finally` alone waits up to 30 s for the run to cancel. So the copy never happens. A job timeout or a lost runner has the same effect.
2. **The `list` reporter prints failure details only when the whole run ends.** As each test ends, it prints just the `✘` line.
3. **Journey reports only record errors raised inside `journey.step()`.** The reports themselves are written into the results as each journey ends, which is why they survived. But the benchmark journeys assert in the test body, so their reports carry no error at all.

## Expected

Every journey that has finished leaves its evidence in the uploaded results at the moment it finishes. Its failure reason can be read in the job log and in its journey report without waiting for the rest of the run, whether or not the run ends normally.

## Proposal

- `run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR=<layer results>/test-results`, and `test/playwright.config.ts` uses it as `outputDir` (falling back to `.e2e/test-results`). The exit trap then copies only the HTML report, which Playwright renders once the run ends anyway.
- A journey report that failed without a failed step gets a "failure reason" section from `testInfo.errors`. It is redacted and truncated like step errors already are.
- When a journey fails, print the first lines of its error after its `journey report (FAIL)` line: the assertion message and expected/received, without the stack, and redacted.

Not in scope: for a cancelled layer, the shared-plan summary still reports "no frozen plan reported … the layer stopped before it collected its tests", because the shared runner writes its accounting only after Playwright exits. With the evidence above, a cancelled run can be diagnosed regardless.

Related: #233 (a delivery failure does not carry the run's own error).
closed_recent.title: bug(e2e): A cancelled or killed E2E run loses the failure evidence of journeys that already finished

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

A real research run that has already been working can stop because the model gateway rejects one tool call whose arguments do not parse. The same happens to a subagent that has already finished its work. The page then tells the user to check the model configuration.

On main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-59** ran for 20.2 minutes. Both subagents completed. The session contained `navigation_cues_summary.md`, `navigation_cues_sources.json`, `disturbance_summary.md`, and `disturbance_sources.json`, and the page showed 167K usage. The required `deepresearchbench-59.md` was not among them. The final answer was empty and the run status was `failed`.

The request error on the failure page was:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell); gateway request chatcmpl-a2101146-60b8-4549-a033-1fe6f70bcfa0
```

The same DRB-59 passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) in 1.3 hours. The gateway and model id had already completed two subagents in the failing run.

On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) (`90db5b8e`), the same failure ended two more journeys, once on an MCP tool rather than `run_shell`. All three events below are logged as `"truncated":false` in the server log's `[model-arguments]` line. The server log has no 5xx or 429 on model calls during the journeys.

| Journey | Where it failed | Gateway request | Tool | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DRB-64 | Main run, after 23 minutes. Both subagents had completed, and the main agent had just said it would write the report. | `chatcmpl-2c3cbc55-d420-4a0e-ab0f-f460883c3061` | `run_shell` | Run `failed`, empty final answer. The session had three files from the subagents (two source packages and coverage notes); the required `deepresearchbench-64.md` was never declared. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 1st attempt. Its `deliverable_check` MCP call had already returned `ok: true`; it failed while writing `signoff.json`. | `chatcmpl-34b150cd-8aa4-478d-8c60-f6b6de204c62` | `run_shell` | Subagent `failed`. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 2nd attempt, on its `deliverable_check` call, which was to carry the full 26,226-byte report. | `chatcmpl-f980e9ac-a76a-422a-af31-11a515383f8f` | MCP `deliverable_check` | Subagent `failed`. The checker never received the call. |

In TC-E2E-01 all five research specialists had completed within 37 minutes and `evidence_brief.md` (26,226 bytes) existed. The two signoff failures and their re-dispatches used the remaining time; the third signoff attempt was still running when the 55-minute test budget ran out, and the test cancelled the run, which had no final answer. How the test reports a run cut off by its budget is #239.

## Why one call ends the run

Code at `90db5b8e`; these files are unchanged on main at `9189206d`.

1. `packages/model/src/client.ts` parses each assembled tool call with `JSON.parse` ([L221-L230](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L221-L230)) and sets `argsParseError` on failure.
2. In the JiuwenSwarm model gateway, `rejectInvalidArguments` ([L220-L228](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L220-L228)) lets truncated turns through to the output-limit recovery, but throws for any non-truncated call with `argsParseError`. The gateway answers that turn with an error (an SSE error event once streaming has started, otherwise HTTP 502). Swarm does not retry the turn, and `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` ([L363-L367](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L363-L367)) turns it into the error of the run or subagent.
3. `classifyRunFailure` ([services/api/src/run-failure.ts L28-L49](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/run-failure.ts#L28-L49)) matches none of its markers for this message and falls through to `semantic-error`. The Web UI renders that class as `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`: "The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry."

The same condition is handled three different ways:

- Native runtime: `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` ([L334-L338](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/tools/src/registry.ts#L334-L338)) returns `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS` with `retryable: true` to the model as a tool result, and the model can re-issue the call.
- Swarm, truncated call: the calls are withheld and the turn goes through bounded output-limit recovery. In Nightly 37875334064 two such events (03:57 and 04:42 UTC) did not end their runs, and those journeys (DRB-58, DRB-62) passed.
- Swarm, non-truncated call: the run or subagent fails.

Passing the call through unchanged would be worse: the gateway re-serializes calls from their parsed arguments (`toolCallsOf`, [L123-L125](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L123-L125)), so Swarm would execute the tool with `{}`.

## Where it fails: in ScienceDiscovery, before JiuwenSwarm sees the call

Every model request from JiuwenSwarm passes two ScienceDiscovery layers before it reaches the provider:

```text
JiuwenSwarm -> adapter /llm/<token>/v1/chat/completions (services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py)
            -> Node model gateway (services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts)
            -> packages/model client -> provider
```

`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` points Swarm's model at `modelGateway.url` ([L555](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L555)), and the adapter route forwards to that URL. The gateway drops the whole turn before Swarm receives the tool call. Swarm only gets an error for its model request; it does not retry that request, and its agent loop ends.

JiuwenSwarm's own handling would not end the run. JiuwenSwarm `workswarm0.2.6` pins agent-core (`openjiuwen`) at `ad0c9dfb`, whose `openjiuwen/core/single_agent/ability_manager.py` parses tool arguments in `_parse_tool_arguments_with_repair`: `json.loads`, then a bracket-balancing repair, and if both fail `execute` raises `AbilityExecutionError` whose `ToolMessage` (`Invalid tool arguments JSON: …`) is returned to the model as the tool result, "so it can self-correct". The native ScienceDiscovery runtime does the same with `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS`.

A second ScienceDiscovery layer would reject the same call for platform tools. The adapter's `StreamingToolRewriter` parses the complete arguments of each platform tool with `json.loads` at `finish_reason` to append the run tag ([L328](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L328)), and on failure ends the stream with `invalid streamed platform tool arguments` ([L362-L366](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L362-L366)). It was not reached in these runs because the gateway had already stopped the turn. Simply passing the call through to Swarm would hit this layer, and would also put unparseable arguments into the history replayed to the provider.

## Expected

- A non-truncated call whose arguments do not parse is not executed, and the model is told which call failed and why so that it can re-issue it, with a bounded number of attempts (the same shape as the truncated-call recovery, or a bounded re-sample in the gateway). One bad call does not end a run that has been working for 20 to 40 minutes, and does not fail a subagent that has already finished its work.
- This holds for every tool, including MCP tools, in the main run and in subagents.
- If recovery is exhausted, the run error says that the model produced an invalid tool call, with the tool name and gateway request id. The user-facing text does not tell the user to check the model configuration when the same model has already been calling tools in that run.
- The Actions log for the journey includes this error instead of only `delivery.status` `"failed"` (#233).

## Evidence limits

Neither Nightly captured the raw argument strings or the parser messages, so whether the model emitted malformed JSON or the stream assembler lost part of the arguments is not known. Making that distinguishable is #246.

### 📚 Documentation Issue Description

> Related: #55 (owns the evolve pages in both languages), #118 (owns the English Idea Tree page and records product status).

## Summary

The Chinese tree has ten pages with no English counterpart, the English tree now has three pages with no Chinese counterpart, and readers cannot tell whether a missing language means "not translated yet", "internal", or "unsupported". I would like each gap classified and then closed, translated, or labeled.

## Current state

Verified against 0e904661:

- `git ls-tree` lists 39 Markdown files under `docs/en/` and 46 under `docs/zh/`, the
  language-index `README.md` included in both. Excluding that index file, the counts are 38
  English pages and 45 Chinese pages.
- Ten Chinese-only pages. Nine sit under `docs/zh/developer-docs/` and one under `docs/zh/core/`:

  ```text
  docs/zh/developer-docs/evolve-standalone.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/plugins.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/runner-inheritance.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/session-trajectory.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-mvp.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-m1.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-library-management-m2.md
  docs/zh/developer-docs/skill-self-evolution.md
  docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md
  ```

- Three English-only pages, all under `docs/en/developer-docs/`: `context-assembly.md`, `context-assembly-examples.md` and `runtime-core.md`. The path move introduced this gap: they were language-neutral under `docs/architecture/`, so before the reorg both language trees could reach them and now the Chinese tree cannot. Fixing this is content work for a later step, recorded here because it is a real gap in the shipped tree.
- The PR 122 body itself lists bilingual semantic drift as follow-up work, so this issue does not own the content alignment of shared pages.

## What to write

1. Classify the nine pages under `docs/zh/developer-docs/`. Two are owned elsewhere: `evolve-standalone.md` stays with #55, and the skill-library drafts are recorded here while their consolidation stays with the PR follow-up. The pages that need a disposition here are `plugins.md`, `runner-inheritance.md`, `session-trajectory.md`, `skill-self-evolution.md` and the four skill-library-management files. Each is either translated (public), labeled as an internal design note, or retired. The public status comes from the capability-entries issue (#118).
2. Classify `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md`. The English counterpart or replacement is owned by #118, so this issue records only the page-level disposition and the status label.
3. Give the three English-only pages their own decision: restore them to a language-neutral location, add Chinese counterparts, or label them English-only.
4. Add a status label to every page that has no counterpart in one language, so a reader can tell "not translated" from "internal".
5. Add the missing language counterpart for every page classified as public.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the eight pages owned by this issue has a recorded disposition (translated, labeled internal, or retired), with maintainer sign-off for the unconfirmed ones.
- [ ] `docs/zh/core/idea-tree.md` has a recorded disposition, and the English page or replacement is delivered by #118.
- [ ] The three English-only pages have a recorded decision.
- [ ] English counterparts exist for the pages classified as public, and Chinese counterparts exist where the decision is to translate.
- [ ] Every page without a counterpart in one language carries a status label.
- [ ] Pages delivered by #117 and #118 land in both languages.

## Open questions

- Public status of plugins, runner inheritance, session trajectory, skill-self-evolution and the skill-library design notes (same confirmation as #118).
- Can the superseded `skill-library-management-m1` / `m2` / `mvp` drafts be retired, or should they be kept as history?
- Should the three former `docs/architecture/` pages return to a language-neutral directory, or is an English-only page with a clear label acceptable?

## Out of scope

- Semantic drift between shared pages such as `mcp-tool-protocol.md`, `subagent-orchestration.md` and `deployment.md`. PR 122 lists that as a content-owner follow-up, so it is not an acceptance criterion here.
- How a page without a counterpart is displayed on any downstream site. The public site repository is deferred for now.
- Translating internal design notes before their public status is confirmed.
- The English Idea Tree page (owned by #118) and the evolve sidecar disposition (owned by #55).

Docs baseline: `feat/jiuwenswarm` @ 0e904661.

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
In `apps/desktop` SSE `pump`, frame `data:` is `JSON.parse`d without try/catch. A single malformed frame ends the stream and drops the live run UI even when the server may still be running.

## Expected
A bad frame is skipped or counted, the pump continues (or one toast surfaces), and the run still reaches a terminal/handled state when the server finishes.

## Verification cases

1. **Malformed mid-stream frame**
   - **Preconditions:** Desktop workbench connected; a run is in flight with an open SSE stream.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Inject one malformed `data:` line mid-stream (invalid JSON).
     2. Observe UI and subsequent frames.
   - **Expected / pass:** Pump does not abort solely due to that frame; user sees at most one clear error/toast; later valid frames or a terminal settle still apply.

2. **Clean stream still works**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1), no injection.
   - **Steps:** Complete a normal turn end-to-end.
   - **Expected / pass:** Transcript, terminal status, and settle behave as today (no regression).

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/499 (foundation). Out of that PR's Act-on scope; code-review inference on `api/stream.ts` pump.
items.title: desktop: harden SSE frame JSON.parse so one bad frame does not end the run stream

items.author: sciencediscovery-bot[bot]
items.body:
跟进 #510（`fix(web): distinguish untitled session labels`，Closes #497）检视时发现的两处显示口径问题。它们是 `session-title.ts` 实现本身带来的，不是 #510 引入的新回归，因此没有作为合入门槛，单独记在这里。

## 现状
`apps/web/src/session-title.ts` 的 `sessionDisplayTitle()`：
- 候选集由调用方传入，`App.tsx` 默认传 `artifactSessions` = `listSessions(projectId, "all")`，**含已归档**；
- 序号按 `createdAt` 升序（`id` 兜底）编号。

而侧栏渲染的是 `sessions`，即 `listSessions(projectId, sessionListState)` 的子集，且**按 `updatedAt` 降序**（`services/api/src/store.ts:2787`）。

## 两个具体表现
1. **编号引用不可见的兄弟**：同一 Project 有两条未命名会话、其中一条归档后，活动列表只剩一条，却显示「未命名会话 2」，用户找不到 1（归档视图同理）。
2. **编号顺序与列表顺序可能相反**：较早创建的那条先有了活动（`updatedAt` 变大）后，侧栏从上到下会是「未命名会话 2」「1」。

## 可选方向
- A：编号按**当前渲染的列表**算（把可见子集传进 `sessionDisplayTitle`），归档视图各自编号；
- B：编号按整个 Project 算（保持现状），但排序键改成与列表一致（`updatedAt` 降序），至少让顺序读起来自洽。

两者都只是显示层改动，不动 `UNTITLED_SESSION_TITLE` 哨兵。最终取哪种属产品/UX 选择，需要维护者定。

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
Desktop workspace upload sends `File.name` into FormData without client-side basename sanitization. Path escape remains a server responsibility (`readWorkspaceFile` notes this), but a crafted name such as `../outside.txt` or a name containing `/` should be rejected or renamed on the client as defense in depth.

## Expected
Before upload, the client strips path segments / rejects unsafe names so only a basename reaches FormData; server still remains the authority and continues to rename/reject escapes.

## Verification cases

1. **Crafted relative name**
   - **Preconditions:** Open session with workspace panel; upload enabled (session not archived).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Upload (or simulate) a `File` whose `name` is `../outside.txt`.
     2. Inspect the FormData filename and the resulting workspace listing.
   - **Expected / pass:** Client does not send `../outside.txt` as-is (sanitize/reject); server listing shows no escape outside the session workspace.

2. **Name with slash**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload a `File` whose `name` contains `/` (e.g. `a/b.txt`).
   - **Expected / pass:** Client basename-only or reject; no nested path created via the client name alone.

3. **Normal basename unchanged**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload `notes.md`.
   - **Expected / pass:** File appears under the session workspace with the expected name (rename-on-conflict still applies).

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/501. Non-blocking; server-side path authority noted in-PR.
items.title: desktop: sanitize upload File.name basename before FormData (defense in depth)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem
Settings › Runtime remote host credentials are write-only (good): empty fields keep the stored secret. The register/update API already accepts `password` / `passphrase` / `privateKeyPath: null` to forget, but the desktop UI never sends null, so there is no way to clear stored credentials from the dialog.

## Expected
A clear/forget control (or equivalent) sends null for the chosen secret fields so `hasPassword` / `hasPrivateKey` clear and later probes fail until a new secret is set.

## Verification cases

1. **Empty save keeps secret (current)**
   - **Preconditions:** Remote host with a stored password (`hasPassword` true).
   - **Steps:** Open credentials; leave password empty; save.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` remains true (keep-on-empty behavior preserved).

2. **Explicit forget**
   - **Preconditions:** Same host with stored password.
   - **Steps:** Use the clear/forget control; save; re-open credentials / probe connect.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` false; probe fails without a new secret.

3. **Re-set after forget**
   - **Preconditions:** Credentials cleared per (2).
   - **Steps:** Enter a new password; save; probe.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` true; probe succeeds with the new secret.

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/502. Out of Act-on scope for that PR (Escape stacking is in-scope there).
items.title: desktop: UI to clear stored remote Runner credentials (API already accepts null)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

#494 adds `scripts/lib/venv-launchers.mjs` (trampoline replace + runtime DLL copy) with portable unit tests, but:

1. Nothing in-tree calls `replaceVenvTrampolines` / `copyVenvRuntimeDlls` (`assemble-backend.mjs` / bootstrap not present yet).
2. Comments claim a closed loop with `fixVenvHome`, but that helper does not exist — after swapping the launcher, `pyvenv.cfg` `home` can still point at the build machine, so the real `python.exe` still fails off-machine.
3. Tests only compare bytes; they do not spawn `Scripts\python.exe`, so the field failures (entity not found / `0xC0000135`) are not covered.

## Expected

- Call sites in assemble-backend (pack-time) and bootstrap (first-run repair) invoke the module.
- `fixVenvHome` (or equivalent) rewrites `pyvenv.cfg` `home` to the bundled interpreter root.
- A Windows smoke test builds a uv venv, relocates it, spawns `Scripts\python.exe -c "..."`, and asserts exit 0 with `sys.prefix` at the new path.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — pack-time wiring
- **Preconditions:** Payload contains a uv-created venv whose `Scripts\python.exe` is a trampoline; assemble-backend runs.
- **Steps:** Inspect `Scripts\python.exe` and `pyvenv.cfg` after assemble.
- **Expected / pass:** Launcher is a real CPython stub (no `uv trampoline` marker); `home` points at the bundled python root; runtime DLLs sit beside the launcher.

### Case 2 — first-run bootstrap repair
- **Preconditions:** `dataDir\envs` still has pre-fix trampolines (reinstall with valid unpack stamp).
- **Steps:** Start the shell once on a clean machine without system Python.
- **Expected / pass:** Bootstrap replaces trampolines, copies DLLs, fixes `home`; each venv `python.exe -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"` exits 0.

### Case 3 — Windows spawn smoke (CI or labeled job)
- **Preconditions:** `os:windows` (or equivalent) test runner with a bundled/minimal CPython + uv.
- **Steps:** Create uv venv → move tree → `spawn(Scripts/python.exe, ["-c", "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"])`.
- **Expected / pass:** Exit code 0; printed prefix equals the relocated venv path. Byte-only unit tests alone do not satisfy this case.

## Context

Refs #494, #493. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.04. #494 should use `Refs #493` until this loop lands (or fold wiring into the same PR).
items.title: win-desktop-client: wire venv-launchers + fixVenvHome + Windows spawn smoke

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

`win-desktop-client/` is an independent pnpm workspace (not listed in the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml` packages: `config / apps/* / services/* / packages/*`). Architecture checks and `tsconfig.tests.json` also skip it. As a result, install / typecheck / unit-test failures under this tree are invisible to GitHub Actions (see #486: missing patch and empty `tsconfig` include were only found by local runs).

## Expected

A CI job (or matrix entry) runs on changes under `win-desktop-client/**` and exercises at least:

- `pnpm install` (lockfile present)
- `pnpm typecheck` (when sources exist)
- `pnpm test` for portable Node tests

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — install gate
- **Preconditions:** PR that only touches `win-desktop-client/` and references a missing `patchedDependencies` file (or otherwise breaks install).
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** The new job fails with a clear install error; root jobs that ignore this tree may still be green.

### Case 2 — typecheck / test gate
- **Preconditions:** PR adds a TypeScript error under `win-desktop-client/src/` or a failing `test/*.test.ts`.
- **Steps:** Open the PR; wait for CI.
- **Expected / pass:** typecheck or test step fails; merge is blocked by the required check once wired.

### Case 3 — no-op on unrelated paths
- **Preconditions:** PR only changes `apps/web/` (or another root package).
- **Steps:** Open the PR.
- **Expected / pass:** The win-desktop-client job is skipped or stays green without installing Electron unnecessarily.

## Context

Refs #486, #485. Non-blocking Follow-up from HongyeZhou review of shell.01.
items.title: win-desktop-client: add CI job for independent Electron workspace

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

`services/api/src/http/static.ts` rejects paths with `candidate.startsWith(\`${staticDir}/\`)`. On Windows `resolve()` yields backslash separators, so the prefix check is always false and every SPA asset/route returns **400 Invalid path**.

This was discovered while reviewing PR #478 (`feat(F3.1): CAS platform abstraction`), which embeds a fix + tests. It is **out of scope for #477 (F3.1 CAS)** and should land as its own change with its own verification.

## Expected

Path containment uses a platform-neutral check (e.g. `path.relative` + `isAbsolute` / `..` segments) so Linux/macOS behaviour is unchanged and Windows serves SPA assets correctly.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows SPA asset served
- **Preconditions:** API built with `apps/web` static output; process running on Windows (or a path with `\` separators for `staticDir`).
- **Steps:** `GET /` and `GET /assets/<existing-bundle>.js` against the static handler.
- **Expected / pass:** Both return **200** with the expected body (not 400).

### Case 2 — Escape still rejected
- **Preconditions:** Same as Case 1; a file exists just above the static root.
- **Steps:** Request `/../escape.txt` and a percent-encoded variant `/%2e%2e/escape.txt`.
- **Expected / pass:** Both return **400 Invalid path**.

### Case 3 — No Linux/macOS regression
- **Preconditions:** Same suite on Linux (or macOS).
- **Steps:** Run the static containment unit tests (`services/api/src/http/static.test.ts` or equivalent).
- **Expected / pass:** All cases green; nested `..data` directory name is still served (not treated as escape).

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478
- Parent Windows desktop track: #400 / #31
items.title: fix(api): SPA static path containment breaks on Windows (serveStatic 400)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

POSIX `chmod 0600` only toggles the read-only bit on Windows NTFS and does **not** strip inherited group/world access. Secrets, bootstrap tokens, and similar owner-only files need an ACL adaptation (`icacls` inheritance strip + grant current user).

PR #478 embeds `restrictToOwner` / `restrictToOwnerSync` under `services/api` and `services/runner` platform layers while claiming only F3.1 (#477). Track **F3.3** here so scope and AC are explicit (or split out of #478).

## Expected

- Sensitive write sites that previously `chmod`'d to owner-only use `restrictToOwner` via `platform/os` (api) / `platform` (runner).
- POSIX keeps `chmod`; Windows uses icacls with inheritance removed.
- Highest-sensitivity stores (e.g. master key / SSH private key paths) are included or explicitly deferred with rationale.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows ACL tightened
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; create a temp file that inherits group-readable ACLs.
- **Steps:** Call `restrictToOwner(file)`; run `icacls <file>` and inspect DACL.
- **Expected / pass:** Inheritance removed; current user has access; unintended group/world ACE gone (or equivalent owner-only outcome documented in the test).

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run posix platform + existing secrets/bootstrap unit tests.
- **Expected / pass:** Mode bits still applied as on `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Sync path at startup
- **Preconditions:** Windows; data dir owned by another principal (or simulated failure).
- **Steps:** Exercise `restrictToOwnerSync` on bootstrap/token paths.
- **Expected / pass:** Failure mode is explicit (error message), not a silent weaken; documented in PR/issue notes.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
- Note from #478 review: `store/secrets.ts` / `store/ssh-config.ts` may still rely on raw `chmod` — include or call out as residual risk.
items.title: [F3.3] Owner-restrict file ACLs on Windows (icacls / restrictToOwner)

items.author: HongyeZhou
items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, killing a runner child with POSIX-style signals does not tear down the full process tree. Desktop Windows work needs a platform adaptation that terminates the child **and** its grandchildren (e.g. `taskkill /T /F`).

PR #478 (`Closes #477` / F3.1 CAS) already embeds `terminateTree` under `services/runner/src/platform/`. That belongs to **F3.2**, not F3.1 — track and accept it here (or split it out of #478).

## Expected

- `services/runner` (and any required API call sites) obtain tree-kill via `platform/index.ts` only.
- POSIX path remains signal-based; Windows uses an explicit tree terminate.
- Unit tests tagged `os:windows` cover child + grandchild cleanup.

## Verification cases

### Case 1 — Windows tree kill
- **Preconditions:** Windows host; spawn a Node/cmd child that itself spawns a grandchild that stays alive.
- **Steps:** Call `terminateTree(child)`; wait briefly; inspect process list for child and grandchild PIDs.
- **Expected / pass:** Both PIDs are gone; helper returns success/true.

### Case 2 — POSIX unchanged
- **Preconditions:** Linux or macOS.
- **Steps:** Run existing runner process-lifecycle / posix platform tests.
- **Expected / pass:** No behaviour change vs `main`; suite green.

### Case 3 — Facade only
- **Preconditions:** PR diff for this issue.
- **Steps:** Grep runner call sites for raw `taskkill` / `process.platform === \"win32\"` outside `platform/`.
- **Expected / pass:** No direct platform branches in consumer code; all go through `platform/index.ts`.

## Related

- Split from / Follow-up for PR #478 and #477 (F3.1)
- Parent: #400
items.title: [F3.2] Runner/API process tree terminate on Windows (terminateTree / taskkill)

items.author: qingkwl
items.body:
## Background

Windows 桌面端需要把原先直接调用 POSIX/Unix 语义的代码收敛到平台适配层，避免 #ifdef 散落在业务代码中。F3.1 聚焦 CAS（Concurrency Access System）相关模块的平台抽象。

## Scope

- `packages/cas`: 新增 `platform/` 目录
  - `types.ts` / `index.ts`：统一导出
  - `posix.ts` / `posix.test.ts`：现有 POSIX 行为
  - `win32.ts` / `win32.test.ts`：Windows 实现
  - `syncDirectory`：Windows 下无操作（NTFS 不支持目录 fsync）
  - `lockFileName`：生成 128-bit 摘要，避免 SQLite journal 路径超过 `MAX_PATH`
- 调整 `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`、`workspace-lease.ts`、`workspace-lifecycle.ts` 使用新的平台入口
- 新增 `workspace-lease.win32.test.ts` 回归深路径场景

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cas` 测试在 Windows 上全部通过（含新增 MAX_PATH 回归用例）
- [ ] 非 Windows 平台行为无退化
- [ ] 所有平台相关调用通过 `platform/index.ts` 导入，原文件不再直接依赖 `node:os` / `process.platform`

## Overview

This issue is the **October 2026 release calendar** for the ScienceDiscovery community. It is intended to serve as the **pinned, single source of truth** for release milestones and community review meetings.

**Key milestones**
- **Oct 10:** `v0.3.0` release kickoff and `v0.3.0-rc1` requirements review.
- **Oct 16:** `v0.3.0-rc1` release exit.
- **Oct 30:** `v0.3.0` official release exit.

## Major requirements and release scope

| Requirement | Scope | Target release(s) | Tracking issue | Owner | Review level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **CI engineering refactor** | Refactor the CI pipeline and implement the tiered testing workflow described in [#248](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/248). | `v0.3.0-rc1`, `v0.3.0` | [#248](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/248) | | Design review |

| **Documentation & official website content** | Video guides, installation docs, tutorials, and other onboarding materials; update ScienceDiscovery official website content. | `v0.3.0` | [#399](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/399) | [@nanzhaogang](https://github.com/nanzhaogang) | Design + code review |
| **System configuration & in-conversation settings / resume** | Configuration recommendations and preset questions to guide setup; in-conversation config card for supported settings, with the ability to resume the task after changes. | `v0.3.0` | [#278](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/278) | [@wyhohyw](https://github.com/wyhohyw) | Design + code review |
| **Routine bug fixes** | Regular bug fixes identified during development and regression testing. | `v0.3.0-rc1`, `v0.3.0` | | | PR review |
| **NPU task state recovery after disconnections or errors** | Recover task state/progress/results after reconnection; continue when possible; avoid duplicate submissions. | `v0.3.0` | [#398](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/398) | [@wyhohyw](https://github.com/wyhohyw) | Design + code review |
| **Recovery of failed long-running tasks** | Reuse completed results and continue from a supported recovery point after a confirmed failure; structured recovery info. | `v0.3.0` | [#401](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/401) | [@wyhohyw](https://github.com/wyhohyw) | Design + code review |
| **Build an initial automated development pipeline** | Stand up a first-pass automated development pipeline (build/test/review/integration hooks) to accelerate iteration. | `v0.3.0` | — | [@zy95-12](https://github.com/zy95-12) | Design + code review |

## October schedule

| Date | Meeting / milestone | Agenda or deliverable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-10 (Sat) | Release kickoff / requirements | v0.3.0 kickoff meeting; review requirements and scope for `v0.3.0-rc1`. |

| 2026-10-19 (Mon) | Requirements review | Review and finalize requirements for `v0.3.0`. |

## Community review meetings

The community review meetings on **Oct 13, 20, 22, and 27** cover:
- **Requirement change review** — evaluate proposed scope changes and their impact on the release.

- **Code review** — discuss implementation quality, correctness, and readiness to merge.

items.body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Strengthen the existing L1–L5 gates so that core scientific features have explicit regression protection, and introduce the full, version-pinned BiomniBench-DA suite as an L5 capability non-regression gate. Keep the existing shared catalog, frozen plans, candidate-SHA/backend identity checks, and exact execution accounting.

BiomniBench-DA should measure data-analysis capability; it must not be treated as complete coverage of Idea Tree, remote execution, provenance, Reviewer, or upgrade/recovery behavior. Those features need dedicated acceptance cases.

This is a follow-up implementation plan to #248. Its pre-merge L5 certification proposal is an explicit policy extension beyond the original release-only L5 scope. Related prerequisites: #252 (wait for the complete Biomni execution/wake chain before checking delivery) and #245 (endpoint latency and empty-terminal-turn diagnostics). Reuse those investigations rather than duplicate them. The source review used commit `e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215`; counts below describe that snapshot, not newly executed CI results. Reconcile with current main before implementation. GitHub rulesets and Environment settings were not verified in this review.

## Current coverage and gaps

- L3 declares nine real cases: response, tool, files, memory, artifact, workspace, cancellation, and two Runner wait/finish recovery cases.
- L4/L5 currently select the same 19 real identities: those nine plus five DRB cases, Research Team, PUCT compression, J5 statistics, and two run/artifact-card provenance journeys. There is no eligible L5-only increment.
- Idea Tree is **not untested**: it has Python/API/package tests and a mocked browser journey covering pause/resume, three rounds, independent assessments, persistence, and termination. The browser fixture supplies one candidate per round and fixed scores; it does not establish real-model research quality or realistic multi-branch exploration.
- Existing Reviewer and literature tests already cover several evidence, identity, lifecycle, and failure contracts. Extend their missing boundaries rather than duplicate them.
- BiomniBench-DA currently has two quarantined cases using a local rubric judge adapter. Evaluation errors are recorded as non-gating, and there is no capability threshold.
- The migration ledger lists 77 Neo4j external identities and 17 unreviewed delegation identities. Map existing replacement coverage before reinstating or retiring individual cases.
- Some public-API journeys have standalone commands but are not wired into the shared CI plan.

## L5: full BiomniBench-DA capability certification

- [ ] Define a versioned manifest for the complete intended BiomniBench-DA release: task IDs, authorized data assets/checksums, instructions, evaluator/grader version, generator and judge configuration, tools, budgets, and attempts. Missing prerequisites must not silently shrink the suite.
- [ ] Repair the current isolated-task prerequisites, then expand beyond the two existing cases to the complete manifest. Record all exclusions explicitly; do not label an incomplete run as full-suite certification.
- [ ] Decide and name the evaluation protocol. The current local rubric adapter is not the upstream Gemini verifier; scores from different protocols/judges must not be silently compared or presented as equivalent official scores.
- [ ] Emit separate `delivery`, `evaluation`, and `capability` verdicts. Required evaluation errors, missing scores, non-finite values, or mismatched identities prevent certification. Optional disabled audits must be explicitly N/A.
- [ ] Define product-failure scoring up front. Generation failures, timeouts, and missing answers cannot disappear from the denominator. Infrastructure/judge failures must remain visible as blocked/incomplete certification, not be silently converted to successful results.
- [ ] Establish an approved baseline with per-task results. Freeze comparable backend/model/judge/data/grader/tool/budget identities; do not compare against an ever-moving baseline that can gradually regress.
- [ ] Calibrate a non-inferiority rule and tolerable regression margin using repeated measurements. Preserve all attempts, use a predefined repetition/review policy, and prohibit retry-until-green or best-of-unreported-attempts reporting.
- [ ] Inspect overall capability, task-category regressions, execution success rate, and severe per-task failures. Track latency, resource usage, and cost separately from answer quality.
- [ ] Bind the verdict and retained evidence to the actual candidate SHA and relevant asset hashes. Reuse certification only when the entire declared execution identity remains applicable.
- [ ] Retain dedicated acceptance cases for core features outside DA benchmark coverage, plus previous-release-to-candidate upgrade/read/continue validation where supported.

### Agreed public-50 gate and recovery policy (2026-10-20)

This is the agreed follow-up specification, not a claim that the current PR implements or has validated every requirement below. This update changes descriptions only; no code is submitted.

#### Quality decision and comparable baseline

The operator's cross-run comparison found a maximum per-task score spread of 76 points and reported 8 tasks with spreads greater than 40 points and 9 with spreads greater than 20 points. These are operator-reported diagnostic counts; the two threshold counts must not be assumed disjoint. Given the observed per-task variability, use the arithmetic mean of all **50** task scores as the quality gate. Retain individual scores and spreads for diagnosis, without hard per-task score regression thresholds.

Compare against a reviewed, frozen public-50 baseline under comparable dataset, generator/judge, evaluator, measurement, backend, machine/resource-class, concurrency and budget configurations. Cross-machine/mixed-revision diagnostic summaries are not themselves an approved baseline. All 50 tasks must have valid delivery and scores before computing a certifying mean; do not shrink the denominator, fill missing scores with zero, or claim a pass from the completed subset.

#### Warning and blocking thresholds

Let B be the approved baseline aggregate and C the current comparable aggregate. Trigger a warning or block when the stated threshold is **reached or exceeded**; a block takes precedence over a warning. Percentage increases mean (C - B) / B, with a positive baseline required.

| Metric | Aggregation across the 50 tasks | Warning | Block |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quality score | Arithmetic mean, denominator fixed at 50 | B - C >= 3 score points | B - C >= 5 score points |
| Token consumption | Sum of generation + judge tokens; retain the two components separately | Increase >= 15% | Increase >= 25% |
| Tool rounds | Sum of recorded tool rounds; retain tool-call counts for diagnosis | Increase >= 30% | Increase >= 50% |
| Peak worker RSS | Maximum per-task sampled peak RSS, not a sum of task peaks | C - B >= max(20% of B, 1 GiB) | C - B >= max(30% of B, 2 GiB) |
| Research duration | Sum of per-task research durations, excluding preparation and judging | Increase >= 20% | Increase >= 30% |

Use metric-specific thresholds, not one shared resource-increase ratio. Keep absolute case timeouts, memory/cost budgets and completeness checks separate from these relative regression rules. Warnings remain visible; blocking thresholds prevent certification. These thresholds are an initial agreed policy to calibrate with comparable repeated runs, not statistically derived confidence bounds. A low but valid score or an exceeded resource threshold is not an execution/evaluation failure eligible for automatic retry-until-green.

#### Deferred, classified recovery: at most three retries

1. Finish the first pass over all 50 tasks before retrying failures. Preserve successful tasks and build a failed/incomplete-task inventory with stage, error, artifact completeness, attempt IDs and execution identity. Upstream LLM instability and stochastic inference motivate bounded recovery, but do not establish the cause of every failure.
2. **Research/delivery failure:** if `trace.md` and `answer.txt` were not both completely produced for the same completed research attempt, rerun that task end to end. Check completion evidence and artifact integrity, not just file existence or remnants from a previous attempt.
3. **Evaluation-only failure:** if both artifacts are complete and research delivery is verified, retry evaluation only against those saved, immutable artifacts. Do not regenerate the research result; retain artifact hashes and the research-attempt identity. Examples include judge timeout, invalid JSON, missing score or incomplete judge usage.
4. Allow **at most three additional retries after the initial attempt** (at most four attempts for a task in total). Use one per-task recovery counter across research and evaluation recovery, so changing failure stage or nesting a judge retry does not reset or multiply the limit. Stop at the first valid completed result; do not select the highest score. A successful research retry whose evaluation fails uses evaluation-only recovery for the remaining retry allowance.
5. If the task remains unresolved after three retries, locate and document the failing stage/root cause where evidence permits, then file or link a deduplicated tracking issue with the candidate SHA, task ID, attempt history, errors, artifacts and known/unknown resource usage. The suite remains failed/incomplete rather than silently passing. Creating those future tracking issues is an implementation requirement, not an action performed by this description update.

#### Evidence and cost accounting

Keep initial failures, every retry and recovery type, the final selected result, first-pass success rate and recovered completion rate. Publish comparable per-task result aggregates and the **actual whole-run cost including all failed and retried research/judge attempts** separately, so recovery cannot hide extra token usage or elapsed time. Include known retry usage in the cost/budget report; do not pool measurements with different accounting scopes into one comparison.

A timed-out request without reported usage remains unknown cost, never zero. Evaluation-only recovery may restore a valid score but cannot retroactively make earlier unknown usage complete or turn the attempt into a full E2E rerun. Do not certify resource non-regression while required accounting is incomplete; preserve separate delivery, evaluation, quality and resource-accounting verdicts. Resource aggregates selected for comparison must use the same declared retry-accounting scope as their approved baseline.

### Required trigger decision: merge gate versus release gate

The current L5 workflow is triggered after a version tag; that can block publication but cannot prevent a regression from entering main. The intended outcome here includes **pre-merge capability protection**.

- [ ] Make L5 certification callable for the final merge candidate (or a deliberately formed merge batch), and require its verdict before that candidate enters main. A rebuilt candidate must not reuse incompatible evidence.
- [ ] Retain release-time asset checks; reuse an earlier certification only with an explicit matching-identity policy.
- [ ] Document queue latency, concurrency, budget, and failure-localization behavior. If the chosen policy runs only on selected changes or only nightly, state the weaker guarantee explicitly rather than claiming every merge is fully benchmark-certified.

## L4: prioritized real scientific journeys

Priority applies to the **new L4 coverage**, not to removal of existing tests. P0 is the first implementation tranche; P1 follows once completeness and budget controls are available.

| Priority | Feature / proposed case | Observable acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | **Idea Tree: multi-branch, multi-round research with an independently computable evaluator** | Generate distinct candidates; reject hard-constraint violations; execute candidates where applicable; preserve lineage; propagate prior insights into later rounds; select a valid result using independent evidence. Do not require every exploratory round to improve monotonically. |
| **P0** | **Reviewer: paired correct and deliberately flawed reports** | Detect unsupported citations, numeric/unit errors, and evidence from the wrong run/version; avoid false accusations on correct reports; return inconclusive when evidence is insufficient. Measure false positives as well as missed defects. |
| **P0** | **Scientific calculation / J5: fixed-data analysis with an independent numerical oracle** | Persist reproducible computation and verify report values, units, and evidence against independently calculated expectations, rather than merely requiring a Markdown artifact. |
| **P1** | **Literature research: retrieval → acquisition → extraction → citation → report** | Verify source identity and evidence support; exercise representative live connector/PDF paths with bounded budgets. Keep deterministic source/failure fixtures in L2 and distinguish provider availability from product defects. |
| **P1** | **Multi-agent research: successful, failed, and delayed child tasks** | Preserve task/result identity; surface partial failure; propagate cancellation; avoid duplicate dispatch and missing results; prevent an unsupported “all succeeded” final conclusion. Extend existing Research Team coverage. |
| **P1** | **Evolve/PUCT: independently evaluated candidate optimization** | Verify candidate/parent/baseline identity, legitimate selection, and validation/test separation; invalid or failed evaluations cannot win. Keep seed-as-best valid; do not require arbitrary improvement in every run. |

For all cases, enter through the product's public interfaces, record model/backend identity and usage, enforce explicit execution budgets, and retain auditable evidence. Generating a score is not itself a passing capability verdict.

## L1–L3: close engineering and integration gaps

### L1: trustworthy policy and manifests

- [ ] Add independent validation of CI-sensitive changes against a trusted base. A change must not weaken selectors/gates and their self-tests together without detection; legitimate policy changes need an explicit review path. Unknown impact must fail or fall back to the full intended plan.
- [ ] Validate benchmark manifest schema, unique IDs, frozen inputs, required evaluation fields, and explicit exclusions.
- [ ] Restore appropriate dependency-vulnerability, secret, and static-security checks that are not replaced by the current test gate.
- [ ] Verify repository administration separately: required `merge-gate`, Merge Queue, current-head review/stale-approval dismissal, and permitted Environment refs. YAML presence is not proof that these are enforced.

### L2: deterministic product and scientific contracts

- [ ] Register suitable existing public-API journeys in the shared catalog, especially remote execution wake-up, detached Runner behavior, and memory/provenance journeys. Preserve isolated processes/data and planned/executed accounting.
- [ ] Add a reproducible temporary Neo4j integration job for the applicable external identities; local-backend tests are not a substitute for Neo4j behavior.
- [ ] Map the 17 unreviewed delegation identities to current Swarm coverage; restore missing behaviors or explicitly document verified replacements.
- [ ] Extend Idea Tree mocked E2E to multiple branches with good, weak, and invalid candidates, pruning, failure recovery, and final selection assertions.
- [ ] Test evaluation aggregation with injected judge timeouts, missing/invalid scores, wrong versions, and missing tasks. No incomplete evaluation may produce full certification.
- [ ] Test suite request/token budget enforcement, including retries, children, judges, cancellation, and unknown usage. Existing context or feature-local budgets do not establish a suite-wide cost ceiling.
- [ ] Extend literature/Reviewer fixtures with wrong pages, unsupported citations, unit errors, cross-session/version evidence, and correct counterexamples. Consider sanitized HTTP replay with CI auto-recording disabled; keep online freshness checks separate.
- [ ] Verify remote success and recovery: input transfer, execution in separate storage, artifact return, completion wake-up, no duplicate execution after reconnect, and no orphan work after cancellation.
- [ ] Verify full provenance from input version through code/environment/execution to report; same-named files in different sessions must not mix, and old reports must not silently point to new versions.
- [ ] Audit existing process-recovery tests and add missing actual API/Runner/Swarm restart journeys. Browser refresh and session reopening do not establish server recovery.

### L3: small real-model and distribution acceptance

- [ ] Add a bounded real-model smoke for critical feature entry points such as Idea Tree; leave deep research and quality evaluation to L4/L5.
- [ ] Exercise critical upload → execution → artifact-read behavior against the actual distribution candidate. Preserve the existing two-architecture binary and Docker gates and publish the assets that were tested.
- [ ] Apply explicit paid-call budgets to the merge-candidate suite without weakening identity or failure accounting.

## Follow-up coverage audits

- [ ] Define supported-platform obligations before adding macOS, real SSH, NPU, R, or additional dependency matrices. Do not infer coverage from Linux/amd64 tests or arm64 boot smoke.
- [ ] Audit long-running concurrency, process cleanup, and upgrade/migration tests before adding duplicates.
- [ ] Maintain a feature × tier × failure-mode coverage map linked to case IDs, so “has unit tests” is not mistaken for “has real scientific acceptance.”
- [ ] Add deduplicated nightly failure tracking, ownership, recovery handling, and sufficient release-evidence retention.

## Completion criteria and rollout

1. Make results trustworthy first: frozen manifests, evaluation-completeness contracts, budget controls, baseline protocol, and required-check configuration.
2. Bring suitable existing journeys and external integration tests into routine CI; resolve delegation coverage mapping.
3. Land L4 P0 cases, then P1 enhancements, reusing existing fixtures and assertions where appropriate.
4. Enable full L5 certification on the intended pre-merge candidate, with calibrated non-regression rules and artifact-bound release evidence.

Acceptance must include deliberate fault injection: a missing selected task, judge failure, invalid winning candidate, mismatched fingerprint, exceeded budget, or weakened selection policy must not produce a green certification. Selection-only checks are not evidence that the complete suite executed successfully.

## Source anchors for the reviewed snapshot

- [Profiles and selection](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs)
- [Tier gate](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/.ci/tier-policy.mjs)
- [CI workflow](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [Existing Idea Tree browser journey](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/journey-idea-tree-fixture.spec.ts)
- [Existing Biomni cases and non-gating evaluation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts)
- [Migration and excluded identities](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215/test/support/tagged/MIGRATION.md)

items.body:
## Summary

When the runtime data directory's absolute path is 88 bytes or longer, the sandbox egress gateway cannot bind its Unix socket and **every** `run_shell` fails before any command executes — including a bare `echo`. The Runner still reports `ready: true` and `sandboxNetwork.available: true`, so the failure only appears per execution, inside the tool result, and the agent cannot tell whether the sandbox or its own command is at fault.

On Linux the limit leaves 87 bytes for the data directory; on macOS 83. A checkout whose path is already deep (for example a handoff/archive directory several levels below `$HOME`) reaches 88 bytes with the default `<repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data` and fails by exactly one byte.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery `54263a4c` (native local mode, `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local --no-build --no-jiuwenswarm`), Linux, bubblewrap sandbox.
- Sandbox network access: global settings `mode: "open"` (also reproducible with `domain-allowlist`).
- Runner data directory: `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` = `<repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data`, absolute length 88 bytes.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Place the checkout so that `<absolute repository root>/.sciencediscovery-data` is **88 bytes or longer** (equivalently, set `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` to an 88+ byte absolute path):

   ```bash
   printf %s "$PWD/.sciencediscovery-data" | wc -c   # 88 or more → reproduces
   ```

2. Start the stack and enable sandbox network access (`open` or `domain-allowlist`) so a session's tool calls need egress.
3. In a session, run any shell command — a trivial `echo` is enough.
4. Observe: every `run_shell` fails with `status: "failed"`, empty stdout, and the same stderr, e.g.

   ```
   Sandbox network access (domain-allowlist and open) is unavailable: the egress socket path is 108 bytes,
   over this platform's 107-byte Unix socket path limit — <dataDir>/eg/<16 hex>.
   The socket has to stay inside the runner data directory, so shorten that directory by at least 1 byte(s)
   (SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR); it must leave 20 bytes for the socket itself.
   ```

5. `GET /health` on the runner and the `check_runner` tool both still report `sandboxUsable: true` / `sandboxNetwork.available: true`, and `sandboxNetwork.modes` still lists `domain-allowlist` and `open`.

## Code path

- `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.ts` — `MAX_UNIX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES` (107 Linux / 103 macOS), `EGRESS_SOCKET_RELATIVE_BYTES = 20` (`/eg/` + 16-hex digest name), `EgressGatewayRegistry.socketPath()`, and `assertUnixSocketPathFits()` called at the top of `EgressGateway.listen()`. The socket path is therefore `dataDir` length + 20, and a data directory of 88 bytes yields 108 > 107.
- `services/runner/src/executor.ts` — `prepareSandboxEgress()` calls `gateways.acquire()` on the launch path for any `domain-allowlist` / `open` execution, so the failure is charged to every execution, not only the ones that use the network.
- `services/runner/src/server.ts` — `sandboxNetworkCapability()` probes only the egress bridge's host Python interpreter. It never measures the socket path, so the capability report and `/health` claim the modes are available while every execution fails.
- `services/launcher/src/preflight.ts` / `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` — likewise check only sandbox usability (bwrap options, user namespaces), not the socket path.
- Default data directory: `.env` → `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR=.sciencediscovery-data`, resolved against the repository root in `scripts/start-stack.sh`.

## Why this is reported as a bug

- The constraint "the runtime data directory must be ≤ 87 bytes (Linux) / ≤ 83 bytes (macOS)" is real but is documented nowhere, and nothing at startup warns about it. The default layout silently depends on how deep the checkout sits.
- The failure is discovered per execution rather than at startup, and the only surface that knows the reason (`/health`, `check_runner`) reports the opposite (`available: true`). In our run the agent spent its turns proving the sandbox was broken and could not open a repair card for the blocker, so an antibody-design session ended with zero commands executed.
- Because the launch path needs the gateway for *any* command, an over-long path does not degrade network access — it takes the whole Runner offline while it still advertises itself as healthy. The preflight code already states this failure mode for bubblewrap options: reporting success from a launch the runner would refuse "is exactly the mismatch that let the service look healthy while every tool call failed".

## Suggested direction

1. Report the socket-path condition in the capability/health surface: `sandboxNetworkCapability()` (and the launcher preflight) should measure `socketPath("")` for the configured data directory and return `available: false` with the byte counts, so the blocker is visible before a session starts.
2. Fail loudly at startup: `scripts/start-stack.sh` (and the single-file launcher) should refuse to start, or warn with the exact shortfall, when the resolved data directory exceeds the platform limit.
3. Document the limit next to `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` in `docs/{en,zh}/reference/configuration.md`, since it is a hard deployment constraint.
4. Optionally decouple the socket path from the install location — keep the digest-of-revision identity but root the socket directory in a short, runner-owned runtime path (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or a 0700 directory the runner creates and verifies ownership of) so a deep checkout is not a functional constraint.

Short term, pointing `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR` at a short path (a symlink keeps the existing 2 GB of state and the absolute paths baked into `envs/` valid) unblocks the Runner.

## Impact

Total loss of code execution on an affected host for every session, with a misleading "Runner is ready" signal; no workaround is reachable from inside a session (the agent cannot change the host's data directory).
items.title: [Bug]: A deep data directory breaks the egress socket path, so every run_shell fails while the Runner reports ready
