## Summary
From an ease-of-use perspective, **review / citation verification should turn on and run automatically when the task needs it**, instead of finishing the research run and expecting the user to trigger a separate review pass.

## Observed behavior
On a basic literature-research run (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0):

- Session had `reviewMode: auto` and `semanticReviewEnabled: true`.
- Enabled skills for the run were only `literature-searcher`, `evidence-extractor`, and `report-writer` — **`citation-reviewer` was not in the enabled skill set**.
- Run completed with report artifacts, but event stream showed **no `review.*` events** and **no citation-reviewer / dedicated semantic-review pass**.
- The agent only did informal metadata cross-checks via `web_search` during synthesis.

So “review is configured on” did not mean “review verification actually ran as part of the same task.”

## Why this is a usability problem
Users reasonably expect that if review is enabled (or the task type clearly needs verification — e.g. literature survey with claims/citations), the product **runs verification inside the same workflow** and surfaces pass/fail or review findings with the deliverable.

Having to notice that review didn’t run and then start another trigger breaks the “set and forget” experience and makes trust in the report harder.

## Expected behavior
When review is enabled (`reviewMode: auto` / `semanticReviewEnabled: true`) **or** when the workflow produces citation-backed claims / literature artifacts:

1. Automatically include / invoke the appropriate review path (e.g. `citation-reviewer` or semantic review) **in the same run**.
2. Surface a clear review result (passed / issues found / skipped with reason) next to the main artifacts — not only after a manual second kick.
3. If review cannot run (skill missing, connectors unavailable, etc.), make that **visible in the UI/run status**, not silent completion.

## Suggested direction (non-prescriptive)
- Treat review as a **default post-synthesis gate** for literature / evidence workflows when settings say auto.
- Or auto-enable `citation-reviewer` (and any required review skills) when those settings are on, so skill selection can’t silently omit verification.
- Make “review ran vs skipped” an explicit run outcome field users can see without digging into events.

## Environment / repro sketch
- Product: ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Task: basic CRISPR / SCD literature research
- Settings observed: `reviewMode: auto`, `semanticReviewEnabled: true`
- Outcome: report artifacts produced; no dedicated review pass in the same run

## Labeling
Usability / enhancement — not claiming a hard functional bug in the settings schema, but a product gap between “review configured” and “review actually executed when needed.”
closed_recent.title: Usability: auto-run review verification when needed (don’t require a second user trigger)

## Summary

Docs describe adding a **custom MCP server**, but ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0** has no settings surface for it and the documented HTTP routes return **404**. End-to-end custom MCP cannot be demoed on this binary.

closed_recent.body:
## Summary
During a literature-research run, the session timeline stays visually frozen on parallel tool cards that only say **Tool is running…** / **Running** for several minutes. There is no incremental progress (queries tried, sources failed, papers found so far), so the product feels stuck even though the run is still working.

## Observed behavior
On a CRISPR / SCD literature demo (ScienceDiscovery 0.2.0, screen recording ~7 min raw):

- Two parallel `task` / tool-call cards stayed on `Tool is running…` with a spinner.
- Roughly **3+ minutes** of the recording had almost no visual change in the main pane.
- The only extra cue was a sidebar tooltip such as `PubMed search: CRISPR SCD clinical · running`, not a progress update in the task itself.
- The run eventually completed and wrote a report; it was not a hard freeze.

## Why this is a usability problem
Users cannot tell “still working” from “stuck”. A literature search that fans out to subagents needs staged status (started search, source unavailable, N records so far, synthesizing) instead of a single indefinite spinner.

## Expected behavior
While a tool or subagent is running:

1. Show a short, updating status in the task card (phase + last meaningful event), not only “Tool is running…”.
2. Prefer human-readable progress over raw subagent paths / token counters as the primary signal.
3. If a source fails (connector missing, network denied), surface that failure in the running card instead of waiting until the final report.

## Not the same as
- Connector tools silently omitted when enabled (#325) — that is a functional bug.
- Sandbox egress should ask for permission (#324) — different ask.
- Empty-state copy that mentions CSV/charts on a literature session — separate copy issue.

## Environment
- ScienceDiscovery linux prepackaged binary 0.2.0
- Task: short PubMed/arXiv literature survey
- Evidence: session screen recording; main pane static while tools report Running

closed_recent.body:
## Summary

Product `web_fetch` on clearly public HTTPS URLs (e.g. `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/...`, `https://export.arxiv.org/...`, Europe PMC) fails with `INVALID_INPUT` and the message **"local and private network URLs are not allowed"**. That string is produced by the control-plane SSRF guard when DNS resolution returns no addresses or any blocked address — so public hosts are being **misclassified** (or DNS failure is labeled as “private”), not correctly blocked as private SSRF targets.

This is **distinct** from Session MCP connector exposure ([#325](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/325)): `web_fetch` is the global Web capability (vendor fetch via Jina/Tavily/Exa), not the PubMed/arXiv MCP path.

## Repro

1. ScienceDiscovery **0.2.0**, Session with Web tools available (`web` connector / product `web_fetch`).
2. Agent calls `web_fetch` with a public literature URL, e.g.:
   - `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<pmid>/`
   - `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?...`
   - Europe PMC article HTTPS URLs
3. Tool returns `INVALID_INPUT` with *"local and private network URLs are not allowed"* (and/or the same text in the attempt error).

Observed alongside literature run `dad3a25d…` (session `27148ad0…`) when MCP literature tools were also missing.

## Expected

- Public, globally routable HTTP(S) hostnames that resolve to public address space must pass `assertPublicUrl` and proceed to the configured fetch provider (default Jina Reader, etc.).
- DNS **failure** / unresolvable host must return a distinct, actionable error (e.g. host could not be resolved), **not** the private-network SSRF message.
- Loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / ULA / multicast rejection remains correct for true SSRF cases.

## Actual

Public literature URLs fail with the private-network message before (or instead of) a normal upstream fetch attempt.

## Code path (path is correct; classification / messaging is wrong)

Documented in `docs/en/reference/web-tools.md`:

```text
Agent web_fetch
  → packages/data-source/src/web/workspace-tools.ts (workspace binding)
  → packages/data-source/src/web/broker.ts  WebBroker.fetch
       - parses URL, requires http(s), no credentials
       - permission.requirePrivilege({ action: "host", resource: hostname })
  → NativeWebProviderClient.invoke (packages/data-source/src/web/native/index.ts)
       - await assertPublicUrl(input.request)   ← failure mapped to WebProviderError(..., "invalid-input")
  → fetchJina / fetchTavily / fetchExa (packages/data-source/src/web/native/fetch.ts)
       - outbound to vendor endpoints from config/external-urls.json (`web.jina_endpoints`, etc.)
```

SSRF guard: `packages/data-source/src/web/native/url-guard.ts` → `assertPublicUrl`:

- Rejects non-http(s), credentials, `localhost`.
- Resolves hostname via `dns.promises.lookup(..., { all: true })`.
- Throws `PublicUrlError("local and private network URLs are not allowed")` when:
  - `addresses.length === 0` (**DNS failure / empty result — same message as private**), or
  - `addresses.some(isBlockedAddress)` (any resolved address in private/loopback/link-local/ULA/multicast/etc.).

Broker maps `invalid-input` → product `INVALID_INPUT` (`packages/data-source/src/web/broker.ts` `invocationError`).

## Why public URLs can hit this

Likely causes (environment + guard semantics):

1. **DNS lookup failed or returned no records** on the API/control-plane host → empty `addresses` → identical “private network” error (misleading).
2. **Over-strict multi-address policy**: if *any* A/AAAA record is blocked, the whole URL is rejected even when a public address also exists.
3. Broken/sinkhole DNS returning private/ULA for external names (true SSRF-style resolution — message would then be accurate, but operators still need clearer diagnostics).

**Not** the sandbox network allowlist (`SandboxNetworkSettings` / bubblewrap): product Web runs on the Node control plane and uses Web proxy settings / vendor endpoints. Connector `networkHosts` apply to MCP governance URL checks, not to `assertPublicUrl`.

## Impact

- Agents cannot open public paper landing pages / API URLs via `web_fetch` when DNS or classification fails, even though `web_search` may still work.
- Error text steers debugging toward “private network / SSRF” instead of DNS, proxy, or dual-stack resolution.

## Suggested fix direction (non-prescriptive)

- Split error messages: unresolvable vs non-public address vs localhost literal.
- Log resolved addresses (or failure reason) on the WebInvocation attempt for supportability.
- Revisit `addresses.some(isBlockedAddress)` vs requiring at least one public address / family policy.
- Add regression tests for: public hostname resolving to public IPv4; DNS empty; mixed public+ULA; literal `127.0.0.1`.

## Related

- [#325](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/325) — Session-enabled arXiv/PubMed MCP tools not injected (separate root cause; literature should prefer MCP, not `web_fetch`).

## Labels

bug, needs triage

# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **全面拥抱 jiuwen-swarm 后端的第一个 Beta 版本**：保留科研工作台体验，以 jiuwen-swarm 支撑 Agent 执行，在新架构上整合科研专属能力。

本 issue 用于征集社区对 Release Note、发布范围及阻塞问题的反馈，**不是正式发布公告**。上一版本为 `0.2.0`；建议版本号为 **`0.3.0-beta.1`（待确认）**，开发主线为 `main`（原 JiuwenSwarm 分支已切换为主线），本次发版分支为 `releases/v0.3.0.beta`。

## Release Note 草案

### 重点支持场景

本版本重点保障以下四类场景，不追求一次性迁移全部历史能力或覆盖所有边界情况。

| 场景 | 主要流程与交付 | Domain 文档 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 文献调研 | 检索与获取文献、提取证据、多专家协作，交付带可追溯引用的调研报告 | [文献调研教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md) |
| 数据分析 | 读取数据、准备环境、执行分析，交付可复现代码、图表与结论 | [脓毒症数据分析教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/analyze-sepsis-endotypes.md) |
| 抗体设计 | 结合领域 Skill、专业模型和科研环境完成设计与筛选；依赖相应模型资源与算力，计算结果不等同于实验验证 | [抗体设计教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/antibody-design.md) |
| 算法优化 | 通过科研产物 RSI / Evolve 生成候选、执行评估与迭代，保留结果与过程记录 | [算法优化教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md) |

### 核心功能与改进

- **统一 JiuwenSwarm 默认后端**：源码、Docker 和发行包启动器均默认选择 JiuwenSwarm；保留显式 native 切换。主子 Agent 默认通过平台 `task` 委派、由 Swarm 执行，并非全面切换为 Swarm 原生多 Agent 编排。
- **科研执行环境与工作区**：支持本地/远程执行、托管环境、后台任务、文件传递、工作区交接及产物版本关联。
- **记忆图谱**：记录科研任务、文件与产物关系，支持引用追溯；源码及 Docker 部署提供默认本地存储，可选 Neo4j。
- **科研 Skill、MCP 与 Specialist**：支持内置能力和自定义扩展，组合专业专家完成科研任务。
- **科研产物 RSI 与 Idea Tree**：支持产物迭代优化、候选评估和研究思路的树状探索。
- **可观测性与测试**：完善执行轨迹、子任务状态和错误诊断，补充 Mock E2E、真实科研 Benchmark 与质量评估记录。
- **文档与入门体验**：整理中英文文档和四类场景教程，明确 Swarm/native 在上下文、规划、工具、Skill 等方面的行为差异。

这些功能包含已有能力的迁移与增强，并非全部首次引入。

### 官网、社区与交付配套（本版本新增）

- **统一对外网站**：提供[官网与安装入口](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html)，集中展示安装指引、使用文档与科研场景教程；网站内容随 `main` 分支同步更新。
- **用户交流社区**：面向海外与中国用户，分别建立 **Slack** 和 **飞书**用户交流群，用于使用交流、问题反馈与社区协作；加入方式见仓库首页。
- **双分支每日 CI**：构建每日质量检查，覆盖 `main` 和 `releases/v0.3.0.beta`。由 main 的定时任务触发两条分支各自的检查，分别保留结果、日志和构建产物，为主线演进与版本发布提供持续质量反馈。
- **多平台、多种安装方式**：支持 Linux、macOS，Windows 可通过 WSL 2 使用；提供源码、Linux 二进制发行包及 Docker 等部署方式。不同系统可用的安装方式与前置条件不同，详见[官网安装页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html)。

### 主要 Bugfix

- **记忆图谱内存与查询性能**：修复折叠查询的路径爆炸，使用共享路径及累计集合预算，避免已复现的高内存分配；超预算返回结构化错误。优化会话索引查询，避免大量无关历史数据拖累新会话（#212，修复 #210）。
- **启动行为一致性**：修复源码与 Docker/发行包默认后端不一致，确保命令行后端选项优先于 `.env`；Docker 转发 Swarm 配置，E2E 显式选择后端（#214）。
- **Swarm/MCP 隔离与恢复**：改进模型、会话、工具绑定隔离，工具刷新、共享连接和权限生命周期（#173、#181、#182）。
- **子任务与远程执行可靠性**：改进并发排队、超时、取消、工作区交接和子 Agent 恢复；远程执行状态查询增加瞬时错误重试（#182、#187、#191）。
- **模型输出与事件流**：改进截断输出恢复，避免执行不完整工具参数，增强工具事件流存活与诊断（#190、#194）。
- **科研数据与交付**：改进 PDF 校验、arXiv 接入兼容性、产物版本关联，以及界面状态、快照作用域和取消诊断（#171、#180、#192、#179、#189、#193）。

## Beta 边界与升级说明

- **Nightly Real E2E 尚不稳定**：自动真实模型 E2E CI 仍在稳定化过程中，当前真实科研场景的验收以本地实际执行并保留记录的结果为准，需注明被测提交、模型和配置。Nightly 结果作为辅助诊断，不单独作为版本质量已达标的依据；跳过或隔离的用例不视为通过。UT/ST/Mock E2E 门禁仍是独立的质量依据。
- **部分安装路径为实验特性**：macOS Docker 以及所有 Windows 安装路径（包括 WSL 2 和 Docker Desktop）尚未全面验证 Agent 执行效果。当前预编译单文件包面向 Linux，不提供原生 macOS/Windows 二进制；macOS 优先使用源码方式，Windows 的 Linux 二进制/源码方式需在 WSL 2 内运行。具体支持范围与依赖见官网安装页。
- **官网与发行版的差异**：官网跟随 main，可能包含尚未进入本次 Beta 的更新；本版本的准确行为与限制以发行分支文档和最终 Release Note 为准。
- **场景验收与效果边界**：四类场景是重点验收范围，效果仍受模型、网络、数据源和算力影响；测试已加入不代表所有真实场景已稳定通过，发布以最终候选版本验收为准。
- **Swarm 初始化与后端切换**：源码首次使用 Swarm 前执行 `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`。保留原生循环可使用 `--no-jiuwenswarm` 或 `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native`。
- **记忆图谱升级与故障处理**：升级不会覆盖已保存的记忆功能设置；此前手动关闭的用户需在系统设置中重新开启。已有图谱可通过 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` 指向原目录，不自动迁移。设置 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0` 可跳过服务；该可选服务启动失败时会报告原因并在禁用图谱的情况下继续启动，修正后需重启。
- **外部数据源限制**：arXiv 406/429、排队超时等外部数据源问题仍由 #208 跟踪。

## 社区反馈

请反馈：版本定位与版本号是否合适、功能或修复有无遗漏、四类场景是否存在发布阻塞，以及哪些限制必须写入正式说明。问题反馈请附配置、复现步骤及日志。

# English version

## Release positioning

This is ScienceDiscovery’s **first Beta release embracing the jiuwen-swarm backend**. It retains the scientific workbench experience, uses jiuwen-swarm for Agent execution, and integrates science-specific capabilities into the new architecture.

This issue collects community feedback on the release notes, scope, and blockers; **it is not a release announcement**. The previous version is `0.2.0`. The proposed version is **`0.3.0-beta.1` (to be confirmed)**, with development on `main` (the former JiuwenSwarm branch) and this release prepared from `releases/v0.3.0.beta`.

## Draft release notes

### Priority scenarios

This Beta focuses on four scientific workflows rather than migrating every historical capability or covering every corner case.

| Scenario | Workflow and deliverables | Domain documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literature review | Search and retrieve literature, extract evidence, collaborate across specialists, and deliver a report with traceable citations | [Literature research tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/literature-research.md) |
| Data analysis | Inspect data, prepare an environment, execute analysis, and deliver reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | [Sepsis data analysis tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/analyze-sepsis-endotypes.md) |
| Antibody design | Combine domain Skills, specialized models, and scientific environments for design and screening; requires appropriate model resources and compute, and computational results do not constitute experimental validation | [Antibody design tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/antibody-design.md) |
| Algorithm optimization | Generate, evaluate, and iterate on candidates through scientific-artifact RSI / Evolve, retaining results and execution records | [Evolve a solution tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md) |

### Core capabilities and improvements

- **Consistent JiuwenSwarm default**: source, Docker, and packaged launchers now select JiuwenSwarm by default, with an explicit native opt-out. Subagents default to platform `task` delegation with Swarm execution—not a complete switch to Swarm-native multi-agent orchestration.
- **Scientific environments and workspaces**: local/remote execution, managed environments, background tasks, file transfers, workspace handoffs, and artifact-version associations.
- **Memory graph**: research-task, file, and artifact relationships with traceable citations; source and Docker deployments provide local storage by default, with optional Neo4j.
- **Scientific Skills, MCP, and Specialists**: built-in capabilities and custom extensions for domain-expert collaboration.
- **Scientific-artifact RSI and Idea Tree**: iterative artifact optimization, candidate evaluation, and tree-based exploration of research ideas.
- **Observability and testing**: improved trajectories, subtask status, and diagnostics, alongside Mock E2E, real scientific benchmarks, and quality-evaluation records.
- **Documentation and onboarding**: reorganized English/Chinese documentation and tutorials for the four workflows, with explicit Swarm/native differences in context, planning, tools, and Skills.

These include migrations and enhancements of existing capabilities, not exclusively new features.

### Website, community, and delivery infrastructure (new in this release)

- **Unified public website**: the [website and installation hub](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) bring together installation guidance, documentation, and scientific workflow tutorials. Website content is kept in sync with `main`.
- **User communities**: **Slack** and **Feishu** groups have been established for international and China-based users respectively, supporting usage discussions, feedback, and community collaboration. See the repository homepage for joining instructions.
- **Daily CI for both branches**: daily quality checks cover `main` and `releases/v0.3.0.beta`. The scheduled main workflow triggers independent runs for both branches, retaining separate results, logs, and build artifacts to support development and release validation.
- **Multiple platforms and installation options**: Linux and macOS are supported, with Windows access through WSL 2. Options include source installation, Linux binary packages, and Docker. Availability and prerequisites vary by platform; see the [installation hub](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html).

### Major fixes

- **Memory-graph query performance and memory use**: eliminate path explosion in folded queries, introduce shared paths and cumulative collection budgets for reproduced allocation failures, and return structured budget errors. Indexed session queries avoid scanning unrelated historical data (#212, fixes #210).
- **Consistent startup behavior**: align source defaults with Docker/packages, make CLI backend selection override `.env`, forward Swarm settings through Docker, and select E2E backends explicitly (#214).
- **Swarm/MCP isolation and recovery**: improve model/session/tool binding isolation, tool refresh, shared connections, and permission lifecycle (#173, #181, #182).
- **Subtask and remote-execution reliability**: improve admission queues, timeouts, cancellation, workspace handoffs, and subagent resumption; retry transient remote execution-status failures (#182, #187, #191).
- **Model output and event streams**: recover from output truncation without executing incomplete tool arguments, and improve tool-stream liveness and diagnostics (#190, #194).
- **Scientific data and delivery**: improve PDF validation, arXiv compatibility, artifact-version associations, UI state, snapshot scope, and cancellation diagnostics (#171, #180, #192, #179, #189, #193).

## Beta limitations and upgrade notes

- **Nightly Real E2E is not yet stable**: automated real-model E2E CI is still being stabilized. For now, acceptance of real scientific workflows relies on recorded local runs, identifying the tested commit, model, and configuration. Nightly results provide supplementary diagnostics, not standalone proof of release readiness. Skipped or quarantined cases are not passes; UT/ST/Mock E2E gates remain independent quality evidence.
- **Some installation paths are experimental**: macOS Docker and all Windows paths (including WSL 2 and Docker Desktop) have not been fully validated for Agent execution. Current prepackaged single-file binaries target Linux, not native macOS or Windows. Prefer source installation on macOS; Linux binaries/source installation on Windows run inside WSL 2. Consult the installation hub for platform-specific requirements and support boundaries.
- **Website versus release documentation**: the website follows main and may describe updates not yet included in this Beta. Use the release-branch documentation and final release notes for the exact behavior and limitations of this version.
- **Workflow acceptance and outcome limitations**: The four workflows are priority acceptance targets. Outcomes depend on the model, network, data sources, and compute. Having tests does not establish that all real scenarios pass reliably; release acceptance must use the final candidate.
- **Swarm setup and backend selection**: Before first using Swarm from source, run `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`. Use `--no-jiuwenswarm` or `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native` to retain the native loop.
- **Memory-graph upgrades and failure handling**: Upgrades preserve saved memory preferences; users who previously disabled memory must re-enable it in System Settings. Use `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` to retain an existing graph directory; data is not migrated automatically. Set `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0` to skip the service. If this optional service fails to start, the launcher reports the cause and continues with memory disabled; correct the cause and restart.
- **External data-source limitations**: External-source failures, including arXiv 406/429 responses and queue timeouts, remain tracked in #208.

## Community feedback

Please comment on release positioning/versioning, missing features or fixes, blockers in the four workflows, and limitations that must appear in the final notes. Include configuration, reproduction steps, and logs for reported problems.

---

依据 / Basis: [0.2.0 → releases/v0.3.0.beta](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/compare/0.2.0...releases/v0.3.0.beta). Updated against `17d0774a` on 2026-09-27, including merged PRs #212 and #214. To be refreshed against the final release candidate.

2026-09-29：补充官网、Slack/飞书社区、双分支每日 CI、多平台安装与相关边界说明。 / Added website, Slack/Feishu communities, dual-branch daily CI, installation options, and associated limitations.

closed_recent.body:
Re-running a GitHub Actions job leaves the previous attempt's artifact in the same workflow run. `actions/download-artifact` resolves an exact name to one package, and that package can be the older attempt.

This showed up on PR #295, workflow run [38526631198](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38526631198). The first UT attempt failed one test and uploaded `ut-coverage` at 07:30 with manifest `status: FAIL` (3821 passed, 1 failed). UT was re-run and passed, uploading a second `ut-coverage` at 07:47. Coverage then ran with `needs.ut.result=success` but read the 07:30 package. `scripts/coverage-report.mjs` treats "the job passed, but the manifest is not PASS" as incomplete coverage and exits 1.

`upload-artifact@v4` does not replace an existing name unless `overwrite: true`. The same lookup applies to every artifact a later job downloads by exact name (`st-coverage`, `mocked-e2e-plan`, `real-e2e-plan`).

Coverage is not a required status check. `main` requires only `merge-gate`, which does not include Coverage, so this red job does not block merge. It does report the wrong run.

## Acceptance

- A successful re-run of UT replaces `ut-coverage`, so Coverage reads that attempt's manifest.
- The same replacement applies to the other artifacts a later job downloads by exact name.
- A contract test fails if a workflow downloads an artifact by exact name and the matching upload omits `overwrite: true`.

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
TC-E2E-01's delivery checker rejects numbered Markdown section headings even when the report contains all three requested sections. The prompt, managed extension, and checker should agree on optional section numbering so a valid report does not trigger a formatting-only rewrite.

## Reproduction

Pass this report to `checkDeliverable` in `test/fixtures/deliverable-check.mjs`:

```markdown
## 3. Methods
## 4. Results
## 9. References
```

Current result: `ok: false`, with `missing: ["Methods", "Results", "References"]`. Expected: `ok: true`.

The checker extracts ATX headings outside fenced code blocks, then compares each entire lowercased title to the required name. It compares `3. methods` to `methods` and therefore rejects the numbered section. The user prompt requests the three section names without excluding numbering, while the report-writer's default template uses numbered headings when formatting is unspecified.

## Observed impact

In Nightly [38318935663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38318935663), research-10's `deliverable_check` reported all three sections missing at `03:53:39Z` even though the report used the numbered headings above. A further report-writer task was dispatched at `03:55:57Z` and cancelled at `03:57:06Z`; total generation was 3,308,937 ms against the 3,300,000 ms budget. The prior report-writing task took about 516 seconds, so the remaining time could not accommodate another similar rewrite.

This does not establish that heading normalization alone makes every full research run finish within its budget. A successful longer research path in Nightly [38170922621](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38170922621) completed delivery in 50.2 minutes. The requested change preserves the existing 55-minute CI budget and 60-minute local default.

## Acceptance

- Count only ATX headings outside fenced code blocks.
- Accept both `## Methods` and `## 3. Methods`, likewise Results and References.
- Remove at most one leading section number matching `^\d+(?:\.\d+)*[.)]?\s+`, then require an exact, case-insensitive section-name match. Preserve trailing `#` stripping.
- Reject `## Methods and materials`, `## 3. Methodology`, prose mentions, and fenced-code examples.
- Apply the same rule in the user prompt, managed extension, MCP tool description, and checker. Have the coordinator pass the rule verbatim in the report-writer's Format Expectation instead of falling back to the default seven-section template.
- Add unit coverage, including the three numbered headings from the failed report; preserve existing negative cases.

This is separate from #239, which tracks how a still-running run is classified when its budget expires. Do not close that issue or change timeout classification in this fix. The report-writer's default template and both generation-budget values are outside scope.
closed_recent.title: test(e2e): delivery signoff rejects valid numbered report sections

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
Nightly real E2E skips J5 while the managed Python base is still in its normal install phase. The gate then counts that skip as a failed shard.

## What happened

Scheduled Nightly run [38318935663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38318935663) (main `b0a25b4c555fe75c9a44ddd942817600f6821510`, 2026-10-13) failed job Gate / Real E2E (research-9). The only identity in that shard is:

`playwright:test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` — `J5 真实请求生成统计结果并交付 Markdown`

The skip reason was:

`BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (installing: Creating the managed Python base environment)`

The real-model credentials were present. The same night, the other real cases passed except research-10, which failed for a separate delivery-budget reason. J5 itself passed on the 2026-10-09 dispatch (37875334064), both 2026-10-10 runs (38041373183 and 38081832760), and the 2026-10-11 schedule (38170922621).

## Why the skip is a race

`Creating the managed Python base environment` is the normal `creating-python-base` phase while the runner installs the managed Python base (Python 3.12 plus the pinned scientific packages). The HTTP server is already accepting requests, so `GET /health` succeeds and `GET /api/environment-setup` returns `state=installing` until that install finishes. The GET does not start the install and does not wait for it.

J5 observed that status once and called `testInfo.skip` whenever `state` was not `ready`. Real E2E requires every planned identity to execute, so a skip fails the shard (`SHARD_FAILED`, and the identity is `NOT_RUN`).

Mocked journeys keep an immediate readiness assertion. Only this real journey should wait, and a `failed` install or a deadline that still shows `installing` must stay BLOCKED.

## Expected

J5 polls the existing setup status for a bounded cold-start window, continues when the state becomes `ready`, and still reports BLOCKED if setup fails or is not ready when the deadline passes.
closed_recent.title: Real E2E J5 skips while the managed Python base is still installing

closed_recent.author: wyhohyw
closed_recent.body:
Mirrors GitCode issue [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137) (root-cause analysis: [comment](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137#comment_193508877)).

## Symptom

After deploying the stack (reported on Ubuntu 25.10, commit `c33c1ae`; the same code is on current `main`), a custom model provider cannot be configured. In **System settings → Model registry → Connect model**, the provider select shows "Custom provider", but the name / Base URL / model ID fields never appear. Only the API key, protocol, variant and "Add model" controls are visible, and picking "Custom provider" again changes nothing.

## Root cause

The backend is fine: `GET /api/providers` always returns the built-in presets. The bug is in the frontend.

1. **Presets are dropped when any unrelated settings request fails.** In `apps/web/src/App.tsx`, `modelProviderPresets` starts as `[]` and is filled only inside one `Promise.all` with ~12 other settings requests (`getMemoryGraphSettings`, `getIdeaTreeSettings`, `getSandboxNetworkSettings`, ...). There are two such batches: one at startup, one when System settings opens. If any request in a batch fails, the whole batch goes to `catch` and the preset list stays empty, even though `listProviders` itself succeeded.
2. **The select's value matches no option.** `ModelConnectWizard` starts with `selectedPresetId = "deepseek"` and `isCustom = false`. With no presets, the only `<option>` left is `custom`, but the select's `value` is still `"deepseek"`. The browser displays the first option, so the UI **shows** "Custom provider" while the component is **not** in custom mode.
3. **Re-selecting the shown option fires no change event.** `onChange` never runs, so `isCustom` stays `false`. The custom fields render only when `isCustom` is true, so they never appear. `selectedPreset` is also `undefined`, so the name and Base URL override fields under "Advanced" are hidden too.

Reproduced with a component test that renders the wizard with `presets=[]`:

```text
presets=[]              : {"selectValue":"deepseek","options":["custom"],"hasCustomUrl":false}
presets loaded, custom  : {"selectValue":"custom","options":13,"hasCustomUrl":true}
```

Which settings request fails in the reporter's environment is still unknown; we have asked on the GitCode issue.

## Proposed fix

**A. Load the provider registry on its own (`App.tsx`).** Take `listProviders()` out of both `Promise.all` batches and request it separately, so presets and configured providers no longer depend on unrelated settings requests. Triggers and error routing stay as before: a failure while System settings is open is shown in that dialog, and a startup failure follows the existing startup rule.

**B. Keep the wizard's state consistent with its options (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx`).** When the selected preset is not in the list, the wizard corrects itself:
- presets available: switch to the first preset;
- no presets: enter custom mode, so the custom fields appear;
- custom mode that was entered automatically for lack of presets switches back to the first preset once presets arrive, but only if the user has not started filling the custom fields. A custom provider the user picked is kept.

**Tests:** five new cases in `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx` cover an empty preset list, presets arriving late (with and without user input), a user-picked custom provider surviving a refresh, and a selected preset disappearing. With the wizard fix removed, three of them fail; the other two guard against regressions from the fix itself. All 27 tests in the file pass, and the web package type-checks. A browser E2E for the App-level change (one settings endpoint failing while custom-provider setup still works) has not been run yet.

---

本 issue 同步自 GitCode issue [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137)（原因分析见[评论](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137#comment_193508877)）。

## 现象

部署完成后（报告环境为 Ubuntu 25.10、commit `c33c1ae`，当前 `main` 上的相关代码相同），无法配置自定义模型服务商。在 **系统设置 → 模型注册表 → 连接模型** 中，服务商下拉框显示“自定义服务商”，但名称、Base URL、模型 ID 输入框始终不出现，只能看到 API Key、基础接口、接口变种和“添加模型”。再次选择“自定义服务商”也没有反应。

## 成因

后端没有问题：`GET /api/providers` 总会返回内置的服务商预设。问题出在前端。

1. **任何一个无关的设置请求失败，预设都会丢失。** `apps/web/src/App.tsx` 中 `modelProviderPresets` 初始为 `[]`，只在一个 `Promise.all` 里和另外约 12 个设置请求（`getMemoryGraphSettings`、`getIdeaTreeSettings`、`getSandboxNetworkSettings` 等）一起加载。这样的批量请求有两处：一处在应用启动时，一处在打开系统设置时。批量中任一请求失败，整组都会进入 `catch`，即使 `listProviders` 本身成功了，预设列表也一直为空。
2. **下拉框的 value 匹配不到任何选项。** `ModelConnectWizard` 初始状态是 `selectedPresetId = "deepseek"`、`isCustom = false`。预设为空时只剩 `custom` 一个选项，但 value 仍是 `"deepseek"`。浏览器会显示第一个选项，于是界面**显示**“自定义服务商”，组件内部却**不在**自定义模式。
3. **再次选择当前显示的选项不会触发 change 事件。** `onChange` 不执行，`isCustom` 一直为 `false`。自定义字段只在 `isCustom` 为真时渲染，所以始终不出现。同时 `selectedPreset` 为 `undefined`，“高级配置”里的名称和 Base URL 覆盖字段也被隐藏。

用 `presets=[]` 渲染向导的组件测试复现了这一点，输出见上文。

报告者环境中具体是哪个设置请求失败仍待确认，已在 GitCode issue 中询问。

## 修复方案

**A. 服务商注册表单独加载（`App.tsx`）。** 把 `listProviders()` 从两处 `Promise.all` 中拿出来单独请求，预设和已配置服务商不再受无关设置请求影响。触发时机和报错去向保持不变：系统设置打开时的失败显示在设置弹窗中，启动时的失败沿用原有规则。

**B. 向导状态与选项保持一致（`ModelConnectWizard.tsx`）。** 当前选中的预设不在列表中时，向导自动修正：
- 有预设：切到第一个预设；
- 没有预设：进入自定义模式，显示自定义字段；
- 因为没有预设而自动进入的自定义模式，在预设到达后切回第一个预设，前提是用户还没开始填写自定义字段。用户主动选择的自定义服务商会保留。

**测试：** 在 `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx` 中新增 5 个用例，覆盖预设为空、预设迟到（用户是否已填写）、用户主动选的自定义在刷新后保留、选中的预设从列表消失。撤掉向导修复后其中 3 个失败，另外 2 个用于防止修复本身引入回归。该文件 27 个用例全部通过，web 包类型检查通过。App 层改动的浏览器 E2E（模拟某个设置接口失败时仍能配置自定义服务商）尚未运行。

closed_recent.author: zy95-12
closed_recent.body:
## Problem and goal

Containers, restricted cloud environments, and remote compute nodes may have bubblewrap installed but prohibit the namespaces or mounts it needs. The ability to install, build, and open the workbench should be separate from the selected Runner's ability to execute code safely.

Users should not need to understand execution modes before using the product. Installation and builds should not be blocked by execution-mode requirements. Explain the limitation and offer choices only when a task actually needs code execution and the selected Runner cannot satisfy its requirements.

## Observed environments and results

On 2026-10-11, different execution environments produced different results. These observations do **not** support a blanket claim that cloud desktops cannot run sandboxes:

1. **Restricted cloud coding container:** while investigating main `cc95884428e64ae853d8758574fff5107c6347f0`, bubblewrap failed with `setting up uid map: Read-only file system`, consistent with that environment's /proc restrictions. Source installation and builds could complete, but sandbox execution remained unavailable.
2. **Tool execution session on another cloud desktop:** at main `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, the project's sandbox probe failed with `loopback: Failed to create NETLINK_ROUTE socket: Operation not permitted`.
3. **Desktop terminal on that same cloud desktop:** the same probe succeeded, and the Runner and workbench subsequently started from the desktop terminal. No sandbox disabling or host security-policy changes were required. The tool session and desktop terminal occupied different network namespaces.

Capability checks must therefore run in the **actual execution environment of the selected Runner**. A failure in an installation shell or another session must not be generalized to the entire machine. Likewise, a remote node merely appearing to be containerized does not establish adequate isolation.

## Current implementation and consequences

Code observations below refer to `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`:

- Standalone dependency installation and builds are possible, but the [one-command source startup path](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/start-stack.sh#L326-L395) checks sandbox executables before installation/build. It also [waits for Runner health before proceeding with API/UI startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/start-stack.sh#L626). Missing sandbox dependencies or a Runner startup failure can therefore prevent access to the workbench.
- [Runner startup preflight](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/server.ts#L1086-L1142) handles failures differently: some Linux sandbox failures only produce a warning, whereas missing/incompatible executables or unusable Seatbelt prevent startup. Process liveness or HTTP health is not equivalent to code-execution readiness.
- Internal probes already expose information such as sandboxUsable, but this is not yet an end-to-end capability and recovery contract spanning Runner registration, task dispatch, and the UI.
- [Code tool bindings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts#L174-L219) do not provide a dedicated just-in-time choice flow for unavailable sandbox execution. Generic permission to run code is not consent to unsandboxed execution.
- [Ordinary code execution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/executor.ts#L933-L1003) still depends on bubblewrap/Seatbelt; there is no general-purpose unsandboxed backend. The direct connection setting means a direct connection to a Runner, not unsandboxed execution.
- The [existing permission mechanism](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/api/src/permissions/index.ts#L28-L80) may provide an interaction foundation, but it does not establish that execution-mode switching, dedicated consent, and reliable recovery already exist.

User impact:
1. Users who only want to install, build, configure models, or browse the workbench may be blocked by local compute prerequisites.
2. A service may appear connected, yet fail when code is executed, making sandbox, network, dependency, and model failures difficult to distinguish.
3. Users with an available remote Runner may still have to troubleshoot local execution; restricted-environment users lack an actionable in-product next step.
4. Silently falling back to direct execution would remove isolation without informed consent, increasing exposure of files, processes, and credentials.

## Expected behavior

1. **Decouple installation, builds, and workbench startup from execution readiness.** Allow installation/build and non-execution configuration/browsing when the local Runner is unavailable. Clearly indicate compute limitations rather than claiming full readiness.
2. **Probe capabilities per Runner.** Distinguish connectivity, dependencies, sandbox availability, and execution readiness; retain structured failure reasons and validate them at the actual execution location.
3. **Ask only when execution requires a decision.** Use an available safe execution path by default. When blocked, explain why and offer an available Runner, environment repair, or cancellation. Do not force users to choose modes during installation.
4. **If direct-execution fallback is supported, design it explicitly.** Reuse task orchestration and artifact handling, branching at the execution backend. Never silently downgrade. Explain the affected scope and obtain dedicated consent first; authorization scope, lifetime, and invalidation require design review.
5. **Retain product responsibility for safety.** An assertion that the external environment is controlled must not replace validation, hazardous-action controls, auditing, cancellation, or recovery. This issue does not request disabling host security policies or bypassing platform restrictions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Independent installation/build completes in three cases: bwrap missing, bwrap present but namespace creation denied, and a working sandbox.
- [ ] When local compute is unavailable, the workbench supports permitted non-execution flows and clearly reports limited capabilities.
- [ ] Preflight results belong to the selected Runner's actual execution environment, not another shell or node.
- [ ] A task requiring code execution reports the blocking reason and allows an available Runner or cancellation; normal environments do not gain unnecessary prompts.
- [ ] If direct execution is implemented, it requires consent distinct from generic code permission, has no silent fallback, and produces auditable records.
- [ ] Tests cover rejection/cancellation, repeated execution, Runner changes, capability changes, and process restarts; already completed side effects must not be duplicated.

## Related issues and scope

- #38 covers the mismatch between serve readiness and actual compute readiness. This issue additionally covers installation/startup decoupling, actual-Runner capability probes, just-in-time interaction, and fallback design.
- #29 covers actionable dependency preflight guidance.
- #264 separately tracks proxy, micromamba download, and SOCKS dependency installation usability.
- These are requirements and design proposals, not a claim that an unsandboxed backend already exists. Delivery staging and the precise direct-execution authorization contract remain design decisions.
closed_recent.title: [Feature]: Decouple sandbox readiness from installation and workbench startup; offer choices when execution is blocked

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #89](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/89) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Write a long, domain-heavy analysis prompt in the composer and send it.

## What I saw instead

When sending fails (expired local token → 401, network error, provider rate limit → 429, busy backend), only a red toast is shown. The composer text, references, and annotations were already cleared, with no restore, no undo, and no retry. Minutes of writing are gone.

## Code pointer

`submitMessage` in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` clears the draft **before** the request is made:

```ts
setMessage("");
setComposerReferences([]);
setPendingAnnotations([]);
```

Only afterwards does it call `client.streamMessage`; the catch path shows the error but never restores the cleared state.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Clear the composer only after the backend accepts the message; on failure, immediately restore the text, references, and annotations.
- Offer a "resend" action next to the failure notice.

Science users routinely write long statistical-methods-plus-plotting instructions; losing the draft costs far more than in a casual chat app.

Reproduction sketch: type a long prompt, send, and make the request fail (invalidate the token or stop the backend); observe the composer is empty.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.8), Chrome, verified against `main` @ 9b3d2e48 (v0.2.0).

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #92](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/92) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Paste my LLM provider's API key and get the agent working.

## What I saw instead

"Connecting a model" currently requires hopping across two separate settings pages, four times:

1. Open system settings → "Models & capabilities → Model registry";
2. Click "+ Add Provider", pick a preset (e.g. DeepSeek) or custom, paste the API token, save;
3. Still not usable: find the concrete model in the provider's expanded list and click "Add" to create a model entry;
4. Still not usable: switch to "General → Global defaults" and select it in the "task model" dropdown (entries like `test · deepseek-v4-flash · ... · model default`).

Nowhere in the flow is there a link for "where do I get a key", nor any hint that "calls are billed by the provider".

*(Screenshots of the model registry page and the global defaults page are available in the cross-tracked GitCode issue above.)*

## Why this is confusing

- The user's mental model is "paste the key and it works", but the design splits provider, model discovery, model entry, and the global default task model into four layers — cognitive overload for researchers.
- Entry names conflict: the README points to `Global defaults`, the empty state says "model registry", the English UI says `Models` — three names for the same thing.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Provide a single-step connection wizard: pick a provider (DeepSeek / Zhipu / OpenAI / …) → paste the API key → click "Test and enable", which verifies connectivity, registers a recommended main model, and sets it as the global default task model.
- Under the API key input, add one line of guidance: a link to the provider's key page, plus "model calls are billed at the provider's standard rates".

Design note: the wizard orchestrates the existing four-layer configuration without changing the underlying model structure; the manual configuration path can remain for advanced users.

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #88](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/88) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4310` for the first time after starting ScienceDiscovery, and see a welcoming entry point to get started.

## What I saw instead

The page immediately opened a settings dialog with **three overlapping red errors at the same time**:

1. A toast in the top-right corner: `Request error: Unauthorized`;
2. A warning bar above the dialog: `Settings error: Unauthorized`;
3. A red alert inside the dialog body: `Access token rejected: The local API rejected this token. Paste the access token the server printed when it started, then save.`

The input field is labeled `Local API token`, and there is no other onboarding content on the page.

*(A screenshot of the three overlapping red errors is available in the cross-tracked GitCode issue above.)*

## Why this is confusing

- Three stacked "unauthorized / rejected" messages right after opening the page make users assume the installation is broken.
- `Local API token` reads like the API key of an LLM provider (OpenAI / DeepSeek). Pasting a model API key gets rejected again with more red text — a dead end.
- The actual token must be found in the server's startup terminal log. If the server runs in the background, in a container, or was started by someone else, users have no idea where to look.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Deduplicate the three errors: when no token is configured, show a single clear guide (where the token lives in the startup log, how to paste and save it) instead of toast + warning bar + in-dialog alert all at once.
- Distinguish "local service access token" from "external model API key" in naming and copy, so users stop pasting model keys into the local token field.
- Open question (not decided): whether loopback (`127.0.0.1`) access should be passwordless by default or issue a one-click session credential — listed here as an option only; it needs a security review first.

## Reproduction

1. Start ScienceDiscovery (`serve`).
2. Open the service URL with a fresh browser profile (no prior localStorage).
3. Observe the toast, warning bar, and in-dialog error appearing simultaneously.

Code pointer: the auth and settings-loading paths in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` trigger three separate error surfaces on a 401 instead of converging on one guide.

Environment: Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.8), Chrome, Simplified Chinese UI, verified against `main` @ 9b3d2e48 (v0.2.0).

> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #99](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/99) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

## What I was trying to do

Find the installer for my OS on the project homepage/README, download it, and run it.

## What I saw instead

- The Installation section of `README.md` only says: `Prepare a ScienceDiscovery executable for the host architecture. Binary packaging, source mode, and Docker procedures are documented in the deployment guide.` — with no Releases download link at all.
- Following that link, `docs/en/how-to/deployment.md` opens with a comparison of three deployment modes, and the single-file binary section then teaches how to **build the binary from source** with the packaging script.
- Meanwhile, the v0.2.0 GitHub release already ships ready-made binaries — `ScienceDiscovery-0.2.0-linux-x86_64` and `ScienceDiscovery-0.2.0-linux-aarch64` — but no entry point directs users to them.

## Why this is confusing

Most researchers will never build from source; the docs funnel "give me the binary" users into "build it yourself" developer documentation. A user has already asked how to obtain the binary in #1; related README/tutorial discussions are in #27 and #26.

## Suggested user-observable outcome

- Put a direct GitHub Releases link in the most prominent spot of the README (before Quick start), explaining which asset to pick per OS/architecture.
- Include verification instructions (how to check the release assets' SHA-256).
- Layer `deployment.md` so "download the released binary" comes before "build from source".
- Align the naming of configuration entry points across docs (`Global defaults` vs "model registry" vs `Models`).

### 背景与本 issue 的定位 #84 已经给出了迁移理念、整体架构、259 条接口清单、32 类事件映射与模块级工作量，并推荐「新写一个 adapter 接 JiuwenSwarm Gateway 的 WebSocket」。 本 issue **不重复**接口清单与事件映射，聚焦 #84 未展开的一个前置问题： > 我们复用的边界，应该划在 **agent-core（`openjiuwen`）** 还是 **JiuwenSwarm（`workswarm`）**？ 这个问题之所以是前置的，是因为一轮只读代码盘点得到一个结论：**我们想复用的能力，大部分实质在 agent-core，不在 JiuwenSwarm**；而我们未来想改的基础算法（上下文组装、多 agent 探索），**替换缝全部在 agent-core**。边界划错，会导致 agent-core 变成传递依赖，出现「想改算法却不能自己决定 agent-core 版本」的结构性矛盾。 本文据此给出后端分层设计、代码结构、迁移映射与侵入分析。前端 `apps/web` 保持不变，本文只讨论后端。 **分析基线（只读，未改动任何仓库）** | 仓库 | 分支 | commit | |---|---|---| | ScienceDiscovery（本仓） | `main` | `3cb3570091ab1559edf356a9a20f9df8bfff764b` | | [JiuwenSwarm](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/jiuwenswarm) | `develop` | `cdf1d0fd4aa6b93f95565383e6e61913981af844` | | [agent-core](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/agent-core) | `develop` | `6dfda012193d09dc3908524d5f8ae406811d909f`（JiuwenSwarm 当前 pin 的是 `d0bd83352f5ef4070baf44d37e788ba692a95b37`） | 行数统计口径为 Git 跟踪文件，未跟踪的虚拟环境与构建产物不计入。 --- ## 一、能力归属：agent-core 与 JiuwenSwarm 的分工 ### 1.1 体量 **agent-core（`openjiuwen 0.1.18`，647,577 行 Python）** | 模块 | 行数 | 主要内容 | |---|---:|---| | `core/` | 167,221 | `foundation` 25,991 · **`context_engine` 23,999** · **`memory` 18,149** · `runner` 13,622 · `retrieval` 13,176 · `session` 11,223（含 `vcs` 1,331、`checkpointer` 1,834）· `single_agent` 9,982（agent 循环、`AgentRail` ABC、`AbilityManager`） | | `harness/` | 148,673 | **`tools` 47,454**（含 **`browser_move` 25,026**、`worktree` 3,388、`filesystem` 2,636、`shell` 2,000、`web` 2,649）· **`rails` 28,250** · `personal_context` 24,351 · `prompts` 10,992 | | `rsi/` | 86,605 | `harness_rsi` 53,685 · `artifact_rsi` 32,206 | | `agent_teams/` | 81,969 | `tools` 15,400 · `agent` 11,493 · **`workflow` 8,454**（swarmflow 引擎）· `team_workspace` 4,139 | | `agent_evolving/` | 56,772 | `agent_rl` · `checkpointing` · `optimizer` · **`ttse`** · `trainer` · `updater` | | `symphony/` | 51,049 | **`retrieval` 21,140** · `orchestration` 8,369 · `discovery` 3,225 · `evaluation` 2,019 | | `extensions/` · `dev_tools/` · `harness_providers/` · `harness_protocol/` | 55,226 | a2a · observability semconv · SKILL.md 解析 | agent-core 的自我定位是 SDK：`pyproject.toml` 里 `description = "openJiuwen agent-core is a feature-rich AI agent SDK…"`，配 49 份 `docs/specs`、21 个 `examples/`、`[project.urls]` 的 Documentation 与 Changelog。 **JiuwenSwarm 分两类。** 用「模块内 import `openjiuwen` 的 `.py` 文件占比」作为归属的代理指标： *自有实质（低依赖率，agent-core 无对应物）* | 模块 | 行数 | 依赖率 | 提供什么 | |---|---:|---:|---| | `jiuwenbox/` | 36,396 | **1%** | 沙箱：bwrap · Landlock · seccomp · netns · cgroup · 推理隐私代理 | | `gateway/` | 57,681 | **6%** | 渠道适配、7 个 IM 平台、路由、cron 调度侧、斜杠命令 | | `resources/` | 41,847 | — | 35 个内置 Skill | | `common/` | 22,673 | 17% | E2A 协议 2,962 · 配置 · 148 个 `ReqMethod` · 自动更新 | | `extensions/` | 16,525 | **5%** | 应用扩展、Rail 插件、扩展包 | | `server/runtime/skill/` | 14,727 | **6%** | Skill 包管理、归档、热更 | | `server/runtime/session/` | 14,217 | 18% | 会话持久化、**项目 Git 与按轮次 diff** | | `agent_ws_server.py` | 12,076 | — | WS 服务端，处理 106 个 ReqMethod | | `marketplace/` | 4,690 | 15% | Skill Hub 客户端 | | `a2ui/` | 2,691 | **0%** | 生成式界面 | | `instance_manager/` | 2,539 | **0%** | 单机多实例 | | `channels/` | 15,979 + 216,621(前端) | — | Web / TUI / IDE / 浏览器扩展 / 桌面 / CLI / ACP | *agent-core 适配层（高依赖率）* | 模块 | 行数 | 依赖率 | agent-core 对应物 | |---|---:|---:|---| | `agents/swarm/` | 6,066 | **87%** | `harness/manifest` + `agent_teams/rails` | | `agents/harness/common/tools/` | 19,006 | **74%** | `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `server/runtime/agent_adapter/` | 36,050 | **65%** | `harness` + `agent_teams` | | `agents/harness/common/rails/` | 27,211 | **50%** | `harness/rails` 28,250 | | `agents/harness/team/` | 14,301 | 48% | `agent_teams` 81,969 | | `agents/harness/common/rsi/` | 11,862 | 46% | `rsi/` 86,605 | | `symphony/`（Swarm 侧） | 8,142 | 36% | `symphony/` 51,049 | | `agents/harness/common/auto_harness/` | 6,761 | 33% | `agent_evolving/` 56,772 | ### 1.2 七条容易记错的归属 | 能力 | 常见认知 | 实际 | |---|---|---| | 浏览器自动化 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `harness/tools/browser_move` **25,026 行**；Swarm 的 `channels/browser` 是浏览器扩展前端 | | Symphony 技能编排与检索 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `symphony/` **51,049 行**；Swarm 侧 8,142 行是服务化封装 | | RSI / Skill 自演进 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `rsi/` 86,605 + `agent_evolving/` 56,772 | | TTSE | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `agent_evolving/ttse`；Swarm 侧是配置开关 | | 四套记忆体系 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `core/memory` 18,149 + `harness/personal_context` 24,351 | | 多 agent / swarmflow 引擎 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `agent_teams/` 81,969，引擎在 `workflow/engine` | | 上下文压缩 | JiuwenSwarm | **agent-core** `core/context_engine` 23,999（6 个压缩器 + 4 个卸载器） | ### 1.3 JiuwenSwarm 相对 agent-core 的净溢价，对本项目是否用得上 | 自有实质 | 行数 | 用得上？ | |---|---:|---| | `agent_adapter` + `agent_ws_server` | 48,126 | ◐ 仅在「整进程复用 AgentServer」时白拿 | | 内置 35 个 Skill | 41,847 | ◐ 部分（xlsx/pdf/doc 等通用 Skill） | | jiuwenbox 沙箱 | 36,396 | ✅ | | Skill 包管理 | 14,727 | ✅ | | 会话存储 + 项目 Git | 14,217 | ✅ | | cron 调度侧 | 3,558 | ✅ | | Skill Hub | 4,690 | ✅ | | A2UI | 2,691 | ✅ | | gateway 渠道适配 + IM | 54,123 | ❌ 本项目有自己的 HTTP/SSE 控制面 | | 多端（TUI/IDE/桌面/浏览器） | 232,600 | ❌ 前端固定用 `apps/web` | **用得上的约 156,000 行。** --- ## 二、结论一：复用边界划在 agent-core，JiuwenSwarm 按块复用 四条理由： 1. **能力在 agent-core。** 只依赖 agent-core 就能拿到 agent 循环、上下文引擎、记忆、检索、47,454 行工具库（含 25,026 行浏览器自动化）、rails 机制、agent_teams 与 swarmflow 引擎、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving，约 64.8 万行。 2. **替换缝在 agent-core。** 想改上下文组装或多 agent 探索，用到的是 `ContextEngine.register_processor`、`ContextEngine.register_window_mutator`、`agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 的 `use_provider()`、`register_{rail,tool,subagent}_provider`、`ModelContext(ABC)`、`AgentRail`——**没有一个在 JiuwenSwarm**（详见第五节）。 3. **穿过 JiuwenSwarm 会造成双层 pin。** JiuwenSwarm 的 `pyproject.toml` 把 agent-core pin 在一个 git rev 上（当前 `d0bd8335`），并有 `make update-openjiuwen` 滚动跟随 agent-core `develop`。若我们经 JiuwenSwarm 间接依赖 agent-core，就**不能自己决定 agent-core 版本**——而所有替换缝都在 agent-core，这是结构性矛盾。 4. **装配成本没有想象中高。** agent-core 的 `openjiuwen.harness` 导出公开工厂 **`create_deep_agent(...)`**（约 30 个关键字参数）与 `DeepAgentConfig`（50+ 字段，全部带文档）。JiuwenSwarm 的 `agent_adapter` 36,050 行里，`interface_code.py`（2,809，code 模式）、`team_helpers.py`（4,411）、`evolution_*`（1,347）、`browser_runtime_security`、`statusline_setup_agent` 等是 **JiuwenSwarm 的产品特性**，不是 agent-core 装配。按本项目自己的产品面（无 IM、无多端、无 code 模式、无 team 模板）重估，**自建装配层约 4,000–8,000 行**。 **与 #84 的差异**：#84 把 JiuwenSwarm 作为复用单位、adapter 接 Gateway WebSocket。本方案把 agent-core 作为硬依赖、JiuwenSwarm 按块可选。两者不是互斥的实现路径，而是**依赖方向的取舍**，建议在第 0 阶段 spike 里一并验证后再定。 --- ## 三、目标后端架构 ### 3.1 三层依赖与一条铁律 | 层 | 内容 | 依赖性质 | |---|---|---| | **L0 agent-core** | `openjiuwen`：agent 循环、ContextEngine、memory、retrieval、tools、rails、agent_teams、symphony、rsi、agent_evolving | **硬依赖，本项目直接 pin 版本** | | **L1 JiuwenSwarm 可选块** | Skill 包管理、Skill Hub、jiuwenbox、cron 调度、A2UI、内置 Skill | **可选依赖，每块一个 port，rev pin** | | **L2 本项目自有** | 科学 rails/tools/explore、科学域服务、科学侧车、runner、产品控制面、Web | 自有 | > **铁律：本项目业务代码不得直接 `import jiuwenswarm`。每块 JiuwenSwarm 能力先定义一个 `Protocol`（port），再在 `adapters/swarm/` 下写适配器实现。** 理由：JiuwenSwarm 是产品不是 SDK（包名 `workswarm`，版本 `0.2.5.beta1`，无公开 API 声明）。把 import 点收敛到一个目录，漂移的爆炸半径就是那个目录；每块可以独立决策、独立回滚；agent-core 保持独立可见。 ### 3.2 进程拓扑 ```mermaid flowchart TB UI["apps/web（React，不变）"] UI -->|"REST + SSE，37 类事件"| API subgraph API["sd-api（Node，:4310，保留）"] A1["http/ · store.ts · 静态托管"] A2["设置 / 模型 / 用量 / MCP 治理 / 权限 / 插件"] A3["agent-client（新增）：驱动 sd-agent"] A4["internal（新增）：科学域服务路由"] end subgraph AGENT["sd-agent（Python，新增）"] L0["L0：import openjiuwen
create_deep_agent · ContextEngine · AgentRail
agent_teams · swarmflow seam"] L2["L2：科学 rails / tools / explore"] L1["L1：ports ← adapters/swarm ⁄ adapters/native"] end API -->|"窄契约：环回 NDJSON + 内部 token"| AGENT subgraph SVC["科学域服务"] R["sd-runner :4311（micromamba · NPU · SSH · kernel）"] E["evolve / memory-graph / paper"] end API -->|"环回 HTTP + token"| SVC AGENT -->|"环回 HTTP + token"| SVC AGENT -.->|"可选，本机 HTTP"| BOX["jiuwenbox"] ``` 四条边界：前端与 `sd-api` 的 REST/SSE 契约**不变**；`sd-api` 与 `sd-agent` 之间用**本项目自定义的窄契约**（不实现 JiuwenSwarm 的 148 个 `ReqMethod`）；科学域服务沿用现有的环回 + 内部 token；JiuwenSwarm 的接触面只有 `adapters/swarm/`。 --- ## 四、代码结构与迁移映射 ### 4.1 新增 `services/agent/` ``` services/agent/ ├── pyproject.toml │ dependencies = [ "openjiuwen==" ] ← L0 硬依赖 │ optional-dependencies: │ swarm-skill / swarm-hub = [ "workswarm==" ] ← L1 按块可选 ├── scripts/check_layers.py ← 分层护栏 └── src/sciencediscovery_agent/ ├── runtime/ ═ L0：只 import openjiuwen ═ │ assembly.py（DeepAgentConfig → create_deep_agent） │ session.py · events.py（→ 37 类 SSE）· model.py · permissions.py ├── context/ ═ L0：上下文三语义 ═ │ processors.py（register_processor） │ window.py（register_window_mutator） │ projections.py（active_skills / plan_state / trust 标注） ├── science/ ═ L2：只依赖 ports/ ═ │ rails/（证据门禁 · 评审检查点 · 溯源记录） │ tools/（执行 · 证据 · 图谱 · 论文） │ explore/（Provider 实现：PUCT / idea-tree） ├── ports/ ═ L1 抽象：纯 Protocol，零依赖 ═ │ skill_store · skill_hub · sandbox · session_store · scheduler ├── adapters/ │ native/ ═ 兜底实现，不依赖 JiuwenSwarm ═ │ swarm/ ═ ★ 唯一允许 import jiuwenswarm ═ └── transport/ ═ 与 sd-api 的窄契约 ═ ``` `check_layers.py` 六条断言进 CI： 1. `runtime/` `context/` `science/` 不得出现 `import jiuwenswarm` 2. `ports/` 不得 import `openjiuwen` 与 `jiuwenswarm`（纯 Protocol） 3. `adapters/native/` 不得 import `jiuwenswarm` 4. `adapters/swarm/` 是唯一允许的目录 5. **每个 `adapters/swarm/.py` 必须有同名的 `adapters/native/.py` 兜底** 6. `science/` 不得 import `adapters/` 第 5 条是关键：没有兜底，「可选」就是假的。 ### 4.2 迁移映射 | 现有 | 行数 | 去向 | 替代者 | |---|---:|---|---| | `packages/runtime-core` | 626 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/single_agent` + `core/runner` | | `packages/context` | 2,439 | ❌ 删，语义迁 `sd-agent/context/` | L0 `core/context_engine` 23,999 | | `packages/model` | 1,465 | ❌ 删 | L0 `core/foundation/llm` | | `packages/tools` + `workspace`（工具部分） | 约 3,400 | ❌ 删 | L0 `harness/tools` 47,454 | | `packages/specialist` + `orchestration` + `plan` | 3,190 | ❌ 删 | L0 `agent_teams` + `harness/rails` | | `packages/governance` | 227 | ◐ 策略留 Node，审批迁 `sd-agent` | L0 `harness/security` | | `packages/provenance` `idea-tree` `memory` `cas` `artifact-manager` `data-source` `trajectory` | 13,675 | ◐ 加 HTTP 外壳成为 `internal/` 域服务 | — | | `packages/schema` `mcp` `mcp-sources` `skill` `plugin-sdk` `executor` `sandbox-capability` | 约 13,000 | ✅ 保留 Node | — | | `services/api/native-agent` | 1,121 | ❌ 删 | — | | `services/api/{runs,agent-run,bootstrap}` | 5,112 | ◐ 改写为 `sd-agent` 客户端 | — | | `services/api` 其余 | 约 25,000 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `services/runner` | 8,798 | ✅ 保留（M2 可选把隔离原语换成 jiuwenbox） | — | | `services/{evolve,memory-graph,paper,gateway}` | 23,045 | ✅ 保留 | — | | `skills/` 17 个 | 3,641 | ✅ 保留，经 `ports/skill_store` 读取 | — | | `services/launcher` + `scripts/binary-release` | 3,203+ | ◐ payload 增 Python 运行时 | — | | **新增** `services/agent/` | 约 8,000–13,000 | ➕ | — | | **新增** `services/api/src/{agent-client,internal}` | 约 3,500–6,000 | ➕ | — | **后端非测试 TypeScript 82,367 行中，保留约 66,400 行（约 81%）。** --- ## 五、改基础算法的路径（这些缝全部在 agent-core） ### 5.1 上下文组装 `openjiuwen/core/context_engine/` 是完整插件架构：`ModelContext(ABC)`（抽象方法含 `get_context_window()`）、`ContextProcessor`（钩子 `on_add_messages` / `on_get_context_window`）、6 个内置压缩器 + 4 个卸载器。四个改造层级，均**零源码改动**： | 层级 | API | 能改什么 | |---|---|---| | L1 注入 | `AgentRail.before_model_call(ctx)` 改 `ModelCallInputs` | 加删消息、加 prompt section | | L2 换处理器 | `@ContextEngine.register_processor` | 压缩 / 召回 / 卸载算法本身 | | L3 换最终窗口 | `agent.context_engine.register_window_mutator(fn)`，`fn: (ModelContext, ContextWindow) -> Awaitable[ContextWindow]` | **最终送进推理的窗口** | | L4 换整个模型 | 实现 `ModelContext(ABC)` 子类 | 整个上下文语义 | L3 正好承接我们现有 `packages/context` 的「model-aware 原子窗口选择 + 最终校验」。**待验证**：`register_window_mutator` 的执行点是否确实在所有 processor 之后。 ### 5.2 多 agent 探索 `openjiuwen/agent_teams/workflow/engine/seam.py` 文件头原文： > "The provider seam: the indirection that lets the engine be swapped. … The engine installs its `EngineProvider` for the duration of a run; **a different implementation … can install its own provider instead, and workflow scripts never change**." API：`Provider(Protocol)` 覆盖 `agent()` / `parallel()` / `pipeline()` / `map_parallel()` / `agent_session()` / `human()` / `budget`，配 `use_provider(p) -> Token` / `reset_provider()`。因为存在 `contextvar` 里，**科学探索 run 与普通 run 可在同进程并存**。 于是把 `services/evolve` 的 PUCT 搜索或 `packages/idea-tree` 的想法树升级成多 agent 分支探索，做法是实现一个 `ScienceExploreProvider` 装上去，**workflow 脚本一行不改**。 另有按名覆盖：`register_subagent_provider(name, factory)` 的文档写明「a later registration for the same name overrides it」，内置探索子智能体名为 `core.explore_agent`。 ⚠️ 注意两张表语义相反：`harness/manifest/catalog.py` 的 `add_descriptor()`（元数据）**拒绝重名并抛 `ValueError`**；provider 注册表（工厂）**后注册覆盖**。要覆盖内置算法走 provider 注册表，不要重复同名的 `@harness_element` 声明。 --- ## 六、侵入分析 侵入要分三种： - **A 型（源码侵入）**：必须改 JiuwenSwarm 的文件 - **B 型（协商性侵入）**：不改今天的行为，但要求冻结或新增扩展点 - **C 型（反向侵入）**：不改 JiuwenSwarm 一行，但**它的运行期假设侵入我们**——改进程状态、强制数据目录布局、注入依赖树 前两种此前讨论过，**C 型是这轮新发现的，也是「按块复用」的真正门槛**。 ### 6.1 C 型：三个全局副作用源 **(1) `jiuwenswarm/common/config.py` 在导入期修改 `sys.path`**（第 48–57 行）： ```python _user_config = os.getenv("JIUWENSWARM_CONFIG_DIR") if _user_config: _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = Path(_user_config) elif get_config_dir().exists(): _CONFIG_MODULE_DIR = get_config_dir() if str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_CONFIG_MODULE_DIR)) # 插到最前 ``` 进程级、导入即生效、不可撤销。若该目录含同名 `.py` 会**静默 shadow** 我们的模块；且行为取决于环境变量与目录是否存在，同一份代码在不同机器上 `sys.path` 不同。`get_config` 被 185 个文件使用。 **(2) `common/utils.py`（2,954 行）假定 `~/.jiuwenswarm` 工作区布局**：解析顺序 `JIUWENSWARM_DATA_DIR` → `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` → `~/.jiuwenswarm`，并期望其下有 `config/config.yaml`、`agent/workspace/` 等结构。我们若 import 依赖它的块，就必须在自己的数据目录下再造一个最小 JiuwenSwarm 工作区。 **(3) 依赖树注入**：`workswarm` 的 `dependencies` 含 `chromadb`、`faiss-cpu`、`playwright`、`tree-sitter`、`sqlite-vec`、`pgvector`、`opentelemetry-*`，以及对本项目完全无用的 `python-telegram-bot` / `discord.py` / `slack-bolt` / `dingtalk-stream` / `wecom-aibot-sdk`。 ### 6.2 C 型按块实测 | 块 | 依赖 `common.config` | 依赖 `common.utils` | `sys.path` 副作用 | **C 型等级** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **Skill Hub**（`marketplace/hub_client` + 3 个兄弟文件） | **0** | **0** | **无** | closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

Nightly trial run [38107013490](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38107013490) (real model, built-in agent loop) was cancelled by hand during its fourth journey. By then three of its ten journeys had already failed: DRB-59, DRB-64 and DRB-58, each after 83–90 minutes. Nothing that was uploaded says why:

- The job log (and `run.log`) has one `✘` line per journey, and no error.
- Each journey report says **FAIL** with "0 / 0 steps passed", and no error.
- `test-results/` is missing. That is where `benchmark-metrics.json` (run status, delivery, error, sub-agents), `error-context.md` and the trace would be. `summary.txt` is missing too.

What could be reconstructed from `stack.log` timing alone: DRB-58 used up its 90-minute run budget. DRB-59 and DRB-64 ended on their own after 83–84 minutes, well inside their 120-minute budget, and then failed at the delivery assertion. Whether those two runs failed, or completed without a readable report, can no longer be told.

## Why

1. **Per-test evidence is copied only on exit.** Playwright writes `test-results/` to `.e2e/test-results`, which is outside the uploaded results directory. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` copies it there only in its EXIT trap. When a job is cancelled, the runner sends SIGINT, then SIGTERM about 7.5 s later, then kills the process tree about 2.5 s after that. bash runs the trap only once Playwright has exited, and Playwright was still tearing down the running journey: its `finally` alone waits up to 30 s for the run to cancel. So the copy never happens. A job timeout or a lost runner has the same effect.
2. **The `list` reporter prints failure details only when the whole run ends.** As each test ends, it prints just the `✘` line.
3. **Journey reports only record errors raised inside `journey.step()`.** The reports themselves are written into the results as each journey ends, which is why they survived. But the benchmark journeys assert in the test body, so their reports carry no error at all.

## Expected

Every journey that has finished leaves its evidence in the uploaded results at the moment it finishes. Its failure reason can be read in the job log and in its journey report without waiting for the rest of the run, whether or not the run ends normally.

## Proposal

- `run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR=<layer results>/test-results`, and `test/playwright.config.ts` uses it as `outputDir` (falling back to `.e2e/test-results`). The exit trap then copies only the HTML report, which Playwright renders once the run ends anyway.
- A journey report that failed without a failed step gets a "failure reason" section from `testInfo.errors`. It is redacted and truncated like step errors already are.
- When a journey fails, print the first lines of its error after its `journey report (FAIL)` line: the assertion message and expected/received, without the stack, and redacted.

Not in scope: for a cancelled layer, the shared-plan summary still reports "no frozen plan reported … the layer stopped before it collected its tests", because the shared runner writes its accounting only after Playwright exits. With the evidence above, a cancelled run can be diagnosed regardless.

Related: #233 (a delivery failure does not carry the run's own error).

closed_recent.author: zhaozhaozz
closed_recent.body:
## What happened

A real research run that has already been working can stop because the model gateway rejects one tool call whose arguments do not parse. The same happens to a subagent that has already finished its work. The page then tells the user to check the model configuration.

On main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-59** ran for 20.2 minutes. Both subagents completed. The session contained `navigation_cues_summary.md`, `navigation_cues_sources.json`, `disturbance_summary.md`, and `disturbance_sources.json`, and the page showed 167K usage. The required `deepresearchbench-59.md` was not among them. The final answer was empty and the run status was `failed`.

The request error on the failure page was:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell); gateway request chatcmpl-a2101146-60b8-4549-a033-1fe6f70bcfa0
```

The same DRB-59 passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) in 1.3 hours. The gateway and model id had already completed two subagents in the failing run.

On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) (`90db5b8e`), the same failure ended two more journeys, once on an MCP tool rather than `run_shell`. All three events below are logged as `"truncated":false` in the server log's `[model-arguments]` line. The server log has no 5xx or 429 on model calls during the journeys.

| Journey | Where it failed | Gateway request | Tool | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DRB-64 | Main run, after 23 minutes. Both subagents had completed, and the main agent had just said it would write the report. | `chatcmpl-2c3cbc55-d420-4a0e-ab0f-f460883c3061` | `run_shell` | Run `failed`, empty final answer. The session had three files from the subagents (two source packages and coverage notes); the required `deepresearchbench-64.md` was never declared. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 1st attempt. Its `deliverable_check` MCP call had already returned `ok: true`; it failed while writing `signoff.json`. | `chatcmpl-34b150cd-8aa4-478d-8c60-f6b6de204c62` | `run_shell` | Subagent `failed`. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 2nd attempt, on its `deliverable_check` call, which was to carry the full 26,226-byte report. | `chatcmpl-f980e9ac-a76a-422a-af31-11a515383f8f` | MCP `deliverable_check` | Subagent `failed`. The checker never received the call. |

In TC-E2E-01 all five research specialists had completed within 37 minutes and `evidence_brief.md` (26,226 bytes) existed. The two signoff failures and their re-dispatches used the remaining time; the third signoff attempt was still running when the 55-minute test budget ran out, and the test cancelled the run, which had no final answer. How the test reports a run cut off by its budget is #239.

## Why one call ends the run

Code at `90db5b8e`; these files are unchanged on main at `9189206d`.

1. `packages/model/src/client.ts` parses each assembled tool call with `JSON.parse` ([L221-L230](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L221-L230)) and sets `argsParseError` on failure.
2. In the JiuwenSwarm model gateway, `rejectInvalidArguments` ([L220-L228](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L220-L228)) lets truncated turns through to the output-limit recovery, but throws for any non-truncated call with `argsParseError`. The gateway answers that turn with an error (an SSE error event once streaming has started, otherwise HTTP 502). Swarm does not retry the turn, and `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` ([L363-L367](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L363-L367)) turns it into the error of the run or subagent.
3. `classifyRunFailure` ([services/api/src/run-failure.ts L28-L49](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/run-failure.ts#L28-L49)) matches none of its markers for this message and falls through to `semantic-error`. The Web UI renders that class as `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`: "The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry."

The same condition is handled three different ways:

- Native runtime: `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` ([L334-L338](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/tools/src/registry.ts#L334-L338)) returns `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS` with `retryable: true` to the model as a tool result, and the model can re-issue the call.
- Swarm, truncated call: the calls are withheld and the turn goes through bounded output-limit recovery. In Nightly 37875334064 two such events (03:57 and 04:42 UTC) did not end their runs, and those journeys (DRB-58, DRB-62) passed.
- Swarm, non-truncated call: the run or subagent fails.

Passing the call through unchanged would be worse: the gateway re-serializes calls from their parsed arguments (`toolCallsOf`, [L123-L125](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L123-L125)), so Swarm would execute the tool with `{}`.

## Where it fails: in ScienceDiscovery, before JiuwenSwarm sees the call

Every model request from JiuwenSwarm passes two ScienceDiscovery layers before it reaches the provider:

```text
JiuwenSwarm -> adapter /llm/<token>/v1/chat/completions (services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py)
            -> Node model gateway (services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts)
            -> packages/model client -> provider
```

`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` points Swarm's model at `modelGateway.url` ([L555](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L555)), and the adapter route forwards to that URL. The gateway drops the whole turn before Swarm receives the tool call. Swarm only gets an error for its model request; it does not retry that request, and its agent loop ends.

JiuwenSwarm's own handling would not end the run. JiuwenSwarm `workswarm0.2.6` pins agent-core (`openjiuwen`) at `ad0c9dfb`, whose `openjiuwen/core/single_agent/ability_manager.py` parses tool arguments in `_parse_tool_arguments_with_repair`: `json.loads`, then a bracket-balancing repair, and if both fail `execute` raises `AbilityExecutionError` whose `ToolMessage` (`Invalid tool arguments JSON: …`) is returned to the model as the tool result, "so it can self-correct". The native ScienceDiscovery runtime does the same with `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS`.

A second ScienceDiscovery layer would reject the same call for platform tools. The adapter's `StreamingToolRewriter` parses the complete arguments of each platform tool with `json.loads` at `finish_reason` to append the run tag ([L328](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L328)), and on failure ends the stream with `invalid streamed platform tool arguments` ([L362-L366](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L362-L366)). It was not reached in these runs because the gateway had already stopped the turn. Simply passing the call through to Swarm would hit this layer, and would also put unparseable arguments into the history replayed to the provider.

## Expected

- A non-truncated call whose arguments do not parse is not executed, and the model is told which call failed and why so that it can re-issue it, with a bounded number of attempts (the same shape as the truncated-call recovery, or a bounded re-sample in the gateway). One bad call does not end a run that has been working for 20 to 40 minutes, and does not fail a subagent that has already finished its work.
- This holds for every tool, including MCP tools, in the main run and in subagents.
- If recovery is exhausted, the run error says that the model produced an invalid tool call, with the tool name and gateway request id. The user-facing text does not tell the user to check the model configuration when the same model has already been calling tools in that run.
- The Actions log for the journey includes this error instead of only `delivery.status` `"failed"` (#233).

## Evidence limits

Neither Nightly captured the raw argument strings or the parser messages, so whether the model emitted malformed JSON or the stream assembler lost part of the arguments is not known. Making that distinguishable is #246.
