stale.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #103](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/103) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

### 🚀 Background Description

Session-level **data connectors** (PubMed, arXiv, UniProt, …) already have a consistent checkbox: the composer “Data connectors” popover, plus the connector field in session / project / global runtime settings. Unchecked connectors are hidden from the Agent.

Custom MCP and Web access do not have an equally obvious counterpart:

1. **Custom MCP**: System settings → MCP servers has a whole-server “Enable this MCP server” switch. Once a server is in the registry it also appears in the connector checkbox list (ids like `custom-…`). The list is titled “Data connectors” and mixed with built-in literature/database sources, so it is easy to miss that a custom MCP must be ticked for the **current session**. Global enable ≠ session enable; the docs say so, the UI does not make it as obvious as data sources.
2. **Web access**: `web_search` / `web_fetch` are a global base capability with **no session switch**. System settings → Web only toggles engines / fetch vendors and keys. That cannot mean “this session must not use the public web.” The model always sees both tools.

Request: like today’s data connectors, give **custom MCP** and **Web access** checkboxes that can be turned on and off. When unchecked, the Agent in that session must not use the corresponding capability.

This is not [GitCode #67](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/67) (per-tool allow/deny on a custom MCP). This issue is server-level / Web-capability enablement.

### Design Ideas

Treat “which external capabilities this session may use” with the same interaction as data connectors: checkboxes, optional project/global inheritance, tools omitted when unchecked.

Suggested behavior:

- **Custom MCP**: one checkbox per saved custom server, labeled with the user-given server name (not only `custom-` + hex). Tools are exposed only when the box is checked **and** the server is globally enabled. Unchecked or globally disabled → no tools. Reusing `enabledConnectorIds` is fine, but the UI should group “Data sources” vs “Custom MCP” so users do not think the list is literature-only.
- **Web access**: one checkbox at the same level (e.g. “Web access”) that gates `web_search` and `web_fetch`. Unchecked: those tools are absent from the schema; permission cards for them must not appear. Engine/key/proxy settings still decide **how** search/fetch work once Web is on; they do not replace this switch.
- **Surfaces**: at least the composer capability picker (same entry as connectors, or immediately beside it) and session / project / global runtime settings. Inheritance matches connectors (inherit / override).
- **Defaults** (undecided, confirm before implementation): Web stays on by default and can be turned off, vs off until explicitly checked. Custom MCP should stay off the session by default (`enabledByDefault: false` today).

Out of scope:

- per-tool MCP allowlists (#67);
- changing Web engine order or vendor list;
- re-registering Web as an MCP Source.

### Involved Public APIs

- Session / project / global runtime settings must persist Web-access enablement (new field or a stable id such as `web` beside connectors). Custom MCP may keep using `custom-…` in `enabledConnectorIds`, but APIs and docs must describe that checkbox clearly.
- Tool assembly: disabled capabilities must not enter the model-visible schema; permission and audit paths must not invoke them.
- No new public network API. CLI overrides such as `--connectors` should be able to turn Web and custom MCP on/off if they already override connectors.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Composer connector picker and `ScopedSettingsEditor` connector field: same checkbox surface;
- Custom MCP system-settings enable vs session checkbox: both gates required;
- Workspace `web_search` / `web_fetch`: gated by the session switch, not unconditional base tools;
- Permissions: `connector:web:search` and `web_fetch` host permission only when Web is enabled;
- i18n: do not use “Data connectors” as the only label for MCP and Web;
- Does not replace MCP response-size protection or the Web providers settings page.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Functional:

- [ ] After adding a custom MCP, the capability list shows the **server name**; checking it lets the session Agent call its tools; unchecking removes the tools from the schema.
- [ ] A globally disabled custom MCP cannot be used from the session (session check alone is not enough).
- [ ] Unchecking Web access removes `web_search` / `web_fetch` from the tool list; checking restores them.
- [ ] Project/global inherit vs session override matches data connectors.
- [ ] Built-in data-connector checkboxes keep current behavior.

Regression:

- [ ] Existing PubMed-style connector tests / E2E;
- [ ] Existing custom MCP journeys (system enable, Inspector, session check then call);
- [ ] Web provider settings, cache, and permission cards still hold when Web is enabled.

User-journey E2E:

- Open the session capability checkboxes: data sources, custom MCP, and Web access can be toggled separately;
- With Web off, a search-like prompt cannot call `web_search` (or fails without a permission card);
- With a custom MCP checked, one tool call succeeds. Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

### Additional Information

Original request: like the current data-source connectors, add enable/disable checkboxes for custom MCP and Web access.
stale.title: [Feature]: Enable/disable custom MCP and Web access with the same checkboxes as data connectors

stale.author: zhaozhaozz
stale.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #102](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/102) (Chinese counterpart of this issue).

### 🚀 Background Description

ScienceDiscovery’s primary entry today is local `serve` plus a browser UI (default `http://127.0.0.1:4310`). The agent runs inside the product’s own control plane: the Web UI submits work, the API orchestrates Runs, the sandbox executes code, and MCP connects external tools. Users who already live in Zed, VS Code, JetBrains, or other editors cannot plug ScienceDiscovery in as a standard coding agent; they have to leave the editor and open a browser.

The [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) is an open standard for communication between editors (Clients) and coding agents. Zed published it in 2025; it is now an Apache 2.0 standard. It uses JSON-RPC 2.0 (typically over stdio) for initialization, sessions, prompt turns, streaming updates, permissions, and cancellation — LSP for coding agents. Any compliant Client can drive any compliant Agent without a per-editor private integration. The stable wire protocol is **ACP v1** (`protocolVersion` negotiated in `initialize`). ACP v2 docs shipped as Draft in 2026-07 and are **not** the default target of this issue.

ACP and the product’s existing MCP sit on different layers and do not replace each other:

| | ACP | MCP (already in the product) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connects | editor / IDE ↔ coding agent | agent / host ↔ tool and data servers |
| Standardizes | how to launch, drive, and render an agent session | how to discover and call external tools |

This repository has no ACP implementation (no `agent-client-protocol`, no stdio JSON-RPC agent entry). Nearby issues are not this work:

- GitCode [#23](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/23) / the HTTP CLI: a **CLI client of `serve`**, not an editor↔agent protocol;
- GitCode [#44](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/44): an internal pluggable-capability / Pending Mode design, not external ACP.

User-observable outcome: in an ACP-capable editor, select ScienceDiscovery, prompt against the current workspace, see streaming output and tool calls, approve sensitive actions through ACP permissions, and still use the product’s sandbox, scientific connectors, and Skills — without opening the browser.

### Design Ideas

**Default role: ScienceDiscovery as an ACP Agent** (the editor is the Client). That matches “put the research agent inside standard editors.” Whether to also be an ACP Client (drive Claude Code / Gemini CLI / etc. from this product’s UI) is an open question and must not block phase 1.

Phase 1 should implement the **ACP v1 baseline methods** (https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/overview):

1. **Transport**: the editor spawns this product’s ACP subprocess; JSON-RPC 2.0 newline-delimited JSON on stdin/stdout. Do not bind ACP to the existing HTTP `:4310` control plane by default.
2. **Lifecycle**: `initialize` (version and capability negotiation) → optional `authenticate` → `session/new` (or `session/load` when advertised) → `session/prompt` / `session/update` / `session/cancel`.
3. **Session mapping**: one ACP session maps to a recoverable Project/Session/Run context in the product; workspace paths follow ACP’s absolute-path rule.
4. **Permissions and sandbox**: Client `session/request_permission` and optional `fs/*` / `terminal/*` must align with existing permission cards and the Bubblewrap/Seatbelt sandbox. The default security posture must not be looser than the Web UI; ACP must not become a bypass around the sandbox.
5. **Capability advertisement**: `initialize` must report only capabilities that are actually implemented (`loadSession`, image prompts, MCP passthrough, …). Research-specific features (literature connectors, artifacts, memory graph) that have no v1 field should use ACP `_meta` / `_`-prefixed custom methods and be documented — do not invent a private JSON-RPC.
6. **Discoverability (can follow)**: ship a launch command and manifest editors can configure. Listing in the [ACP Registry](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry) is not decided.

**Alternatives considered**

- Extra subcommands on the HTTP CLI (#23) without ACP methods: editors still cannot connect.
- ACP Client only, never an Agent: users still cannot use ScienceDiscovery inside a standard editor.
- Wrapping the product’s private event stream and calling it ACP: no interoperability with Zed / VS Code / JetBrains clients.
- Targeting ACP v2 Draft as the only goal in phase 1: v2 is still draft; implement against the stable spec at implementation time, with v1 as the default acceptance line.

**Open questions (need a decision before implementation)**

- Whether to ship an ACP Client in the same phase;
- Whether phase 1 lists the agent in the ACP Registry (the registry currently requires authentication support);
- How ACP cwd / workspace maps to a product Project, and whether a full Gateway/Runner stack is required when `serve` is not already running;
- Whether permission prompts are owned by the editor’s ACP UI or still fall back to in-product permission cards.

### Involved Public APIs

- **ACP wire protocol**: expose ACP v1 JSON-RPC over stdio to editors. This is a new external contract, not an alias of the existing REST/SSE API.
- **Existing HTTP control plane**: may be reused locally for Project/Session/Run, but users must not have to open a browser before ACP works. If the ACP process embeds or starts the control plane, that should be one launch command.
- **MCP**: stays on the agent↔tools axis; do not multiplex MCP stdio and ACP stdio on the same pipe.
- **No anonymous public ACP service**: default remains trusted local/workstation use, consistent with “not a multi-user production service.”

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Launcher / CLI: add an ACP Agent entry alongside `serve` and GitCode [#23](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/23); they do not replace each other;
- Session / Run / permissions / sandbox: ACP prompt turns must hit the same execution and governance path;
- MCP: an ACP session should still use configured MCP servers;
- Web UI: not a required surface for this issue; whether ACP sessions appear in the web session list is undecided;
- GitCode [#44](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/44): the internal capability framework may be reused if the composition layer is in the way; acceptance is external ACP interop, not the internal plugin protocol.

### Test Design and Test Plan

**Protocol conformance**

- [ ] Complete `initialize` against a reference ACP Client (or the official schema / SDK): negotiate v1 (or the then-stable version); advertised capabilities match behavior;
- [ ] `session/new` → `session/prompt` completes one scientific turn (user message, streaming `session/update`, explicit stop reason);
- [ ] `session/cancel` interrupts an in-flight prompt turn;
- [ ] Privileged tool calls go through `session/request_permission` and do not run when denied;
- [ ] Errors use JSON-RPC 2.0 `error` objects; notifications have no response.

**Product constraints**

- [ ] Python / shell execution stays in the existing sandbox; the ACP path is not looser than the Web UI;
- [ ] Tokens, API keys, and session bodies do not leak into ACP logs or unauthenticated client traffic;
- [ ] Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

**Interop / user journey**

- [ ] In at least one real ACP Client (e.g. Zed or a VS Code ACP extension): configure the launch command → prompt against the open workspace → see streaming text and at least one tool call;
- [ ] Focused unit tests for JSON-RPC dispatch, failed version negotiation, and unauthenticated calls if `authenticate` is enabled;
- [ ] Docs include a Client configuration example (launch command, workspace, auth).

### Additional Information

Public spec and repos:

- Protocol overview: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/overview
- Schema / reference implementation: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/agent-client-protocol
- Registry: https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/registry

The product entry remains `./ScienceDiscovery serve` plus the browser. This issue adds an editor-spawned ACP Agent process, not another private chat protocol.
stale.title: [Feature]: Support the standard Agent Client Protocol (ACP)

stale.author: zhaozhaozz
stale.body:
> Cross-tracking: [GitCode #26](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (Chinese original of this issue). ### 🚀 Background Description Research agents often produce scripts, logs, configs, and prose (`.py`, `.r`, `.sh`, `.txt`, `.log`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.sql`, …). Users need to read those files in the artifact panel, not download them or jump to a new browser tab. The current viewer has two gaps: 1. **Plain-text artifacts have almost no in-app preview.** Catalog kinds only cover dataset / figure / html / json / latex / markdown / notebook / report / structure. Files such as `.py`, `.txt`, and `.log` fall into `other`. `ArtifactModal` loads only a few scientific kinds as text; `other` has no preview branch, so opening them is often a blank panel. In the workspace file sidebar, only `.md` uses the in-app Markdown reader; everything else is handed to `window.open` and the browser. 2. **Existing source / raw views are not a code-reading experience.** JSON, LaTeX source, Markdown source, CSV raw, and notebook code are plain `
`: no language highlighting, no line numbers, and long files are hard to scan or compare.

The viewer should:

- open plain-text files in-app;
- syntax-highlight common file types;
- show line numbers.

This is a viewing-experience request only. It does not change artifact registration, versioning, or provenance semantics.

### Design Ideas

Keep the existing specialized previews (Markdown render, tables, images, PDF/HTML iframe, molecular structure, notebook cells). Add one shared path for “read as source.”

Suggested behavior:

- Open recognizable UTF-8 text in-app — not a blank panel, and not a new browser tab by default.
- Pick a highlight language from the extension (and `mediaType` if needed). At least cover common research/engineering types:
  - plain text: `.txt`, `.log`, `.out`, `.err`
  - code: `.py`, `.r` / `.R`, `.jl`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.sh` / `.bash`, `.sql`, `.c` / `.h` / `.cpp`, `.java`, `.go`, `.rs`
  - config / data source: `.json`, `.yaml` / `.yml`, `.toml`, `.ini`, `.xml`, `.css`, `.html`
  - document source: `.md`, `.tex`
- Unmatched extensions that are still text: show as plain text, still with line numbers.
- Binaries, images, PDFs, Office files, etc. keep the current specialized viewer or download; do not force them through a text decoder.
- Markdown / table / notebook specialized previews stay; their “Source / Raw” views should reuse the same highlight + line-number component.
- Oversized files keep truncated preview (reuse the existing ~100_000 character cap) and tell the user they can download the full file.
- Highlighter library and whether to add `kind=text/code` are implementation choices, as long as the user gets highlighted text with line numbers. Do not change the artifact catalog or provenance semantics just to enable highlighting.

Out of scope:

- editing or saving files in the viewer;
- turning every file into a source view (images still show as images, CSVs still show as tables);
- a full IDE (folding, go-to-definition, diagnostics).

### Involved Public APIs

No new public HTTP API is expected. The viewer should keep using the existing artifact-version content and workspace-file read endpoints.

Possible internal adjustments (for implementation, not a product contract):

- load `other` / uncategorized text as text instead of skipping it as binary;
- if extension classification gains a `text`/`code` kind, use it only for preview routing and do not change the meaning of existing scientific kinds.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Artifact panel `ArtifactModal`: main catalog preview; `other` text must be readable.
- Workspace file tree: clicking `.py` / `.txt` etc. should open the same in-app text view, not only a new browser tab.
- Existing source views: JSON raw, Markdown/LaTeX source, CSV raw, notebook code, provenance scripts/logs — good candidates to reuse the same component.
- Artifact classification (`classifyScientificArtifact`): there is no text/code kind today; do not mis-label `.py` as dataset/report.
- i18n: new buttons / empty states / truncation copy must go through the existing message catalog.
- E2E: artifact panel, workspace file open, and existing Markdown/table/structure previews all need regression.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Functional:

- Open `.txt`: in-app full text (or truncation notice), line numbers; highlighting optional.
- Open `.py` / `.yaml` / `.json` and other common types: matching syntax highlighting, line numbers aligned with source lines (at least line 1 and the last visible line).
- Unknown extension, UTF-8 text: still opens as plain text with line numbers.
- Images, PDFs, structure files, other non-text: unchanged, not treated as source.
- Markdown artifacts: default remains rendered; Source view has highlighting and line numbers.
- Huge text: preview truncates, offers download, page stays responsive.
- Empty file: stable empty state, no error.

Regression:

- Markdown reports, CSV/JSON tables, images, HTML, notebooks, and molecular-structure previews still work.
- Workspace `.md` still uses the Markdown reader.
- Artifact download, version switching, and the provenance page still work.

Web E2E (required after changing the user-visible viewer):

- Open a text artifact in the panel; screenshot the highlighted, numbered end state.
- Open `.py` or `.txt` from the workspace tree; confirm in-app viewing rather than relying only on a new browser tab.
- Regression on one existing specialized preview (Markdown or CSV).

Formal E2E must not use the human trial port 4310 or its fixed data directory.

### Additional Information

Original request: support viewing plain-text artifacts, syntax highlighting for common file types, and line numbers.
stale.title: [Feature]: Artifact viewer should preview plain text with syntax highlighting and line numbers

stale.author: zy95-12
stale.body:
## Background

ScienceDiscovery is strengthening its end-to-end test coverage. We want to collect the complete user journeys that the community believes must remain continuously protected.

This RFC does not prescribe an implementation. It focuses on four questions: **What task is the user trying to complete? What outcomes must be observable? Does the scenario require a real model? Should it run as a pull-request gate or as a scheduled test?**

## How to contribute

Copy the comment template below and add one row for each proposed test scenario. Maintainers will periodically consolidate actionable feedback into the main table.

Guidelines:

- **Test scenario**: describe a complete flow from the user's goal, rather than an internal function or an isolated component.
- **Observations**: list user-visible outcomes and critical states, such as the final answer, tool calls, permissions, artifacts, citations, and recovery after a refresh.
- **Test method**: use `Mock LLM`, `Real LLM`, or `Both`, and explain why a real model is necessary when applicable.
- **Estimated token usage**: use `0 (scripted)` for Mock LLM cases; for Real LLM cases, estimate total input and output tokens for one run.
- **Estimated duration**: give the target duration for one case, excluding first-time dependency installation.
- **Priority**: use `P0` for basic platform availability, `P1` for core scientific capabilities, and `P2` for enhancements or corner cases.
- **Notes**: record environment requirements, external services, credentials, cost, side effects, candidate benchmark sources, or stability risks.

## Initial candidates

The following entries are both examples of the requested format and an initial backlog. The community is welcome to refine their priority, observations, estimates, and execution method.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Basic multi-turn conversation and refresh recovery | The run completes; the second turn uses conversation history; message order, terminal state, and refreshed content remain consistent | Mock LLM | Session, Agent Loop, History, SSE | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | No external network |
| Tool call, permission, and continued reasoning | Permission moves from pending to allowed; the tool executes once; its result returns to the model; the Agent continues and finishes | Mock LLM | Tool, Permission, Runner, Agent Loop | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a safe local tool fixture |
| Plan creation, update, and completion | Plan and step states remain ordered and correct; updates do not block tools; the final state persists and recovers | Mock LLM | Plan, Context, Workspace UI | 0 (scripted) | 2–3 min | P0 | Use a deterministic tool-call sequence |
| Subagent delegation and result return | The child Agent lifecycle is complete; tool ownership is correct; the result returns to the lead Agent; reasoning continues; refresh restores the state | Mock LLM | Subagent, Team, Tool, Context | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | No external provider |
| Generate and deliver an artifact | The file exists; deliverables are distinct from temporary files; preview and download work; provenance is traceable; the final answer references the artifact | Mock LLM | Workspace, Artifact, Provenance, Tool | 0 (scripted) | 3–4 min | P0 | Use a local Python or Shell environment |
| Literature review | The Agent searches multiple sources, retrieves and extracts selected papers, produces traceable citations, handles source failures, and delivers a review artifact | Both | MCP, Literature Sources, Governed Download, PDF Extraction, Citation, Review | 0 mocked; 20k–60k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Real run requires network access and may depend on source availability |
| Evolve a solution | The Agent defines an objective and evaluation, runs iterative candidates, preserves checkpoints and logs, compares results, and delivers the best reproducible solution | Both | Evolve, Runner, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Candidate source: Terminal-Bench-Science |
| Data analysis | The Agent inspects an input dataset, selects and executes a valid analysis, validates intermediate results, and delivers reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | Both | Workspace, Python/R, Artifact, Provenance, Review | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 10–25 min | P1 | Candidate source: BiomniBench-DA |
| AI model workflow | The Agent prepares valid model inputs, invokes the model workload, exposes execution progress, preserves outputs and environment metadata, and explains the result | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, NPU, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Candidate tools/models: Protenix, ProteinMPNN, and similar workloads; hardware availability may constrain scheduling |
| Simulation tool workflow | The Agent prepares a valid simulation, invokes the selected simulator, reports progress and failures, and delivers reproducible configuration, logs, and results | Both | Scientific Environment, Runner, Tool, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 10k–40k real | 15–60 min | P1 | Real cases may require licensed software, large dependencies, or specialized hardware |
| Memory graph | Research outputs are written to the graph with correct identities and relations; retrieval returns relevant prior context; graph-backed citations remain traceable after refresh | Both | Memory Graph, Context, Provenance, Citation | 0 mocked; 8k–25k real | 5–20 min | P1 | Mocked case can use the local backend; scheduled case may use Neo4j |
| Agent team collaboration | The lead Agent decomposes work across multiple specialists; child scopes remain isolated; progress is observable; results return to the lead and are synthesized without loss or duplication | Both | Agent Team, Subagent, Context, Permission, Trajectory | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Include concurrent child execution and one recoverable child failure |
| Idea Tree research | The Agent starts an Idea Tree run, expands and evaluates candidates, supports pause and resume, persists the tree, and delivers the selected result with its reasoning trail | Both | Idea Tree, Evolve, Workspace UI, Artifact, Provenance | 0 mocked; 15k–50k real | 10–30 min | P1 | Validate both tree state and the user-visible explorer |

## Comment template

Copy this table into a comment. Add more rows when proposing multiple scenarios.

| Test scenario | Observations | Test method (Mock or Real LLM) | Related feature | Estimated token usage | Estimated duration | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Describe the complete user journey | List user-visible outcomes and critical states | Mock LLM / Real LLM / Both | List related capabilities | Estimate | Estimate | P0 / P1 / P2 | Add environment, cost, dependency, or stability notes |

## Suggested areas

- Agent Loop, tools, permissions, planning, and Agent teams;
- MCP, skills, Web Search, and Web Fetch;
- literature retrieval, paper download, PDF extraction, and scientific databases;
- artifacts, provenance, evidence, claims, citations, and review;
- context compression, long-running task continuity, and error recovery;
- local and remote Runners, scientific environments, NPU workloads, and background tasks;
- settings, onboarding, observability, and critical usability journeys;
- scenarios that can reveal issues only with a Real LLM or a real external service.

## Expected outcome

Community feedback will form a prioritized E2E case backlog, divided into:

- fast Mocked E2E cases executed for every pull request;
- comprehensive Mocked and Real LLM E2E cases executed on a schedule;
- real scientific-task acceptance tests executed before a release.

This issue is for collecting and clarifying test requirements. Implementation can be split into follow-up issues and pull requests by scenario.
stale.title: [RFC] Collect community requirements for E2E test scenarios

stale.author: zy95-12
stale.body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Developers cannot reliably answer “which command runs this test?” or “did this invocation cover all selected tests?” The repository has overlapping entry points, inconsistent discovery rules, and test assets that are not represented in the shared catalog.

Consolidate test discovery and execution around the existing catalog so that local development and CI use the same selection logic. Every maintained test asset should have an identifiable owner and execution entry point, and a successful command must not conceal missing, unsupported, or unexecuted tests.

This is a focused implementation issue derived from [GitCode RFC #107: UT, ST and E2E test coverage and engineering](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/107). That is a GitCode issue, not GitHub issue #107.

## Evidence from the current branch

Inspected branch: `feat/jiuwenswarm`, commit [`57ff5f48802d4c495d10f01a2b211fccfdeb62ae`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/tree/57ff5f48802d4c495d10f01a2b211fccfdeb62ae). These observations describe this revision, not necessarily the current default branch.

- Root `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`, and `pnpm ci:ut` execute different combinations. Root `test` builds, runs binary-script tests, and invokes workspace package tests; it does not mean all Python, ST, and E2E tests ran.
- `.ci/test-catalog.mjs` registers eight aggregate tasks. The seven standalone `test/api/*journey.mjs` drivers, `test/contract` scenarios/tooling tests, and the new Python adapter suite are not fully represented in the shared execution path.
- `test/playwright.config.ts` scans the entire `test/` directory without an explicit browser-only `testMatch`. During the preceding E2E assessment, Playwright discovery also triggered TAP output from the contract tooling's `node:test` files.
- Node package scripts enumerate different glob depths. Web currently includes both `tests/*.test.ts` and `tests/*.test.tsx`, but does not recursively discover subdirectories. The RFC's earlier missing-`.test.ts` observation must not be reapplied as an unresolved fact on this branch.
- Some API journey drivers construct their own environment and start the native executor. Setting an outer JiuwenSwarm environment variable does not make those drivers validate JiuwenSwarm.
- Existing catalog and E2E metadata checks pass despite these gaps. Entry-point consistency checks alone do not prove that all test assets are collected.

Relevant files: root `package.json`, `.ci/test-catalog.mjs`, `.ci/test-selector.mjs`, `.ci/ci-contract.mjs`, `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, `apps/web/package.json`, `test/playwright.config.ts`, and `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`.

## Proposed scope

### 1. Load adjacent test configuration through the existing catalog

Do not create a competing registry or replace the existing test frameworks.

- Register module tests as suites with explicit discovery rules; do not manually enumerate thousands of unit-test cases.
- Give important ST and E2E journeys stable case IDs for individual selection and reporting.
- Include standalone journey/smoke drivers, JSON contract scenarios, Python suites, and test-tooling self-tests, not just files named `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*`.
- Describe source, runner, owner, layer, capabilities, environment requirements, timeout, gates, and supported executors where applicable.
- Keep model mode, sandbox/hardware requirements, and executor support independent of the test layer.
- Store scenario metadata in adjacent versioned `*.case.yaml` files and module discovery rules in `*.suite.yaml` files. The existing catalog loads these configurations; it is not a second manually maintained registry.
- Use `llm.mode: none | stub | real | unreviewed`, separate `supportedExecutors` from `ci.pr.executors` / `ci.daily.executors`, and declare `required` per CI policy. A nonblocking policy requires a reason and must retain its actual failures/blockers.
- Preserve narrative E2E-META comments for purpose, steps and dependencies; use YAML as the authority for machine-readable classification and policy.

The catalog can initially remain at `.ci/test-catalog.mjs`. A later move to `test/catalog.mjs` should retain a compatibility export rather than two independently maintained definitions.

### 2. Provide one documented command interface

Shared command interface (install dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first):

```bash
pnpm test:list
pnpm test:doctor
pnpm test:check
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --profile local
pnpm test --layer st --capability permission
pnpm test --layer e2e --surface browser --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both
```

Existing `ci:*` commands should remain compatible wrappers over the shared selector/runner. Document precisely what the default profile includes; do not silently reduce existing coverage when changing `pnpm test`.

A full selection must show gated real-model, hardware, and legacy tasks as blocked when prerequisites or opt-ins are absent. Listing must not execute test bodies or contact live model endpoints. Distinguish static asset inventory from framework-expanded test counts.

### 3. Enforce complete, framework-specific discovery

- Recursively enumerate Node/Web test files and pass explicit file arguments to the runner, avoiding shell-dependent glob depth.
- Check source-to-build test mapping so stale `dist` files cannot keep deleted tests alive.
- Restrict Playwright to the browser journey directory and an explicit `**/*.spec.ts` pattern.
- Preserve Python runner discovery semantics and explicitly identify tests requiring live dependencies.
- Fail asset validation for unowned files, stale catalog/quarantine entries, unintended duplicate ownership, and unknown case IDs.
- Treat unexpected empty selections as an error, not a successful run.

Keep module tests near their modules. Separate cross-module assets into `test/st/`, `test/e2e/`, `test/st/api/`, and, where appropriate, `test/st/local-stack/`. Test helpers and their own unit tests must not be collected as browser journeys. A broader domain-by-domain directory reorganization is not required for this issue.

### 4. Make selected scope and execution results explicit

Record the selected suites/cases, actual runner and executor, revision, outcomes, reasons, and evidence locations. Distinguish `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`, `SKIPPED`, and `NOT_RUN`; retain retry history instead of hiding instability.

An executor-specific selection must never silently fall back to another executor. Existing native-only drivers should declare that limitation until they support JiuwenSwarm. Executor-independent tests need not run twice.

Full assessment mode should continue independent suites after a failure and still return a failing result. Preserve fail-fast as an explicit option. A zero process exit code alone is insufficient evidence when the selected cases or required contract assertions were not executed.

## Suggested delivery sequence

1. Inventory existing assets and extend catalog/validation coverage while keeping existing paths and commands operational.
2. Introduce shared selection/discovery and targeted directory separation. Update imports, root calculations, metadata checks, CI paths/cache keys, documentation, and the E2E skill together.
3. Route local and CI entry points through the shared implementation and normalize selection/results reporting.

Keep product fixes separate. The agreed scope now also includes case-configured subject models and deterministic/LLM/hybrid assertions, with the original framework checks retained. Two obsolete browser declarations were subsequently approved for retirement: the unconditional persistent-kernel teardown placeholder and the fixme for the removed manual paper-search form. Record both original identities, reasons, replacement coverage or the remaining coverage gap in the migration record. Rename issue-number filenames by scenario/object. Preserve a before/after mapping of all remaining identities, not just equal aggregate counts.

## Agreed directory and layer model

UT is colocated with its owning code; `test/support/` is implementation code for the test infrastructure, with its own adjacent UT. It is not a test layer.

```text
test/
  support/             # test infrastructure and colocated UT
    contract/          # shared replay, normalization and comparison code
  fixtures/            # shared data and stubs
  st/
    agent-runtime/     # cross-module agent collaboration
    api/               # backend HTTP/service-chain integration
    contract/          # HTTP/event-stream scenarios, baselines and policy
  e2e/                 # browser user journeys
```

Directly calling running backend services is ST for this browser-facing product. Both L1 HTTP contracts and L2 run-event contracts are ST; a longer backend flow does not make it a browser user E2E test. Contract tooling is shared once rather than copied between scenarios.

Case metadata and IDs follow these boundaries: `st.api.<scenario>` and `st.contract.<scenario>`, while browser IDs remain unchanged. The former draft paths/IDs are recorded in `test/support/migration.json` under `layoutMigration`. This move preserves all 92 configurations, their supported executors and PR/daily policies. `--layer e2e` now selects browser work only; `--layer st` includes API and contract scenarios.

## Scenario naming

Use lowercase kebab-case object/behavior names, without issue numbers, `journey-` / `-journey` or `l1-` / `l2-` labels. Examples:

- `test/e2e/first-run-onboarding.spec.ts` and `.case.yaml`, ID `e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding`.
- `test/st/api/child-workspace.mjs` and `.case.yaml`, ID `st.api.child-workspace`.
- `test/st/contract/cases/run-approval-denied.case.yaml`, scenario ID `run-approval-denied`, catalog ID `st.contract.run-approval-denied`.
- `session-multi-turn` describes the former `l2-two-turns` contract scenario; `run-events.json` holds run-event scenarios.

Implementation/config filenames and IDs stay aligned. Shared browser helpers are `scenario-fixtures.ts`, `scenario-report.ts` and `browser-fixture.ts`. Module UT follows module names; Python's conventional `test_*.py` discovery remains unchanged.

Step-report validation is now explicit in YAML (`reporting: steps`) rather than inferred from a `journey-` filename; all formerly marked journeys retain this enforcement. Naming validation rejects the historical test filename prefixes/suffixes.

`namingMigration` in `test/support/migration.json` records old/new paths, catalog IDs and contract scenario IDs. Baseline keys and accepted-difference case references are renamed together; expected response payloads, scenario steps and difference predicates are unchanged. External baselines using the old IDs need the same key migration. The naming migration preserved all 92 configured entries and their policies; the subsequent real-model extension below adds daily coverage, and all 88 retained browser test identities were verified after filename mapping.

## Test triggers and usage

| Trigger | Entry point and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Pull request opened, synchronized or reopened | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: run `pnpm test:pr --layer ut`, `pnpm test:pr --layer st`, and the reusable `test-policy.yml` with `profile: pr`, `surface: browser`. Existing binary/Docker distribution gates remain. |
| Push to `main`/`master`, or manual dispatch of CI | Same PR policy and distribution jobs as above. Opening a PR into `feat/jiuwenswarm` also triggers the PR workflow; pushing only to an unrelated feature branch does not trigger the push rule. |
| Daily at 00:17 UTC / 08:17 Asia/Shanghai | `test-daily.yml` invokes the reusable workflow with `profile: daily`. GitHub scheduled workflows run from the default branch, so this starts only after the workflow reaches that branch. Manual `workflow_dispatch` is also declared, subject to GitHub workflow availability on the default branch. |
| Local PR/daily reproduction | `pnpm test:pr` / `pnpm test:daily` resolve the same YAML policy. Local callers must supply the required infrastructure; these commands do not reproduce all GitHub provisioning steps. |
| Explicit assessment | `pnpm test --profile full --executor both` selects all maintained scenario entries, including gated work. Unsupported/missing prerequisites are BLOCKED, not silently omitted. |

PR policy includes both UT tiers, native deterministic agent ST, and four JiuwenSwarm browser scenarios: first run, plugin composition, execution management and result delivery. Daily policy expands reviewed deterministic browser coverage to both executors and includes all seven native-only API journeys. After integration with target revision `9670568`, all 27 contract scenarios on two executor labels are observational because CI does not yet provision isolated contract targets or select the reviewed platform-specific comparison baseline. The target branch now includes `test/st/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json` with L2 coverage. Real-model browser work now runs in the required daily real job; hardware and quarantined legacy work remain manual opt-ins.

```bash
# Inventory and inspect the exact policy without running test bodies.
pnpm test:list --profile pr --json
pnpm test:list --profile daily --json
pnpm test:doctor --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm

# Run the configured policy or a selected scenario.
pnpm test:pr
pnpm test:daily
pnpm test --case e2e.browser.first-run-onboarding --executor jiuwenswarm
pnpm test --case st.api.child-workspace --executor native
pnpm test --profile full --executor both

# Validate configuration and test the harness itself.
pnpm test:check
pnpm test:tooling
pnpm ci:selftest
```

For JiuwenSwarm browser runs, provision an isolated instance (the GitHub reusable workflow calls `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup/start/env`) and supply `JIUWENSWARM_GATEWAY_URL` and `JIUWENSWARM_MGMT_URL`. Formal browser/API runs require a built, committed candidate and isolated services. `test:doctor` reports declared prerequisites; READY is not a service health or product-pass certification.

Real model calls require `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1` and the named credentials/endpoints. Hardware, adapter-live, contract and legacy cases have their own explicit gates; selecting a profile never enables them. Contract replay additionally requires an isolated target, token, declared target executor and reviewed comparison baseline. An operator-declared executor label is not independent backend verification.

`required: true` outcomes fail the gate unless they pass. Observational failures/blockers remain visible and produce `passed-with-observations` when all required tasks pass. Full/manual assessment treats all selected entries as required. PR/daily executor matrices cannot be overridden by `--executor`; edit and review the YAML policy instead.

`pnpm test` retains its original build + binary tests + workspace-test scope; it does not mean all repository tests. Existing `ci:*` commands remain compatibility entry points, and CodeArts retains those commands' existing native scope. Reports are written below `.test-runs/` or `CI_RESULTS_DIR`, with selected IDs, configuration paths, revision, requested/actual executor, PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/SKIPPED/NOT_RUN outcomes and command evidence. Static entry counts and framework-expanded test counts must be distinguished.

The implementation's `test/README.md` is the usage and configuration reference. New browser/API scenarios require adjacent case configuration; module unit tests inherit their suite entry point's policy. Unknown fields, duplicate IDs, missing sources, unsupported policy executors and unintended empty selections fail validation.

## Implementation and validation status

Implementation PR: [#129](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/129), with an additional commit aligning directories and YAML layers to the agreed UT/ST/browser-E2E boundaries. The implementation branch is `refactor/configured-test-harness`, targeting `feat/jiuwenswarm`. It has been rebased onto target revision `9670568` and includes the latest three browser files and all 27 contract scenarios.

- Configuration inventory: 92 execution entries and 48 suites; static inventory currently contains 437 assets.
- PR policy: 7 required execution entries. Daily policy: 82 required entries and 54 observational contract entries (27 × two executor labels).
- Browser collection compared against the latest target: 90 upstream framework-expanded tests versus 88 retained tests in 47 files. The only removals are the two explicitly approved obsolete declarations. Both the original snapshot and upstream integration are recorded in `test/support/migration.json`.
- Validation before PR submission: 65 harness/contract-tooling tests, 53 CI self-tests and 19 architecture tests passed; architecture boundaries and documentation lint/link checks also passed. These checks and framework collection are not a full product E2E run. Remote workflow execution must be assessed separately; existing product failures are not waived by this refactor.
- New configuration, scheduling and usage documentation is in `test/README.md` in the implementation branch.

## Configured subject models and assertions

Every case now explicitly declares `assertions.mode`: `deterministic`, `llm`, or `hybrid`. Real subject models are configured independently from judge models:

```yaml
llm:
  mode: real
  model:
    protocol: chat-completions
    baseUrlEnv: E2E_LLM_BASE_URL
    modelEnv: E2E_LLM_MODEL
    apiKeyEnv: E2E_LLM_TOKEN
assertions:
  mode: hybrid
  judge:
    model:
      protocol: chat-completions
      baseUrlEnv: E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL
      modelEnv: E2E_JUDGE_MODEL
      apiKeyEnv: E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    maxTokens: 1200
    maxInputCharacters: 24000
    rubric:
      - id: task-completion
        description: The answer and supplied artifact meet the requested task.
        threshold: 0.8
```

A model profile accepts exactly one literal `model` or `modelEnv`; each case may bind different environment names. Credentials are never stored in YAML. The initial transport is OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions; scoring requires a model supporting its temperature/max-token parameters.

Browser cases use `assessment.check(name, callback)` for configurable programmatic assertions and `assessment.submit({task, answer, artifacts, context})` for actual bounded evidence. Deterministic mode runs checks without a judge call. LLM-only mode skips those optional assertion callbacks. Hybrid mode requires at least one successful named check and all judge thresholds to pass. Ordinary framework `expect` calls remain mandatory structural/workflow guards. Never put setup/actions inside the optional assertion callback.

Judging runs only after the test body passes. Missing evidence, missing model configuration, malformed/missing/duplicate scores, low scores, HTTP errors and timeouts cannot produce PASS. There is no automatic fallback or retry. Every criterion has an explicit threshold in [0,1]. The configured input limit rejects oversized evidence rather than silently truncating it. Reports include per-attempt assessment attachments, resolved subject/judge identities, sanitized evidence, rubric, scores, reasons, usage when supplied and latency. A framework pass without required scoring evidence is rejected by the harness. Qualitative scoring does not prove numerical correctness; keep objective calculations checked programmatically.

The initial production example is `e2e.browser.model-request`: real subject + hybrid completion/delivery checks and report-quality scoring. The other two existing real-browser files retain deterministic assertions. All non-browser runners currently support deterministic assertions; unsupported scoring/runner combinations fail configuration validation explicitly.

## Daily real-model execution and setup

`test-daily.yml` invokes independent `external:none` and `external:real` jobs through the same reusable workflow. The external tag is derived from **either** a real subject or a live judge, so stub-subject/live-judge cases cannot accidentally enter the deterministic job. PR remains deterministic and receives no model secrets.

All three real-browser files run daily on both native and JiuwenSwarm as required work: six added entries. Daily now expands to **136 entries: 82 required and 54 observational contracts**. PR remains seven required entries. The real job explicitly sets `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1`; missing credentials cause required work to fail with unmet prerequisites.

Configure these repository Actions secrets for the supplied profiles:

- `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN`.
- `E2E_JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `E2E_JUDGE_MODEL`, `E2E_JUDGE_TOKEN`.

Custom case-specific environment names must also be wired into the workflow. The implementation does not create secrets or choose a paid provider. Inspect with `pnpm test:list --profile daily --tag external:real --json`; with the six values exported and the isolated stack prerequisites ready, use `CI_ALLOW_REAL=1 pnpm test:daily --tag external:real`.

`literature-review` now registers/selects the configured model rather than hardcoded DeepSeek profiles; it still depends on its Skill/connector fixtures and PubMed availability. Those remaining requirements can block daily runs. Real-project Playwright traces are disabled because registration request bodies contain model keys; step screenshots and sanitized scoring evidence remain.

Local validation includes actual Playwright fixture execution against a local HTTP judge: three expected passes, three deliberate failures (native check, missing evidence, low score), three scoring requests and five assessment attachments. This verifies execution/reporting integration without calling an external model. No real-provider or complete product E2E pass is claimed: subject/judge variables were absent in the local environment during validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every maintained test asset maps to an execution entry point or an explicit, reviewable exclusion/gate.
- [ ] The Python adapter suite, all seven standalone API/Runner journeys, and all eleven existing contract scenarios are represented; their tooling self-tests are classified separately.
- [ ] A nested Web `.test.ts`/`.test.tsx` file and a deeper Node module test are discovered without editing package-specific glob depths.
- [ ] Browser discovery does not execute Node tooling tests or collect helpers as journeys.
- [ ] Local and CI commands resolve to the same selected test set for the same profile and capabilities.
- [ ] Unknown IDs, unintended zero-test selections, stale entries, and unsupported executor requests cannot produce a misleading green result.
- [ ] Missing credentials/hardware are reported explicitly; no live-model invocation is enabled implicitly by listing or selecting a full profile.
- [ ] Reports distinguish selected, executed, failed, blocked, skipped, and unexecuted cases and identify the actual executor.
- [ ] Before/after discovery mappings account for the existing browser cases, standalone journeys, and contract scenarios. Reclassification is recorded explicitly; tests are not lost to preserve a green count.
- [ ] Existing public commands have documented compatibility or migration behavior, with a single repository testing guide explaining where tests belong and how to run them.
- [ ] Focused regression checks cover discovery, selection, compatibility wrappers, empty/missing cases, and truthful failure propagation.

## Follow-up work

A complete service-lifecycle/isolation harness, product compatibility fixes, broad legacy remediation, new ST/E2E coverage, coverage-percentage thresholds, automated nightly failure triage should be handled separately; real-model judging is now included in the agreed implementation scope above. This issue establishes the shared entry points and discovery guarantees those improvements depend on.

items.body:
Importing a research evidence package restores the conversation and the evidence needed to inspect and continue the original work. The `.sdresearch` plugin exports and imports workspace file versions, artifacts and provenance, execution history, trajectory details, and the scientific memory graph.

## Behavior

- Imported sessions are read-only snapshots. **Create a new session to continue research** creates an independent, writable copy with the imported conversation and evidence. New research preserves the original snapshot. The compact continuation action appears beside the composer notice; the copy-origin notice disappears after 10 seconds.
- Workspace files open in a preview dialog. Text previews are limited to 256 KiB, supported images including PNG use the original bytes, and downloads preserve the original filename and complete contents.
- Trajectory export preserves model inputs, reasoning fragments, and tool-detail payloads. Import, restart, and continuation retain access to verified detail objects. Older packages cannot recover evidence they never contained.
- Necessary exports omit optional history and diagnostics while retaining required evidence dependencies; complete exports include broader history and trajectory details. File selections, export profiles, counts, and source limitations survive import and repeat export.
- User messages have a copy action; the existing assistant copy action is retained. Completed assistant replies offer **Branch to a new chat**, creating a writable conversation prefix through that reply. A persistent **Continue from chat** link returns to the immediate source reply, including after restart and for branches of branches.
- Branching preserves attributable historical evidence and discloses unavailable history; it never replaces a missing historical file with a later version. Busy sessions are rejected, request retries are idempotent, and imported snapshots remain protected.
- Importing a legacy package without scientific memory no longer fails snapshot capture solely because the local graph service is unavailable. Packages containing scientific memory still require successful graph restoration.

## Validation

Tested commit: `4e198ebe9ea9161d826827af816df59a09d02fb1`, based on official `main` at `9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`. Exactly one feature commit; author and committer are `zhaochen39 <zhaojichenjc@126.com>`.

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: 4 planned, 4 executed, 4 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Targeted feature regressions: 50 Node tests passed (21 package/API/import/branch cases and 29 UI-control/trajectory cases), plus 2 scientific-memory Python tests passed. These are targeted results, not a passing full UT layer.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: failed during Node collection with `NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED` after the collector's 120,000 ms timeout; no plan was produced and no tests executed. The same full-layer command on pristine official `main` failed at the same collection timeout.
- `pnpm ci:st`: 24 planned, 24 executed, 17 passed, 7 failed, 0 skipped. Pristine official `main` has the same counts and the same seven failed planned identities: five specialist-runtime/ACP cases, the Evolve Python-runtime download reaching the worker timeout, and the Swarm SDK contract command. Nested SDK results differ: the candidate reports 26 failed / 53 passed / 1 teardown error, while main reports 25 failed / 54 passed; both also report 20 passed subtests. The candidate has an additional timeout in `test_http_disconnect_propagates_cancellation_to_adapter`; this runtime validation difference remains unresolved. The SDK check completed normally before the local wait limit; it was not reported as a pass or skipped.
- No test assertions were weakened or cases skipped to obtain a passing result. Runtime failures and browser coverage gaps remain open; this PR stays Draft.

## E2E user journeys

**FAIL / incomplete coverage**, on the tested commit above, using the shipping JiuwenSwarm backend and local mocked models. `pnpm ci:e2e` reports 103 planned, 9 reported/executed, 7 passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped; 94 identities were not run. One of the two reported failures is an interrupted case, not a completed assertion failure.

Command: `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1 CI_RESULTS_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/results CI_RUNTIME_DIR=.tmp/publish-finalized/runtime pnpm ci:e2e`, after dependencies, full build, bubblewrap, and the pinned Chromium were prepared in an isolated detached worktree.

| Batch | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research, 20 planned | Healthy isolated stack, then research journeys | BLOCKED before browser execution: scientific memory did not become healthy within the startup script's 10-second wait. |
| Standard, 77 planned | Healthy gateway, valid serialized ordering, then UI journeys | Reporter raised `FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST`; the gateway also timed out during WebSocket opening handshake. Network guard passed, the first inline-card case failed, and the unhealthy run was manually interrupted: 1 passed / 1 failed / 1 interrupted / 74 not run. The tagged summary counts the interruption as FAIL. Supplemental Swarm `history` recorded FAIL; remaining supplemental checks were stopped. |
| Literature, 6 planned | Offline literature-source contracts complete through the local product stack | 6 executed, 6 passed. |

The changed user goals are importing and inspecting evidence, continuing a snapshot in a writable session, previewing/downloading workspace files, inspecting trajectory/export scopes, copying a user message, and branching from a reply with navigation back to its source. Expected outcomes are persistent inspectable evidence, original-name downloads, complete selected detail payloads, independent writable branches, and return to the source reply. These changed UI journeys remain **unverified by browser E2E** because of the blocked/interrupted batches. The targeted package/API tests are regression tests, not external-client API or local-stack journey certification; that additional journey coverage also remains open.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Validation
Focused checks on `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928`:
- `node --test .ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`: 24 passed, 0 failed. After the TAP summary the process aborted with status 134. That abort is a host behavior and not a failed assertion.
- Static collection of `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs` reported no dynamic registration.

Earlier local layers were run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`, before the exemption was narrowed. They were not rerun on `3bde9d39`. This follow-up does not change product code.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4453, executed 4453, passed 4452, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure is `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.test.ts` (the scratch directory was already 86 bytes, so the fitting socket path could not be constructed). That case passed when rerun with a shorter temporary directory. The CLA file in that run had 19 cases.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5, skipped 0. All five failures are in `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts`. That file matches baseline `7ee6c1d0`. Pre-existing host `PATH`.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked): planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure is `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. The spec matches baseline `7ee6c1d0`. Pre-existing.

A later local `pnpm ci:ut` was reported as planned/executed/passed 4456/4456/4456 after the three allowlist cases were added. This pull request does not attach that run's logs, so the reproduced check on the current head is the 24-case file above.

## E2E user journeys
FAIL for one pre-existing layout assertion on `92b8022`. The other mocked journeys in that run passed. The suite was not rerun on `3bde9d39`. This change does not alter product UI or product behavior. Real-model journeys were not run.

Tested SHA for that run: `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`. Browser journeys, mocked model, isolated local stack. Scenario: open the model registry in the empty state and use the connect control as the only create entry. Expected: that control is narrower than 580px. Actual: 601.23px. Counts: planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0.

## Release
Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. Only `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` can merge when `license/cla` is present and not success. Other bots and human authors stay blocked in that case. A CLA check that never appears does not block anyone.

Compatibility and migration: none. `license/cla` stays off the required status checks on purpose. This workflow change needs a human review; merge-when-ready is not enabled.

items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.
